articles.title: Golpes online fazem parte da vida de 45 milhões de brasileiros, mostra estudo • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Golpes online fazem parte da vida de 45 milhões de brasileiros, mostra estudo
Levantamento do Cetic.br revela que 32% dos usuários de internet no Brasil foram abordados por criminosos.
Golpes online já atingiram cerca de 45 milhões de brasileiros com 16 anos ou mais, o equivalente a 32% da população que acessa a internet no país. Os dados fazem parte da Pesquisa Privacidade e Proteção de Dados Pessoais, divulgada nesta segunda-feira (31/08) pelo Cetic.br, departamento do Núcleo de Informação e Coordenação do Ponto BR (NIC.br) que cuida de estatísticas e indicadores sobre o uso da internet no Brasil. O NIC.br também é a entidade responsável pela gestão dos domínios .br.
O Tecnoblog teve acesso ao estudo, que detalha os canais usados nessas abordagens. Os aplicativos de mensagem são o principal meio usado pelos criminosos e aparecem em 84% dos casos, mas as ligações telefônicas e o SMS, métodos mais tradicionais, surgem logo depois, com 79% e 71%, respectivamente. Ou seja, mesmo quem navega pouco pela internet está sujeito a golpes que envolvem dados pessoais.
Os criminosos não dependem de um único meio para abordar as vítimas. Aplicativos de mensagem são o canal mais citado, presentes em 84% dos relatos, seguidos por ligações telefônicas (79%). Sites e aplicativos falsos aparecem em 71% dos casos, mesma proporção registrada para mensagens SMS. E-mails e redes sociais foram mencionados por 69% e 67% dos entrevistados, respectivamente.
O dispositivo usado para acessar a internet também parece influenciar o tipo de exposição. Entre quem acessa a rede pelo celular, foram mais frequentes os relatos envolvendo sites e aplicativos falsos. Já um acesso mais limitado à internet pode dificultar a adoção de ferramentas e práticas de segurança, ampliando a vulnerabilidade diante dessas abordagens.
Os golpes que usam dados pessoais já fazem parte da experiência de uma parcela significativa dos entrevistados. Segundo a pesquisa, 32% afirmam ter sido abordados por cibercriminosos, enquanto 20% dizem ter sido efetivamente enganados. Os resultados indicam que a exposição não está restrita a quem faz uso intenso da internet: os criminosos também recorrem a canais tradicionais para alcançar as vítimas.
O fator emocional aparece como uma das principais brechas exploradas pelos golpistas. Segundo o estudo, 58% dos entrevistados se consideram mais vulneráveis a esse tipo de abordagem quando estão passando por situações de mal-estar ou estresse emocional. O impacto dos golpes também é diverso: 48% relatam roubo de dinheiro, 43% perda de acesso às próprias contas, 42% dívidas contraídas em seu nome e outros 42% roubo de dados sensíveis.
A escolaridade também aparece associada à exposição. Pessoas que cursaram até o Ensino Fundamental se mostraram mais suscetíveis aos golpes, segundo o levantamento.
A pesquisa ainda revela que a preocupação dos brasileiros aumenta quando há risco direto de perda financeira, enquanto atividades cotidianas de comunicação e armazenamento parecem gerar uma sensação maior de segurança.
No entanto, 66% dos entrevistados afirmaram se preocupar com o uso de seus dados pessoais por ferramentas de inteligência artificial. O nível de escolaridade também influencia esse resultado: a preocupação chega a 72% entre pessoas com ensino superior, mas cai para 54% entre aquelas que estudaram até o Ensino Fundamental.
Também foram avaliados os hábitos de proteção de dados. Há uma queda em quase todas as práticas em relação a 2021. A exceção foi a configuração de cookies, que ganhou espaço no período. A parcela de pessoas que diz ler políticas de privacidade caiu de 68% para 65%; a que verifica a segurança de páginas, de 70% para 63%; e a que restringe o acesso à localização, de 62% para 57%.
A sensação de segurança varia conforme a atividade. Compras online e acesso a contas bancárias são as situações que mais despertam preocupação: 35% e 32% dos entrevistados, respectivamente, se dizem muito preocupados. Já atividades como usar aplicativos de mensagens e armazenar arquivos na nuvem provocam menos receio: 49% e 43%, respectivamente, afirmam estar pouco ou nada preocupados.
O levantamento foi feito em dezembro de 2025 com 2,5 mil indivíduos espalhados pelo país, em entrevistas online.

articles.title: E-Mail-Chaos bei Microsoft: Systeme erholen sich – doch nicht alle sind wieder online
articles.text:
Outlook: Microsoft-Nutzer konnten stundenlang keine Mails senden – das war der Grund
Nach einem stundenlangen, großflächigen Ausfall entspannt sich die Lage bei den E-Mail-Diensten von Microsoft wieder. Die betroffenen Systeme laufen nach Angaben des US-Konzerns schrittweise an und stehen weiten Teilen der Nutzer wieder zur Verfügung.
Am Montagabend hatte eine massive Störung den Mailverkehr von Millionen Nutzern weltweit lahmgelegt. Sowohl Unternehmenskunden der Cloud-Suite Microsoft 365 als auch Privatnutzer des E-Mail-Dienstes Outlook konnten sich über Stunden hinweg nicht einloggen oder Nachrichten senden und empfangen. Auf Plattformen wie Downdetector waren die Fehlermeldungen zeitweise auf Zehntausende emporgeschnellt.
Microsoft: Problem in der Cloud-Infrastruktur von Exchange Online
Als Ursache für den Ausfall nannte Microsoft ein Problem in der Cloud-Infrastruktur von Exchange Online. Ein Fehler in einer zentralen Authentifizierungs- und Verbindungskomponente habe den Zugriff auf die Server blockiert.
Techniker des Konzerns leiteten Gegenmaßnahmen ein und spielten in der Nacht gezielte Korrekturen auf den betroffenen Servern ein. Microsoft teilte mit, dass die Telemetriedaten eine deutliche Erholung zeigen und der Datenverkehr schrittweise wieder über die regulären Systeme abgewickelt wird. Einige Nutzer müssen sich nach Konzernangaben jedoch noch gedulden, bis alle Rückstaus im E-Mail-Versand vollständig abgearbeitet sind und die Synchronisation weltweit wieder stabil läuft.

articles.title: Lachy Groom backs Indian startup aiming to keep aircraft aloft for a year | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Prominent solo investor Lachy Groom has backed a Bengaluru startup attempting an ambitious feat: keeping an aircraft in the sky for more than a year by harvesting energy from ocean winds.
Alteon, founded by 20-year-old Samay Sanghvi, announced Tuesday that it raised $2.5 million in a pre-seed round led by Groom, with participation from Together Fund, to develop autonomous aircraft inspired by dynamic soaring, a technique albatrosses use to extract energy from the wind. Groom decided he wanted to invest within the first 30 minutes of their first meeting, Sanghvi told TechCrunch.
Conventional aircraft need to carry the fuel or battery power required for a flight. Alteon is trying to break that limitation by designing its small, fixed-wing autonomous aircraft that can extract energy from wind shear above the ocean through dynamic soaring — a maneuver in which an aircraft repeatedly moves between layers of air traveling at different speeds.
“Once you build airplanes that can stay in the air for more than a year, there are millions of things you can do with them,” Sanghvi told TechCrunch. Alteon plans to initially use the aircraft for maritime surveillance, giving governments real-time visibility into activity in their waters.
The initial plan is to build an aircraft with around a three-meter-wingspan that will fly close to the ocean’s surface, climb, and turn through faster-moving air, and repeat the cycle to gain energy from the wind. Eventually, Alteon plans to use its propellers as turbines to convert some of that energy into electricity and recharge its onboard batteries, Sanghvi said.
However, the startup has not yet demonstrated that its aircraft can actually sustain flight using energy harvested through dynamic soaring. It did complete a recent of its test of its autonomous flight system over the Bay of Bengal in which the aircraft autonomously completed seven O-shaped cycles at more than 62 miles per hour, flying within one meter of the water’s surface.
Alteon’s next major milestone will be what Sanghvi calls “energy-neutral dynamic soaring.” This would allow the aircraft to fly continuously with its propulsion switched off, extracting enough energy from the wind to remain aloft.
Dr. Gabriel Bousquet, a Silicon Valley-based aerospace and robotics engineer who researched dynamic soaring during his PhD at MIT, called Alteon’s low-altitude flight over water a “promising first result.” But he noted that the harder challenge will be proving that the aircraft can reliably extract enough energy from real-world winds to sustain flight for extended periods.
Flying low enough to harvest that energy safely is particularly difficult, Bousquet told TechCrunch, as the aircraft would have to contend with turbulence, waves, spray, rain, and changing light conditions while continuously sensing and reacting to a moving ocean surface.
Dr. Bharath Swaminathan, who earned his PhD from IIT Madras studying the stability of dynamic soaring, said the underlying physics is well established and called Alteon’s effort commendable. Keeping an aircraft airborne for several days using dynamic soaring would itself be “a very big step, and a big achievement,” he told TechCrunch.
Swaminathan, however, added that while large-scale wind conditions may be predictable, local wind shear and turbulence can vary substantially, complicating an aircraft’s ability to continuously extract energy from the wind. Some of those challenges, he suggested, may only emerge through real-world flight testing.
Groom acknowledged the technical risk behind the bet. “Ambitious problems are always going to come with risks,” he told TechCrunch. “For me, it came down to believing Samay and the Alteon team are the ones to figure them out.”
Sanghvi began working on what would become Alteon straight out of high school in 2023, learning to build aircraft by making — and crashing — radio-controlled models before developing early prototypes. He formally founded Alteon in 2025 and received early backing from Emergent Ventures and 1517.
Alteon now has a team of 20 in Bengaluru and operates from a 10,000-square-foot facility. The startup is building four to five aircraft a week for testing and has conducted more than 200 test flights in the past 30 days, Sanghvi said.

articles.title: Google enforcing new Android app memory limits in February
articles.text:
Google is now enforcing new memory limits and has set a date for when they come into effect.
Starting in February 2027, any Android app that exceeds the new limit may be slowed down or shut down. The Google Play Store can also bury the app if the requirements aren’t met.
Now, before we get any deeper, this isn’t exactly new information. A few weeks back, Google announced it was cracking down on apps that use a lot of memory and shared resources for devs to prepare for upcoming broader memory limits.
This time around, the thresholds have actually been set, and we now know the limits:
- 4GB: 2GB while running in the foreground, 1GB for user-perceived services, 1GB while running in the background.
- 6GB: 2.25GB while running in the foreground, 1.25GB for user-perceived services, 1.25GB while running in the background.
- 8GB: 2.25GB while running in the foreground, 1.5GB for user-perceived services, 1.5GB while running in the background.
- 12GB: 3.25GB while running in the foreground, 1.75GB for user-perceived services, 1.75GB while running in the background.
- 16GB: 4.25GB while running in the foreground, 2GB for user-perceived services, 2GB while running in the background.
It should be noted that if your device has more than 16GB of RAM, it is largely exempt from these limitations.
In terms of why these limitations are coming into place, all of the signs are pointing towards the RAM shortage caused by the AI boom.
“The mobile industry is navigating significant hardware supply constraints that are altering device memory availability that over time can negatively impact the user experience,” Google said in a post on the Android Developers Blog. “Android is addressing this challenge head-on with broader memory limits that aim to protect the overall user experience from apps using excess memory and causing system-wide slowdowns.”
Source: Google via The Next Web

articles.title: CD Projekt Red confirme que The Witcher 4 est déjà jouable sur PC, PS5 et Xbox
articles.text:
« Vous venez au studio, vous pouvez lancer The Witcher 4 aujourd’hui. Vous pouvez le lancer sur PC. Vous pouvez le lancer sur PS5. Vous pouvez le lancer sur Xbox Series X, et il tournera » : cette déclaration, signée Michal Nowakowski, co-CEO de CD Projekt Red, dans les colonnes de Game Developer le 27 août 2026, peut paraître anodine. Elle témoigne en réalité d’un changement d’approche dans le développement pour le studio polonais.
En effet, CD Projekt Red n’a pas envie de revivre un fiasco comparable au lancement de Cyberpunk 2077 — qui offrait des performances tellement désastreuses sur certaines plateformes qu’il a été temporairement retiré de la vente sur le PlayStation Store. La firme a donc changé son fusil d’épaule pour The Witcher 4, qui est déjà jouable sur un maximum d’appareils. Une approche totalement nouvelle pour CD Projekt Red.
CD Projekt Red a changé pour The Witcher 4
Auparavant, CD Projekt Red développait pour la version PC en priorité, puis s’arrangeait pour faire rentrer le jeu ailleurs, ensuite. Cela a fonctionné pour The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, avec un peu de chance, dixit Michal Nowakowski. Mais pour Cyberpunk 2077, ce fut une autre paire de manches.
Il raconte cette erreur : « Le studio se disait que nous cherchions à obtenir le meilleur rendu visuel possible. Nous voulions repousser les limites de ce qu’il est possible de faire en matière de rendu cinématique et tout ce qui s’ensuit, et le PC était tout simplement la machine la plus adaptée pour cela. Il y avait cette fausse croyance, comme nous l’avons constaté par la suite, qu’adapter le jeu à la baisse pour la génération de consoles de l’époque ne représenterait pas un si grand défi. »
Désormais, les développeurs ne mettent plus un problème de côté dès qu’il se présente. Admettons que The Witcher 4 rencontre un bug majeur sur Xbox Series X, alors il deviendra une priorité à corriger avant que les chantiers normaux ne reprennent. En toute transparence, Michal Nowakowski explique : « Par exemple, sur le plan technique, nous devions cocher, admettons, 10 cases. Par le passé, si on en ratait une ou deux, on se disait : « on rattrapera ça plus tard ». Parfois c’était le cas, parfois non, et puis deux ou trois étapes plus tard, vous vous retrouvez avec quatre ou cinq cases manquantes, et là, ce n’est plus aussi simple. » Cette mauvaise habitude a laissé des traces.
On rappelle que CD Projekt Red a choisi la PlayStation 5 pour la toute première démo technique de The Witcher 4 — qui tourne avec le moteur graphique Unreal Engine 5. Ce choix représente déjà un changement de paradigme, puisque les versions console de Cyberpunk 2077 avaient longtemps été cachées. En espérant que ce n’est pas trop beau pour être vrai.

articles.title: Cómo ‘apagar’ WhatsApp y seguir usando internet en el celular para ver series o jugar
articles.text:
Cuando surge la necesidad de evitar interrupciones en el teléfono móvil, como durante una partida en línea, una maratón de series o una sesión de trabajo, muchos usuarios se preguntan cómo es posible desconectar WhatsApp sin perder la conexión a internet.
La solución consiste en impedir que la aplicación reciba mensajes o notificaciones, mientras que el resto de las funciones del teléfono, tanto en Wi-Fi como con datos móviles, continúan operando con total normalidad.
PUBLICIDAD
El resultado es que WhatsApp queda inactivo y quien intente escribir verá la señal de mensaje no entregado, sin afectar la navegación ni las demás aplicaciones.
Cómo deshabilitar WhatsApp en Android sin perder conexión a internet
En dispositivos Android existe un método para lograr que WhatsApp deje de funcionar temporalmente sin tener que desconectar el teléfono de la red. El proceso es sencillo y no requiere instalar aplicaciones adicionales. Todo se basa en la gestión del sistema operativo, que permite forzar el cierre de cualquier aplicación.
PUBLICIDAD
Para quienes utilizan Android, el primer paso es ingresar a la configuración general del dispositivo. Dentro del menú de aplicaciones, se debe localizar WhatsApp y seleccionar la opción para detener su funcionamiento. La función suele denominarse “Forzar detención” o simplemente “Detener”, y se encuentra visible al abrir la información de la aplicación. Al confirmar esta acción, todos los procesos relacionados con WhatsApp se interrumpen por completo.
Mientras no se vuelva a abrir la aplicación, WhatsApp permanece sin conexión. Los mensajes que otras personas intenten enviar llegarán únicamente como enviados, pero no entregados.
PUBLICIDAD
Esto se traduce en que el remitente visualizará solo un “check” gris, el mismo símbolo que aparece cuando el destinatario no tiene acceso a internet o el teléfono está apagado. Las llamadas, tanto de voz como de video, tampoco llegan ni generan ningún tipo de notificación.
El resto del teléfono mantiene su funcionamiento habitual. Plataformas de videos, navegadores, redes sociales y cualquier otro servicio que utilice internet siguen activos. De esta forma, es posible disfrutar de juegos en línea o ver series sin interrupciones, con la tranquilidad de que no aparecerán mensajes ni alertas indeseadas de WhatsApp.
PUBLICIDAD
Pasos para bloquear WhatsApp en iPhone y seguir conectado a internet
Los usuarios de iPhone también cuentan con alternativas para silenciar WhatsApp de manera temporal, sin desconectarse de internet. A diferencia de Android, donde se detiene la aplicación por completo, en iOS se gestiona el acceso de WhatsApp a la red y a las notificaciones.
Una de las opciones disponibles es desactivar la actualización en segundo plano para WhatsApp. Esto se realiza desde la aplicación de ajustes del iPhone, donde se debe buscar la sección correspondiente a WhatsApp y desmarcar la función de actualización en segundo plano. Así se impide que la aplicación reciba información o mensajes cuando no está activa.
PUBLICIDAD
Adicionalmente, es posible anular el permiso de notificaciones, accediendo al menú de notificaciones y desactivando la opción para WhatsApp. De este modo, aunque la aplicación reciba mensajes, no mostrará ningún aviso en la pantalla ni interrumpirá otras actividades.
Si el usuario solo utiliza datos móviles y no Wi-Fi, existe la posibilidad de deshabilitar exclusivamente el uso de datos móviles para WhatsApp. Esto se consigue en el mismo menú de ajustes, desactivando el interruptor correspondiente. De esa manera, la aplicación queda sin acceso a la red móvil, pero el resto de las aplicaciones siguen navegando normalmente.
PUBLICIDAD
Qué sucede cuando WhatsApp queda inactivo en el teléfono
La principal consecuencia de dejar WhatsApp sin conexión temporal es que los contactos que intenten comunicarse no recibirán respuesta. Los mensajes enviados quedarán en estado de “enviados”, sin avanzar a “entregados”, replicando la sensación de que el dispositivo está fuera de cobertura o apagado. Para quien llama, ya sea por voz o video, la llamada no suena y no genera interrupciones en la pantalla.
Mientras tanto, el resto de las aplicaciones y servicios del teléfono continúan funcionando con normalidad. Se puede navegar, mirar videos en streaming, utilizar redes sociales o jugar en línea, sin que las notificaciones de WhatsApp interfieran en la experiencia. Cuando se decida volver a utilizar WhatsApp, solo hay que abrir la aplicación para restaurar su funcionamiento y recibir todos los mensajes pendientes.
PUBLICIDAD
Este método es útil para quienes buscan periodos de concentración, entretenimiento o descanso, sin desconectarse completamente del entorno digital.

articles.title: GTA 6 fait exploser la demande de PS5 Pro malgré les hausses de prix
articles.text:
Les dates de sortie de GTA 6, vous avez arrêté de les compter ? Rockstar en est à la troisième (l’automne 2025, puis le 26 mai 2026, et désormais le 19 novembre). Ce qui a changé le 27 août, c’est que Rockstar a enfin montré son jeu en long et en large sur Netflix. Près de 27 minutes de jeu, capturées sur une PS5 tout ce qu’il y a de plus standard. Vingt-quatre heures plus tard, la PS5 Pro avait disparu des rayons américains.
Sony a préparé le terrain, les revendeurs encaissent
Le décor était planté depuis des mois, puisque Sony et Rockstar mènent une campagne commune autour du jeu, avec un slogan qui promet que GTA 6 « se joue dans les meilleures conditions sur PS5 ». Dans les heures qui ont suivi la présentation du 27 août, Best Buy et Target n’avaient plus une seule PS5 Pro en stock. Amazon et Walmart n’affichaient plus que des vendeurs tiers autour de 1 299 dollars, soit 400 dollars de plus que le tarif officiel de 899 dollars. Seule la boutique PlayStation Direct tenait encore le prix catalogue, avec un stock qui fondait à vue d’œil.
L’Europe suit le mouvement avec un temps de retard et des euros à la place des dollars. En Allemagne, la console coûte officiellement 899,99 euros, mais les comparateurs démarrent autour de 999 euros et Amazon annonce jusqu’à sept mois de délai. En France, la Pro s’affichait encore à 899 euros sur les comparateurs à l’heure d’écrire ces lignes, et il serait imprudent d’annoncer une pénurie nationale sur la foi de quelques rayons vides. Aucun chiffre de vente ne dit ce que la démo a réellement déclenché, ce qui n’a pas empêché les spéculateurs de ressortir leurs robots d’achat.
Pour Sony, cette ruée tombe après une série de hausses qui aurait fait rougir n’importe quel autre constructeur. La PS5 standard, lancée à 499,99 euros en 2020, a pris 50 euros en 2022 puis 100 de plus au 2 avril dernier, pour atteindre 649,99 euros. La Pro a suivi le même chemin, de 799,99 euros à 899,99 euros, officiellement en raison des « pressions continues dans le paysage économique global ». Une console plus chère qu’à sa sortie, un jeu qui la rend introuvable et des revendeurs qui ajoutent 400 dollars par-dessus : le joueur paie trois fois, et Sony n’a rien eu à faire.
Faut-il vraiment une PS5 Pro pour jouer à GTA 6 ?
La réponse courte tient dans la présentation elle-même : tout ce que Rockstar a montré le 27 août tournait sur une PS5 de base, à 30 images par seconde. Rockstar promet des améliorations spécifiques à la Pro sans en avoir détaillé une seule, et le studio a confirmé un plafond de 30 images par seconde au lancement, PS5 Pro comprise. Acheter une Pro aujourd’hui pour GTA 6, c’est réserver une place en première classe sans savoir si le train en aura une. La Pro devrait apporter un rendu plus fin grâce à sa puce graphique plus musclée et à son suréchantillonnage maison (le PSSR). La version standard reste toutefois la seule sur laquelle on a vu le jeu tourner.
Reste la question des stocks d’ici le 19 novembre, et là, deux discours s’opposent. Sony affirme avoir sécurisé la mémoire nécessaire pour produire assez de consoles jusqu’en mars 2027, fin de son exercice, et n’anticipe aucune pénurie pendant les fêtes, au moment même où le jeu sortira. Un important distributeur européen tient un discours nettement plus sombre et estime que les volumes livrés d’ici novembre seront insuffisants si la demande atteint le niveau attendu. Entre les deux, votre décision relève de la patience. Sony dispose d’onze semaines pour réapprovisionner les Pro si elles venaient à manquer dans l’Hexagone, sans qu’aucun calendrier ait été communiqué, et la PS5 standard à 649,99 euros fait déjà tourner le jeu que tout le monde attend.

articles.title: Llevamos años programando nuestras casas inteligentes. LG tiene otra idea: contarles lo que queremos y que ellas se apañen
articles.text:
Hay una contradicción con esa idea del hogar inteligente que desde hace años nos venden las empresas de electrónica de consumo: aunque la tecnología está ahí para ahorrarnos trabajo, conseguir que todo funcione cuesta. Hay que crear "escenas", establecer horarios o encadenar acciones y condiciones (si ocurre esto, haz aquello). LG cree que la IA generativa permite salvar ese obstáculo con una idea aparentemente sencilla y muy potente: decirle a nuestra casa qué queremos conseguir y dejar que sea ella quien averigüe cómo hacerlo.
Hola, ThinQ Claw. LG presentará estos días en IFA 2026 un agente de IA que han creado a partir de OpenClaw y que se puede usar como una herramienta de chat en su plataforma AI Home. Se llama ThinQ Claw, y la compañía asegura que no interpreta cada mensaje por separado, sino que va usando información sobre horarios, rutinas, preferencias y dispositivos que tenemos en casa para entender el contexto y actuar en consecuencia. Así, en luagar de recibir un compando dirigido a un aparato específico, ThinQ Claw recibe una petición y determina qué servicios y dispositivos necesita coordinar (y cómo hacerlo) para cumplirla.
"Esta tarde vienen unos amigos". Este tipo de información es la que LG quiere convertir en una interfaz para nuestro hogar. ThinQ Claw podría usarla para ir preparando los electrodomésticos que usaremos para cocinar, y saber cuándo vamos a regresar a casa permite comprobar la calidad del aire o ajustar previamente la climatización. También puede obtener información sobre nuestras últimas compras para saber qué ingredientes tenemos , sugerir un plato con ellos y proporcionarnos la receta. En LG explican que el agente se puede conectar a nuestro calendario y recordar nuestros gustos para personalizar futuras decisiones. Por ahora son demos, eso sí, no algo que hayamos podido probar, así que queda por ver cómo se comporta el sistema en la práctica.
No programes, simplemente pide. La verdadera novedad del sistema consiste realmente en ese soporte del lenguaje natural a través del chat. La domótica tradicional funciona fundamentalmente mediante reglas: un sensor, un horario o una acción provoca otra que alguien ha configurado previamente. ThinQ Claw introduce esa forma de trabajar que ya conocemos de otros agentes de IA: el usuario expresa un objetivo con un mensaje (un prompt) y es el agente el que interpreta qué significa la petición y qué pasos y herramientas tiene que usar para lograr cumplir con el objetivo que se ha pedido.
LG tiene las herramientas. LG fabrica televisores, frigoríficos, lavadoras, hornos, climatizadores y aspiradores, pero además compró Athom en 2024 y con ella consiguió Homey, una plataforma diseñada precisamente para conectar dispositivos de distintos fabricantes. En IFA mostrará como Homey puede coordinar electrodomésticos con contadores inteligentes, placas solares, baterías domésticas y cargadores de coches eléctricos para decidir cuándo generar, almacenar o consumir energía. Una agente de IA que gestione toda esta infraestructura de dispositivos distintos es mucho más versátil que uno que tiene que actuar restringido al ecosistema de una sola marca.
La casa que se programa sola. Hasta ahora hemos intentado resolver esa coordinación entre dispositivos con todo tipo de estándares e interfaces. Primero fueron aplicaciones para cada aparato, luego plataformas como Alexa o Google Assistant para controlarlos con la voz, y luego llegaron las plataformas domóticas con rutinas para automatizarlos a todos. Agentes de IA como ThinQ Claw prometen eliminar complejidad a esa configuración: ya no tenemos que saber que existen ciertas automatizaciones para poder usarlas: simplemente le decimos al asistente de chat lo que queremos y le dejamos trabajar.
Problema: privacidad. Hay una cara incómoda de ese futuro tan estupendo. Para que el agente pueda decidir que va a poner un poco el aire acondicionado para refrescar la casa antes de que lleguemos, debe saber cuándo llegamos. Para preparar todo para la cena necesita conocer nuestro calendario, preferencias e incluso compras. Todos esos datos que ayudan a este sistema a hacernos la vida más cómoda también son datos que acaban planteando una nueva amenaza a la privacidad. La compañía asegura que su arquitectura LG Shield protege tanto dispositivos como servicios y datos, pero en el anuncio no se especifica qué información se procesa localmente, cuál llega a la nube, durante cuánto tiempo se conserva allí y si se utiliza para entrenar quizás modelos de IA o para terceras partes de cara a fines publicitarios.
¿Quién tiene la última palabra? Hay que dejar claro que una cosa es que una IA nos recomiende bajar la temperatura y otra que pueda bajarla realmente. En LG utilizan cuidadosamente ambas posibilidades: según ellos, ThinQ Claw puede recomendar acciones y también "ayudar a iniciarlas". mientras que en algunas demos parece sugerirse que recomienda y ejecuta sin problemas. Queda por tanto por ver a qué tipo de limitaciones nos enfrentamos con un sistema de este tipo, porque paradójicamente, cuanto más útil es un agente de IA que controla nuestros dispositivos, más importantes son esos límites.
LG lleva tiempo apuntando a ese futuro. Hace ya más de un año que LG integró en sus televisores con webOS 25 y superior un nuevo sistema de inteligencia artificial con esa misma idea. Es decir, convertir "deseos" en acciones, y poderle decir a través del mando que "la pantalla se ve oscura" para que automáticamente el sistema operativo ajuste sus opciones y podamos ver mejor la imagen. Basta de trastear con el menú de configuración: tú le dices a la tele lo que quieres, y ella lo hace (o lo intenta, al menos).
A por los robots con brazos. La estrategia de LG va más allá, porque por ejemplo en el CES 2026 presentaron su CLOiD, su robot doméstico con ruedas, brazos y manos con las que era capaz de manipular objetos y utilizar electrodomésticos. La compañía lo mostró sacando leche del frigorífico, metiendo un croissant en el horno o encargándose de la colada, y en LG lo integran dentro de su ambicioso concepto (nombre ambicioso incluido) Zero Labor Home. LG hace los electrodomésticos, crea un agente que pueda coordinarlos, y añade finalmente una máquina capaz de intervenir físicamente allí donde aún necesitamos nuestras manos. La idea: que el usuario no tenga que hacer nada más que disfrutar.

articles.title: Private AI cloud shift pulls AI workloads back on-premises - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Enterprises pull AI workloads back on-premises as costs and threats mount
Enterprise infrastructure strategy is being rewritten around the private AI cloud, as security exposure, spiking hardware prices and rising token costs push artificial intelligence workloads back inside the data center. What started as a virtualization refresh has become the main event for on-premises computing.
That shift has put platform consolidation at the center of enterprise buying decisions, a theme running through this year’s VMware Explore. Broadcom Inc. has spent three years folding VMware’s accumulated products into a single stack, and customers ranging from small businesses to United Airlines, Audi and the London Stock Exchange are now running on it, according to Krish Prasad (pictured), senior vice president and general manager of the VMware Cloud Foundation Division at Broadcom.
“We have taken the goodness that people see in the public cloud, which is the developer experience, the agility, and we have combined that with the things people like in the private infrastructure, which is security, which is cost controls, the resiliency,” Prasad told theCUBE. “The combination is what VCF is all about, and that’s why customers are very interested in deploying it.”
Prasad spoke with theCUBE’s John Furrier at VMware Explore 2026, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed platform consolidation, memory economics, sovereignty and the security demands of frontier models. (* Disclosure below.)
Security and cost pressures redefine the private AI cloud
Three forces are converging on enterprise infrastructure teams at once. Frontier models have raised the stakes on hardening, server prices driven by dynamic random-access memory are climbing, and companies want to keep intellectual property away from external models, Prasad said.
“Customers are concerned about the token cost in the cloud. They are also concerned about IP protection, going to these external models and exposing their IP and data,” he said. “So they are bringing the AI workloads back on-prem where they can keep it closer to their data and protect their IP.”
Security is the first line of defense in that move, and Broadcom has been updating VMware’s platform for AI-era threats. The company had early access to frontier models through the Project Glasswing and turned that head start inward, Prasad noted.
“We really have built Mythos-like frontier models into our software development lifecycle, so our infrastructure is pretty hardened by the time customers get it,” he said. “We have done some innovations in our core platform, things like live patching … where customers can patch their environment while the workload is running without disrupting the workload.”
Cost is the second lever. Memory tiering, shipped a year before the DRAM squeeze, cuts application memory requirements by about half by tiering to NVMe storage, while VCF 9.1 extends the AI stack across more than 150 models, AMD and Nvidia Corp. accelerators and any original equipment manufacturer server. For Prasad, that convergence defines the company’s next private AI cloud bet.
“The whole focus now is around making VCF the best place for running the workloads. That’s where our customers are focused,” he said. “Everything that goes around AI, the security, the runtime, the models, and all of that. So that’s the big bet we are making, and we are doubling down on it.”

articles.title: Google remplace les limites quotidiennes de Gemini Notebook par une nouvelle restriction bien plus complexe
articles.text:
Les plafonds journaliers sur Gemini Notebook, c’est terminé : à partir du 2 septembre, Google revoit entièrement vos limites d’usage.
L’heure est au changement pour Gemini Notebook, l’assistant de recherche IA anciennement connu sous le nom de NotebookLM : Google, a, en avril dernier, fusionné les espaces de travail de ce service et de son intelligence artificielle via la fonction « Notebooks » avant de lancer en juin une mise à jour très ambitieuse. Le géant de la Tech s’attaque désormais aux limites d’utilisation de cet outil. On vous explique.
Des limites d’utilisation entièrement remaniées
Auparavant, sur Gemini Notebook, les choses étaient claires : avec un compte gratuit, par exemple, on ne pouvait obtenir que 3 résumés audio et 10 quiz par jour. Les choses vont, toutefois, devenir un peu plus complexes.
Google a, en effet, expliqué dans l’une de ses pages de support qu'« à compter du 2 septembre 2026, Gemini Notebook appliquera des limites d’utilisation basées sur la puissance de calcul, déterminant ainsi votre niveau d’interaction avec les fonctionnalités. Ces limites prennent en compte la complexité de votre requête, les modèles et fonctionnalités utilisés, la durée de votre conversation et certaines fonctionnalités spécifiques. »
- Réponses liées aux sources
- Nombreux formats de fichiers
- Génération audio et visuelle
Cette nouvelle formule s’inspire du fonctionnement actuel de Gemini, dont la limite d’utilisation avait drastiquement chuté après l’I/O 2026 : elle était, en effet, passée de 24 à 5 heures, ce qui sera aussi le cas désormais pour Gemini Notebook.
Un argument pour faire payer les utilisateurs plus cher ?
Dans les faits, Google a fait le choix de se baser sur l’usage réel plutôt que d’imposer le même forfait à tous ses utilisateurs. Dans son annonce, la firme explique notamment vouloir leur offrir un « meilleur contrôle sur (leur) flux de travail ». Les utilisateurs bénéficieront de limites standards, tandis que les abonnés AI Plus, Pro et Ultra profiteront d’usages accrus : selon l’abonnement, ils auront des limites de 2 à 20 fois plus élevées. En agissant ainsi, Google essaye probablement de pousser gentiment les utilisateurs vers ses formules les plus généreuses.
À noter, le géant de la Tech a tout de même fait un petit geste sympathique : si vous dépassez votre quota et que vous ne souhaitez ni attendre 5 heures ni passer à un abonnement supérieur, Gemini Notebook vous « suggérera des alternatives si votre premier choix dépasse votre limite ». L’outil proposera également de mettre en attente les tâches un peu trop lourdes, comme la création de vidéos et de diaporamas, et de vous envoyer une notification quand celles-ci seront achevées.

articles.title: FTC-Klage: Hat Amazon Werbepreise manipuliert?
articles.text:
20 Milliarden Dollar abgezockt? FTC verklagt Amazon wegen Manipulation von Werbepreisen
Erst im Herbst 2025 hatte Amazon sich zur Zahlung von 2,5 Milliarden US-Dollar bereiterklärt, um eine Klage der FTC beizulegen. Darin hatte die US-Handelsbehörde dem E-Commerce-Konzern vorgeworfen, Kund:innen zur Anmeldung bei seinem Prime-Dienst verleitet zu haben. Auch die Abo-Kündigung soll Amazon erschwert haben.
Systematisch überhöhte Preise berechnet?
Jetzt sieht sich der Konzern mit einer weiteren FTC-Klage konfrontiert, der sich die Generalstaatsanwält:innen aus 22 US-Bundesstaaten angeschlossen haben. Wie die FTC mitteilt, soll Amazon Werbeauktionen manipuliert und Werbekund:innen über Jahre hinweg „heimlich und systematisch überhöhte Preise berechnet haben“. Dabei habe der Konzern rund 20 Milliarden Dollar zusätzlich eingenommen.
Konkret wirft die FTC Amazon vor, bei seinen Auktionen den Mindestpreis für die Schaltung von Produktwerbung angehoben zu haben, ohne dass die Werbetreibenden davpn gewusst hätten. 2019 habe der Konzern seine Auktionsstrategie entsprechend geändert und gibt seitdem ein eigenes Gebot ab, eine sogenannte „Soft Reserve“.
Werbepraxis auch intern verschwiegen
Dieses Gebot soll jeweils über dem Preis des zweithöchsten Bieters gelegen haben, wie Investing.com schreibt. Dadurch seien die Anzeigenpreise gestiegen. Amazon soll die konkurrierenden Gebote der Händler gekannt, aber seine Praxis nicht offengelegt haben.
Auch intern sollen die zuständigen Manager:innen versucht haben, das Wissen darum zu begrenzen. Um die hohen Preise erklären zu können, sei die Strategie zudem nur an umsatzstarken Einkaufstagen eingesetzt worden.
Anzeigenpreise um 50 Prozent erhöht
Insgesamt, so der Vorwurf der FTC, soll Amazon in bis zu 70 bis 80 Prozent der Fälle in Auktionen eingegriffen haben, um den Mindestpreis zu erhöhen. An wichtigen Einkaufstagen wie dem Black Friday seien auch dadurch die Kosten für Pay-per-Click-Anzeigen um 50 Prozent in die Höhe geschossen.
Der FTC zufolge sollen davon Millionen Kund:innen, darunter über 500.000 kleine und mittelständische Unternehmen, betroffen gewesen sein. Die höheren Kosten sollen dann zu einem großen Teil an US-Verbraucher:innen weitergegeben worden sein, so FTC-Chairman Andrew Ferguson laut CNBC.
Amazon weist FTC-Vorwürfe zurück
Amazon wies die Vorwürfe derweil per Blog-Post zurück. Das Unternehmen bezeichnete die Klage der FTC als „fehlgeleitet“. Dabei würde die Arbeitsweise von Werbetreibenden grundlegend verkannt.
Zudem gebe es für Preiserhöhungen für Verbraucher:innen keine Beweise. Und: Amazon habe Werbetreibenden durch seine Auktionssysteme zwischen 2021 und 2025 vielmehr Einsparungen in der Höhe von acht Milliarden Dollar ermöglicht.

articles.title: Close to half the merchants not willing to pay MDR on UPI: Survey
articles.text:
Close to half the merchants not willing to pay MDR on UPI: Survey
LocalCircles surveyed 32,796 people across districts for this study. MDR is a fee paid by businesses to payment processors for accepting digital payments.
Almost half of the merchants in the country refused to pay any charges (Minimum Discount Rate) on UPI transactions above Rs 2000, a survey reveals. According to a survey by LocalCircles, 41% of the total merchants surveyed said this. While 9% said they did not accept any UPI payments, 33 % said that they would pay .25% or less.
LocalCircles surveyed 32,796 people across districts for this study. MDR is a fee paid by businesses to payment processors for accepting digital payments. An MDR of up to 0.3% of the transaction value applied to UPI person-to-merchant transactions until December 2019. Zero MDR was introduced in January 2020.
“If you are a business that accepts UPI payments, what is the maximum MDR that you would be willing to bear on UPI payments above INR 2000?” was the question posed by Local Circles. “This question received 32,796 responses. In response, the largest group at 41% said they would not bear any MDR charges. 15% said 0.04%, 12% said 1%, 8% said 0.25%, 5% said 0.5%, 5% said 0.2%, 5% said 0.1% and 0% said 0.08%. A further 9% said they do not accept UPI payments,” said LocalCircles in a statement.
LocalCircles conducted another survey this month, which received over 45,000 responses from UPI users located across 322 districts of India. “The survey found that 53% of UPI users surveyed would move away from UPI for higher-value transactions if an MDR is levied and recovered from them — 27% said they would switch to credit cards, 14% to debit cards and 12% to cash or bank transfers. Only 12% said they would pay the fee and continue using UPI, while another 18% said they would continue only if the merchant absorbed the cost,” it says.

articles.title: Microsoft permet enfin de refuser OneDrive dans Windows 11
articles.text:
Vous pouvez désormais refuser la sauvegarde des données de votre PC sur OneDrive dès la première configuration de votre ordinateur. Microsoft vient en effet de mettre fin à une de ses pratiques particulièrement agaçantes qui vous poussait jusqu’alors à configurer OneDrive pour sauvegarder vos fichiers dans Windows 11.
Microsoft ajoute un bouton pour refuser OneDrive dans Windows 11
Jusqu’à maintenant, à la première configuration de Windows 11, Microsoft affichait dans son assistant de configuration une page incitant fortement à configurer votre compte Microsoft avec OneDrive pour pouvoir sauvegarder les données de votre PC.
Cette option était d’ailleurs difficilement contournable puisque la firme de Redmond n’affichait aucun bouton de refus. À la place, Microsoft proposait simplement de remettre la configuration de OneDrive à plus tard. L’entreprise ne proposait en effet que deux options, permettant soit de proposer de nouveau la sauvegarde après trois jours, soit de remettre celle-ci à plus tard, se laissant ainsi une nouvelle fenêtre de tir pour tenter de vous convaincre ultérieurement.
Une pratique aussi désagréable qu’agaçante, puisque le système d’exploitation de Microsoft n’hésitait pas à vous rappeler de configurer OneDrive à travers des pop-up non sollicités. Une pratique longtemps dénoncée par les utilisateurs, lassés par les vaines tentatives de Microsoft d’imposer certains de ses produits et services maison.
Cependant, Microsoft semble avoir mis fin à cette pratique très récemment. En effet, depuis le déploiement des dernières versions stables de Windows 11, un nouveau bouton de refus a fait son apparition sur la page de configuration dédiée à OneDrive que le système d’exploitation affiche lors du paramétrage après le premier boot du PC (OOBE).
Pendant longtemps, Microsoft nous a habitué à l’utilisation de différentes techniques pour tenter d’imposer l’utilisation de ses outils. Si la firme de Redmond est par exemple connue pour pousser les utilisateurs de Windows 11 à adopter Microsoft Edge comme navigateur Web par défaut, l’entreprise a également tenté à plusieurs reprises d’installer certains utilitaires maison sans demander le consentement de l’utilisateur.
L’exemple le plus récent remonte à quelques semaines, quand Microsoft a installé, par surprise, son application OneDrive Photos. La firme de Redmond avait ensuite plaidé l’erreur, indiquant avoir procédé à un déploiement plus large que prévu, avant d’annuler le déploiement de l’appli face aux commentaires négatives reçus de la part des utilisateurs de Windows 11.

articles.title: ChatGPT volta a funcionar após falha nesta segunda (31) • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
ChatGPT volta a funcionar após falha nesta segunda (31)
Problema técnico impedia assinantes de começarem ou continuarem tarefas no ChatGPT Work.
O ChatGPT enfrentou dificuldades técnicas na tarde desta segunda-feira (31/08). Segundo a página de status da OpenAI, usuários de diversos planos pagos enfrentaram problemas na hora de começar ou continuar tarefas no ChatGPT Work, versão corporativa da inteligência artificial. Outros serviços, como a ferramenta de programação Codex, a plataforma de anúncios e o chatbot pessoal, funcionavam normalmente.
Segundo a empresa, o problema foi corrigido por volta das 17h30 (horário de Brasília), cerca de meia hora após uma correção. Antes disso, a companhia disse ter identificado uma alta latência por volta do meio-dia.
O DownDetector, que monitora falhas na web, confirmou que as queixas sobre a instabilidade no ChatGPT começaram por volta do meio-dia. As reclamações começaram a cair pouco antes das 15 até voltar ao patamar de costume às 18h.

articles.title: Google Maps cambia el nombre del lago Ontario a ‘Lago América’ por orden de Donald Trump
articles.text:
La reciente actualización de la aplicación de mapas de Google ha provocado reacciones en ambos lados de la frontera entre Estados Unidos y Canadá. A partir de una orden del presidente Donald Trump, el lago Ontario ahora aparece como ‘Lago América’ para los usuarios estadounidenses, mientras que los usuarios canadienses mantienen el nombre original y quienes consultan desde otros países pueden ver ambas denominaciones.
Esta decisión tecnológica surge en un contexto de tensiones comerciales y políticas entre ambos países, generando respuestas oficiales y sociales tanto de gobiernos como de ciudadanos.
PUBLICIDAD
Google Maps modifica el nombre del lago Ontario en Estados Unidos
La multinacional tecnológica Google implementó un cambio relevante en su plataforma de mapas, ajustando la denominación del lago Ontario exclusivamente para quienes acceden a su servicio desde Estados Unidos. Desde este país, el cuerpo de agua fue renombrado como “Lago América”, reflejando una directiva presidencial emitida por Donald Trump días antes.
La actualización no afecta a los usuarios en Canadá, para quienes el lago mantiene su designación original, ni a quienes acceden desde otros territorios, quienes pueden visualizar ambas opciones.
PUBLICIDAD
Google explicó que esta modificación responde a su política de seguir las nomenclaturas oficiales proporcionadas por el Sistema de Información de Nombres Geográficos de Estados Unidos, conocido como GNIS.
La compañía detalló en un comunicado que la actualización comenzó a desplegarse y que su criterio en casos de nombres geográficos disputados es mostrar el nombre asignado por la autoridad competente de cada país. Este enfoque busca evitar conflictos cuando existen diferencias en la denominación de accidentes geográficos compartidos.
PUBLICIDAD
Según el comunicado de Google, quienes utilicen Google Maps en Estados Unidos encontrarán ‘Lago América’, mientras que en Canadá permanece lago Ontario. Para el resto del mundo, la plataforma mostrará ambos nombres, ilustrando la política de la empresa acerca del tratamiento de nombres variables en distintas jurisdicciones.
Contexto político y comercial detrás del cambio en Google Maps
El cambio de nombre promovido por Donald Trump se produjo en un contexto de incremento de las tensiones comerciales entre Estados Unidos y Canadá. Ambos países han impuesto aranceles a productos del otro por valores que ascienden a miles de millones de dólares, intensificando la denominada guerra comercial entre ambas naciones.
PUBLICIDAD
La orden presidencial de modificar el nombre del lago Ontario se enmarca en esta coyuntura, interpretándose como un gesto simbólico en medio de la escalada diplomática y económica.
No es la primera vez que una directiva presidencial de este tipo tiene repercusiones en los servicios digitales. En 2025, Trump ya había ordenado el cambio de nombre del Golfo de México a Golfo de América en las plataformas bajo jurisdicción estadounidense, una decisión que Google también adoptó siguiendo su política de reflejar las designaciones oficiales de cada país en sus mapas digitales.
PUBLICIDAD
Reacciones y respuestas institucionales al cambio de nombre del lago Ontario
El primer ministro de Ontario, Doug Ford, respondió al anuncio presidencial con una acción simbólica: colocó un cartel de gran tamaño en la orilla canadiense del lago con la frase “Lago Ontario. Ahora y para siempre”, reafirmando la denominación tradicional y rechazando la imposición estadounidense.
Por otro lado, ni la Casa Blanca, ni la oficina del primer ministro canadiense Mark Carney, ni la del propio Ford emitieron declaraciones oficiales el domingo ante la decisión adoptada por Google.
PUBLICIDAD
Detalles sobre Google y su política de nombres geográficos
Google, cuya sede se encuentra en Mountain View, California, gestiona una de las principales plataformas de búsqueda y una vasta red de publicidad digital a escala global. La empresa es subsidiaria de Alphabet Inc. y mantiene una política de larga data en la gestión de nombres geográficos, guiándose por las autoridades oficiales de cada país para evitar conflictos internacionales.
La compañía argumentó que la actualización de los nombres en Google Maps responde a la necesidad de adaptarse a las diferentes denominaciones que pueden recibir los cuerpos de agua y otros accidentes geográficos en distintas regiones.

articles.title: Eurovision applications now open to Canadians
articles.text:
Canada joins the Eurovision Song Contest, and you can join, too, if you have the skills.
Eurovision, which has hosted the contest since 1956, is a song competition organized by the European Broadcasting Union (EBU). Last year, CBC/Radio-Canada officially became a member of the EBU in June 2026, making Canada eligible to compete in Eurovision.
Applications are officially open for artists hoping to represent Canada. CBC says it’s “seeking a magnetic Canadian performer with an established career and a proven track record of captivating large live audiences, who is fully prepared to commit to this historic moment and the extraordinary adventure of the Eurovision Song Contest.”
Artist selection criteria and guidelines are available on the CBC Radio Canada website, with the registration period beginning on Wednesday, September 9.

articles.title: Trois EVA en trois semaines : Sophie Adenot dirige pour la première fois une sortie spatiale
articles.text:
Et une, et deux, et trois sorties extravéhiculaires pour Sophie Adenot. Après deux premières interventions les 18 et 25 août 2026, l’astronaute française va ressortir dans l’espace le 1er septembre. Cette nouvelle EVA sera placée sous le signe de la nouveauté, puisque le binôme change, tout comme le profil de la mission et les responsabilités.
Les points clés de la 3e EVA de l’astronaute française
- Quand ? Le mardi 1er septembre 2026. La NASA prendra l’antenne dès 13h (heure de Paris) pour montrer les derniers préparatifs. L’ouverture du sas et le début effectif de la sortie (EVA) sont prévus vers 14h30 (heure de Paris).
- Où ? Sur la chaîne YouTube officielle de l’ESA (le lecteur est intégré ci-dessous).
- L’enjeu ? Environ six heures et demie de travail pour remplacer un rétroréflecteur sur le module Harmony, qui sert à guider l’amarrage des vaisseaux sur l’ISS.
Suivez en direct la sortie de Sophie Adenot
L’Agence spatiale européenne met à disposition un flux vidéo en direct pour suivre toute la séquence, qui s’étalera sur plusieurs heures.
Le programme de Sophie Adenot dans l’espace
La mission centrale de Sophie Adenot consiste à changer un réflecteur sur le module Harmony dont le rôle est d’assister le guidage des vaisseaux qui se préparent au rendez-vous avec la Station spatiale internationale (ISS) pour s’y amarrer. La sortie complète doit durer près de six heures et demie, avec comme binôme l’Américaine Jessica Meir.
Au-delà du réflecteur, les astronautes effectueront plusieurs tâches de maintenance, notamment l’installation de câbles de raccordement pour le système de relais de données, la préparation du radiateur du spectromètre magnétique Alpha en vue d’une future maintenance et le remplacement d’une caméra HD sur la poutre de la station.
Pour repérer la Française à l’image, c’est simple : sa combinaison aura des bandes rouges sur les bras et les jambes, tandis que sa collègue sera en blanc intégral. Il y aura aussi, comme autre signe visuel distinctif, les patchs d’épaule avec les drapeaux de la France et des États-Unis. Bien sûr, Sophie Adenot aura les trois bandes tricolores.
Cette sortie extravéhiculaire sera l’occasion pour la France de diriger pour la première fois une EVA, en étant le membre numéro un du duo. Ce sera aussi la première fois qu’une Française participe à une EVA 100 % féminine. Pour la petite histoire, c’est avec Jessica Meir (qui va effectuer au passage sa 7e EVA) qu’a eu lieu la toute première.

articles.title: Apple shares 'shocking evidence' against former employee accused of stealing company data for OpenAI | TechCrunch
articles.text:
In its lawsuit against OpenAI, Apple filed what it calls “shocking evidence” to bolster its allegations that former employees stole trade secrets for OpenAI’s benefit. These new details emerged after the legal counsel for former Apple employee Chang Liu — who now works at OpenAI — handed over Liu’s old Apple work laptop for investigation earlier this month.
Apple now alleges that Liu used a confidential Apple circuit schematic in his work at OpenAI, as well as a tool that shares a name with an internal Apple engineering application. The company claims that OpenAI was “well-aware” of Liu’s access to Apple data, and that Liu enlisted OpenAI colleague Yu-Ting Peng to help destroy evidence in June when he learned that Apple was investigating him.
“The MacBook represents the very limited information Defendants provided so far (and only after weeks of delay), and shows Apple is not conducting ‘fishing expeditions’ but that its trade secrets are being used and evidence is being destroyed,” the filing reads.
While this new evidence is redacted from public view, past filings from Apple have included text messages from Liu — which he punctuated with “crying laughing” emojis — showing he was aware that he still had access to Apple files.
OpenAI has previously defended Liu by saying that he only accessed Apple files after he stopped working there in order to help former colleagues who asked for his assistance. “Apple now tries to shift the blame to ‘residual access,’ but they also don’t disclose that this is a common issue with Apple which is caused by them failing to properly manage system access when people leave,” OpenAI wrote in a blog post earlier this month.
But Apple claims that Liu had continued access because he “exploited a rare, previously unknown authentication bug.”
TechCrunch has requested comment from OpenAI on Apple’s newest allegations.
Apple is seeking a preliminary injunction — a court order that would block OpenAI from working on hardware based on Apple’s technology while the case is ongoing — as well as expedited discovery, a fast-tracked process for gathering evidence, since the company alleges that more former employees may also be implicated.
According to Apple’s initial filing, more than 400 former Apple employees now work at OpenAI.

articles.title: ‘I want one. And you should too. But I’m not convinced either of us can afford it’ — the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ gave me staggering performance with its Intel Arc G3 Extreme SoC but I’ll never stretch to that price
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
Honestly, the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ has changed what I believed a handheld console is capable of. The Intel Arc G3 Extreme chipset it’s packing offers astounding performance, delivering fantastically smooth frame-rates for modern games like Doom: The Dark Ages and Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. That screen is gorgeous and richly colored and the Hall effect thumbsticks and triggers are hard wearing and sensitive. But there’s a catch: it costs easily as much as many midrange gaming laptops, while not being able to rival them for performance. And that seriously limits the number of people I’d expect to buy one.
Pros
- +Absurdly powerful chipset
- +Staggering performance
- +Vibrant and super-smooth 120Hz display
Cons
- -Sorry, it costs how much?!
- -MSI Center M layer can be buggy
- -No mouse controls
Why you can trust TechRadar
MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ review: two-minute review
The MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ is a high-octane handheld games console that can run PC and Xbox games from a wide range of game stores. With the Intel Arc G3 Extreme chipset — featuring the Intel Arc B390 GPU and 32GB RAM — it’s easily the most powerful portable console I’ve ever (quite literally) gotten my hands on. But there’s a pretty huge catch to that performance: a price tag that would buy you two Steam Deck OLEDs or a mid-price gaming laptop.
Let’s start with the superficial stuff: the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ looks gorgeous. Its screen is an extensive eight inches across, offers wonderfully rich colors and a silky-smooth 120Hz refresh rate. Combined with its discreet RGB lighting around the asymmetrically placed thumbsticks and Void Purple colorway, it has a unique look that definitely helps it stand out from the crowd.
But its design goes far beyond aesthetics. Its Hall effect thumbsticks and triggers should not only offer greater longevity, but they felt really responsive, even if they’re not quite as sensitive as the TMR versions now offered by some controllers. Meanwhile, it felt perfectly ergonomic in my hands — I was genuinely surprised how light it felt for a 1.73 lb / 786g console — although its laser-etched grips sure made my hands feel sweaty, for some reason.
What cements the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ as one of the best handheld games consoles out there, though, is its performance. It’s the first gaming handheld on the market with the Intel Arc G3 Extreme chipset and, boy, does that have a pronounced effect on how it plays. While benchmarks showed it offered similar CPU performance to the recent Asus ROG Xbox Ally X, thanks to its Intel Arc B390 GPU and 32GB RAM, it managed to smash its 3D Mark benchmarks by between 35% and 76% — that’s a significant performance upgrade.
Numbers only tell part of the story, though: what was the Claw actually like in action? Well, Baldur’s Gate 3 looked truly gorgeous on Ultra graphics settings and yet it hovered around a decent 38fps. Meanwhile, despite only being released in 2025, both Doom: The Dark Ages and Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 played at a rock-solid 60fps — whether I was punching demons to death or countering devastating attacks, there wasn’t a hint of latency or lag. Even the boss-level challenge of The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion Remastered hit 60fps at points… before plunging to a stuttery mess in busier areas. Still that’s impressive stuff for a handheld console.
But the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ has a pretty huge barrier to Fosbury flop over: its price. In return for its premium components, you’ll pay a seriously premium price tag of $1,799.99 / £1,399.99 / AU$2,849. Not only is that significantly higher than any other gaming handheld to date, it’s also as expensive as some mid-range gaming laptops.
And that presents an enormous problem for the Claw. Despite the fact that some of the best gaming laptops come in at a similar price, many of them offer superior performance in our benchmark tests. Now don’t get me wrong: no gaming laptop offers the kind of ergonomics or compact form factor you get here, but I do have doubts that the pro gamers that can afford this kind of device will be willing to trade performance simply for the sake of increased maneuverability.

That’s a real shame because in almost every respect, the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ is a fantastic gaming handheld that has really stretched my expectations of what this kind of device is capable of. I want one. And you should too. But I’m not convinced either of us will be able to justify the spend.
MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ review: price & availability
Having launched on June 23, 2026, the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ is available now. As you can see from the specs — or if you took sneaky peak at the benchmarks in the performance section — it’s seriously mighty for a gaming handheld.
It’s the first handheld console on the market that rocks the Intel Arc G3 Extreme chipset, which includes the 12-core Intel Arc B390 GPU and a hefty 32GB RAM. That puts it considerably ahead of most of its competitors, even if it can’t quite rival any of the best gaming laptops for sheer processing punch.
Unfortunately, like the hero in a Greek tragedy — or Oddyseus, apparently — it has a fatal flaw. The price. At $1,799.99 / £1,399.99 / AU$2,849, its cost is possibly the most eye-watering thing I’ve come across in a while and that includes all the people on social media that bragged about raw-dogging the solar eclipse in August. While the price tag here might not literally melt your retinas, it’s likely to give you second thoughts.
By comparison, we threw some shade on the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X for its price on its release — and that only retailed for $999.99 / £799.99 / AU$1,599. The Claw 8 EX AI+’s sticker price outstrips every other handheld console by quite some margin, sitting more up the gaming laptop end of the spectrum. For example, a mid-spec Alienware 16X Aurora, with Intel Core Ultra 9 275HX, Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 and 32GB DDR5, goes for $1,999.99 / £1,799 (around AU$2,800). Ultimately, I think there aren’t going to be that many mainstream gamers able to pay this price and those that do are going to expect stellar performance in return.
MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ review: specs
| Category | Specification | 
| Price | $1,799.99 / £1,399.99 / AU$2,849 | 
| Display | 8-inch FHD+ (1920 x 1200), 16:10, 500 nits, 120Hz IPS touchscreen | 
| CPU | Intel Arc G3 Extreme | 
| Graphics | Intel Arc B390 | 
| RAM | 32GB LPDDR5X-8533 | 
| Storage | 1TB PCIe Gen4 NVMe SSD | 
| Port selection | 2x USB-C / Thunderbolt 4, 1x microSD Express card reader, 1x 3.5mm headphone/mic combo jack | 
| Weight | 1.73 lbs / 786g | 
| Dimensions | 11.7 x 4.9 x 0.94 inches / 297 x 124 x 24mm | 
MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ review: design
I’ll be honest: when I first picked up the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+, I was pretty shocked by how light and manageable it felt. Fundamentally, this is not a small console — it’s as broad-shouldered as the Steam Deck OLED or the Lenovo Legion Go S and weighs in at 1.73 lbs / 786g, which is the heaviest gaming portable I’ve gotten my hands on to date. But despite this, it never felt at all bloated, sitting comfortably in my grasp.
I’d chalk this up to its ergonomic design. On top of feeling well balanced, it offers flared grips, unlike previous iterations of the MSI Claw. These sat really comfortably in my hands, although they aren’t quite as easy to wrap your hands around as the controller-mimicking forked grips of the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X.
This was also helped by the laser-etched texture of its grips, which enabled me to keep a decent grasp on the Claw. But I will say they aren’t quite as comfortable as those on some of the best Xbox controllers I’ve tested, feeling a little on the rough side and quickly getting sweaty as I tried to splat sakapatates in Clair Obscure: Expedition 33.
The MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ also left a pretty good impression on some of my other senses too. No, I didn’t lick it — I’m talking visual appeal here, rather than gustatory. Subtle RGB lighting around each of the thumbsticks is my personal highlight, although I’ll also give its gentle curves and Void Purple colorway honorable mentions as well. Honestly, I’m a little less jazzed about the way the screen juts out past the bottom of the device, but this does seem to be a more common look these days, with the jutting grips of the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X creating a similar effect.
Speaking of screens, despite it not quite rocking the richness of the Steam Deck’s OLED display, the Claw 8 EX AI+ has a beautiful looking screen. As a result of its expansive eight-inch breadth and 16:10 aspect ratio, it rocks a 1920 x 1200 resolution, not to mention a variable refresh rate of up to 120Hz. Every game I played always felt detailed and smoother than whipped cream under a heat lamp. Meanwhile, its 500 nit typical brightness felt plenty bright enough in most settings — on max brightness, I even found I was able to play it outside, although when I faced it directly toward the blazing August sun, it was quickly overpowered by the fiery onslaught.
Anyone familiar with previous incarnations of the MSI Claw will be pretty familiar with the layout here. The Claw 8 EX AI+ has the same combo of asymmetrical thumbsticks, Xbox-style face buttons and vertically aligned Menu, MSI Center M, View and Quick Setting buttons that you’ll have seen on previous iterations. There’s only two macro buttons on its rear, which honestly feels a bit stingy compared to the four offered by the Steam Deck and many Xbox controllers.
On the plus side, the Claw 8 EX AI+ is packing both Hall effect thumbsticks and triggers — as well as preventing the inexorable drift issues that plague potentiometer thumbsticks, Hall effect sticks and triggers also offer smaller deadzones and increased sensitivity. They’re not quite as sensitive as the marginally fancier TMR thumbsticks and triggers you see in a lot of premium controllers these days but I’m not aware of any portable consoles that offer those currently.
So for the most part, its control scheme is suitably versatile. The only area it falls a little short is the lack of built-in mouse control for games that require a cursor. Unlike the Steam Deck’s super flexible trackpads or the quirky hybrid mouse-cons offered by the Nintendo Switch 2 and Lenovo Legion Go 2, the only way I could mimic a mouse input on the Claw 8 EX AI+ was by jabbing its touchscreen with my greasy hand-sausages. That ain’t gonna cut it for some Steam and Windows games. Now, in MSI’s defense, it has never pitched the Claw as a substitute for PC gaming, but it is a shame that some sections of my Steam library will lay tantalizingly just out of reach. Of course, I could connect a mouse via USB or Bluetooth, but that then prevents the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ from being as portable.
Another criticism I have is the fingerprint scanner. While I appreciate that these narrow scanners are space-efficient, they’re not efficient in any other sense of the word. Every single time I tried to log in to the MSI Claw, I found I had to pop my pinky on the scanner three or four times just to access the home screen. Given my MacBooks’ Touch ID readers require just a single tap to unlock, I honestly wish MSI found a way to squeeze in a circular scanner here.
MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ review: performance
Here is how the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ performed in our suite of benchmark tests:
3DMark Port Royal: 3,544; Fire Strike: 12,358; Time Spy: 6,534
GeekBench 6.5: 2,492 (single-core); 12,550 (multi-core)
Total War Warhammer 3 1080p (Ultra) 81.3fps (Low) 142.5fps
Cyberpunk 2077: 1080p (Ultra) 43fps (Low) 75fps
Dirt 5: 1200p (Ultra) 48.3fps (Low) 95.7fps
PCMark 10 Battery Life (Gaming): 1:40 hours
While the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+’s looks are impressive, what makes it exceptional is what’s going on underneath the surface. While gaming handhelds have previously involved some performance tradeoffs in return for their diminutive size, that’s not the case here, thanks to the Herculean Intel Arc G3 Extreme chipset it’s packing. MSI claims that the Arc G3 Extreme should unlock 42% faster performance on average compared to the AMD Ryzen Z2 Extreme that the Asus ROG Xbox Ally X is rocking, although this requires a little unpacking.
Certainly, performance benchmarks alone don’t suggest the Arc G3 Extreme is leading the field. The Claw 8 EX AI+ hit 2,492 single-core performance and 12,550 multi-core performance in our GeekBench tests, compared to the 2,788 and 12,883 scores nabbed respectively by the ROG Xbox Ally X. So for raw processing power, there’s not a huge amount of light between the two chipsets, with the Ryzen Z2 Extreme taking a narrow lead.
But factor in graphical performance and Intel’s SoC absolutely spanks AMD’s. With the help of the Intel Arc GPU B390, the Claw 8 EX AI+ gets some seriously punchy 3D performance — in our 3DMark benchmarks, it scored 3,544 in Port Royal, 12,358 in Fire Strike and 6,534 in Time Spy, compared to the 2,006, 9,141 and 4,033 the ROG Xbox Ally X hit. Those are 76%, 35% and 62% increases respectively, gains which show the Claw’s graphics are seriously swole.
And that translates to some staggeringly smooth performance in-game. On Ultra settings, Total War: Warhammer 3 comfortably averaged out at 81.3fps, while on Low settings Dirt 5 ran smoother than a nitro cold brew at 95.7fps and still managed a very creditable 48.3fps on Ultra. But what blew me away most is how well it ran Cyberpunk 2077 on Ultra settings with ray-tracing disabled, netting a reasonably polished 43fps — that’s downright playable and throws some serious shade on the ROG Xbox Ally X, which only managed 8fps.
Unfortunately, while these benchmarks are impressive compared to other gaming handhelds, at this price those aren’t the Claw’s biggest competition. Several of our picks for the best gaming laptops have costs in the same region and yet offer significantly better performance.
For example, the Alienware 16X Aurora with Intel Core Ultra 9 275HX, Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 and 32GB DDR5 we tested costs only a few hundred dollars / pounds more at $1,999.99 / £1,799. And yet its performance is leagues ahead of the Claw, hitting a 3DMark Time Spy score of 13,594 and Fire Strike score of 31,480 — that’s double and nearly triple the Claw’s scores respectively. Naturally, you’re not getting the same compact form factor but I wonder how much that truly matters for the kinds of gamers that are willing to drop almost one and a half grand on a pro gaming device.
Okay, enough nerding out over numbers. Time to focus on the thing you actually care about: how the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ actually feels to play.
Honestly, what the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ is capable of kinda blew me away. As those benchmarks would suggest, it can offer ludicrously smooth frame rates. Playing a 2D game like Hollow Knight: Silksong, it remained rock solid at 120Hz, with all the action as Hornet zipped around the rich, mysterious landscapes of Pharloom as slick as ice on a spring day.
Granted, that might not feel like much of a challenge, but this unflappable stability carried over when I transitioned to modern 3D games. Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 ran at a wonderfully smooth 60fps. Rather than having to strip it down to the basic visuals required to get it running on the Steam Deck, it actually looked pretty great and ran so stably I was able to crack out counter after counter on chromatic bosses. Being able to enjoy the game on the go felt like such a novelty that I’d honestly be happy to mop up the game’s remaining optional bosses purely on handheld.
Keen to push the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ to breaking point, I even tried playing a bit of The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion Remastered on Xbox. I’ll admit my expectations were pretty low here, as I’ve heard plenty of people complaining about performance issues on their 5000 series Nvidia GPUs. And yet, amazingly, it was playable.
Well, kinda. With the graphics settings on Low while in the depths of Xedilian, performance plowed along steadily at 60fps, which is truly wild for a AAA Bethesda game. However, it didn’t take long for it to start exhibiting some pretty hinky behavior — sporadically I encountered some audio stuttering and, once I entered a more densely populated open area, the frame rate dropped so far it was more 19th century zoetrope than an RPG from 2025. But I feel like most gaming handhelds would spontaneously combust if you even had the cheek to try this, so Imma still put this one in the win column for MSI.
On top of this, the Claw 8 EX AI+ seems to be able to keep a cool head during all of this. In comparison to its predecessor, the Claw 8 AI+, MSI promises the EX AI+ can achieve an extra 5W cooling capacity, 25% higher static pressure for fans, and 9% higher airflow, thanks to fans that are 0.5mm taller. I can’t speak to how accurate such granular figures are but certainly even slamming out epic boss fights or pushing the CPU to its limit, I rarely noticed the EX AI+ getting unbearably warm, which speaks to the strength of its cooling.
What the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ is capable of is honestly pretty staggering. The only criticisms I have come down to software and input issues.
The Claw’s MSI Center M launcher felt a little unreliable. Occasionally, I got locked out from being able to access it — hitting the MSI button did nothing, and switching between windows just returned me to the Xbox app. On top of this, sometimes switching out to this menu then returning to a game would lock the input, meaning I could no longer use controller settings till I’d switched out and back again. That’s not a total deal-breaker, but it is a shame, given how stable the Steam and Xbox OSes feel by comparison, and shows that even the mighty MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ isn't immune to Windows 11's unsuitability for gaming handhelds.
MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ review: battery
Given its huge 80Whr battery capacity, I was expecting the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ to have some serious endurance. Unlike the ephemeral life I get out of my 40Whr Steam Deck — where I’m lucky if I get 90 minutes out of many 3D games — the whopping battery in the Claw had me anticipating some pretty epic gaming sessions. Which is why I was a bit bemused by the actual results I eked out during our benchmarks.
Running our standard PC Mark 10 Gaming Battery benchmark with all the settings switched to balanced in both MSI Center M and Windows 11, I was shocked to see the battery discharged from 100% to 0% in just 1 hour 36 minutes. So sure was I that I must have made a mistake, I recalibrated the battery using the Claw’s built-in software, revisited all the settings and ran the benchmark two more times. Despite this, I was only able to squeeze out 1 hour 40 minutes and 2 hours 31 minutes on subsequent tests.
Certainly that’s not completely incompatible with my objective experience — on the console’s default AI Mode, I comfortably drained its full battery in a two-hour play session of The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion Remastered, for example. But that’s an incredibly demanding game, even for the MSI’s specs, and 2D games didn’t seem quite as thirsty in comparison.
So what’s going on here? Ruling out a fault with my review unit, I suspect that the capacious 80Whr battery the unit ships with is only part of the picture when it comes to the life you’ll squeeze out of it. The more important part? Its AI performance mode.
While our standard benchmarks set consoles and gaming laptops to balanced mode, the default performance mode for the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ automatically adjusts its power consumption on the fly for the best efficiency in any given moment. That means the mode you’re most likely to play it on will stretch out the battery life without causing a noticeable dip in performance.
Even when the battery has run dry, it doesn’t take long to top it up again. With its 65W charging, you’d expect it to take about 90 minutes to juice up that 80Whr battery — and that’s bang in line with my experiences. When plugged into a cable capable of at least 65W, charging up the Claw only ever took around an hour and a half. However, I did occasionally experience some glitchy behavior here, with progress freezing at 98% or 99% full even when left for 20 minutes, suggesting the console’s battery monitoring software can occasionally be a touch off.
Should I buy the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+?
Buy it if…
You want amazing performance
Thanks to its high-octane Intel Arc G3 Extreme chipset, the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ achieves genuinely wild performance for its petite, portable size.
You want to access to all your PC and Xbox games libraries on the go
Installing extra storefronts on a console like the Steam Deck is honestly a bit of a hassle. On the MSI Claw, you have access to the Steam, Xbox, Epic, GOG, EA, Ubisoft Connect games stores.
Don’t buy it if…
You’re not loaded
The MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ is one pricy meatball — at $1,799.99 / £1,399.99 / AU$2,849, it comes closer to the cost of a gaming laptop than a handheld console. And while it’s more compact than a laptop, it’s not as powerful.
You need a mouse input
One of the things that makes consoles like the Steam Deck or Lenovo Legion Go so versatile is their mouse inputs. Lacking an equivalent means the Claw 8 EX AI+ isn’t compatible with some mouse-based titles unless you plug in a mouse.

Asus ROG Xbox Ally X
The Asus ROG Xbox Ally X packs the AMD Ryzen AI Z2 Extreme chipset, which includes the slightly less impressive AMD Radeon RDNA 3.5 GPU, and hasn’t managed to squeeze as much RAM on-board, clocking in at 24GB rather than the Claw’s 32GB. On the plus side though, it’s significantly cheaper, coming in for $700 / £600 / AU$1,250 less, making it more manageable for a wider range of people. Read our full Asus ROG Xbox Ally X review.
Lenovo Legion Go S (SteamOS)
With integrated AMD Radeon Graphics, 16GB RAM and a 512GB SSD, the Lenovo Legion Go S (SteamOS) is more cruiser motorcycle to the MSI Claw’s superbike. But it’s still able to deliver steady performance, offering rock-solid performance during Baldur’s Gate 3 on max settings or a steady 40fps on Black Myth: Wukong on its lowest settings. And it’s cheaper than either of its rivals here, with a list price that starts from $649.99 / £699 / $1,329. Read our full Lenovo Legion Go S (SteamOS) review.
How I tested the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+
- Tested it over two weeks
- Tried playing a wide range of titles at different graphics settings
- Conducted TechRadar’s full suite of testing benchmarks
I tested the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ over the course of two weeks. I made sure to play a wide variety of games from multiple game stores, whether they were from TechRadar’s Steam library or Xbox Games Pass Ultimate. On top of this, I tried out a wide variety of games at different graphics settings, from relatively undemanding 2D games to AAA 3D titles.
When it comes to more detailed assessments of its performance, I conducted our usual suite of benchmarks. Not only did that entail getting detailed performance scores from 3DMark and GeekBench 6.5, but I also conducted a range of in-game fps benchmarks at both ultra and low graphics settings. To test the console’s battery life, I ran multiple PC Mark 10 Gaming Battery tests to see how rapidly it drained the battery from 100% and I also timed how long it took to charge the console from 0% to 100% using a cable that was rated more than its 65W max charging rate.
During my career, I’ve tested a wide variety of gaming gadgets and accessories, from wireless controllers to gaming handhelds. I’ve also invested a truly ludicrous amount of my four decades on this Earth playing computer games, whether they be RPGs, action adventure games or creative sandboxes. And while I’m a little hazy on the details, I’m told this investment will pay dividends any day now.
