articles.title: Ultradünne Solarfolie für Luft- und Raumfahrt
articles.text:
Effizient wie ein Solarmodul: Marktstart für ultradünne Solarfolie von Solarwindow
Flexible Solarfolien sind nichts Neues. Aufgebracht auf E-Autos sollen sie deren Reichweite verlängern. Zudem sollen sie in transparenter Ausführung auf Fensterscheiben geklebt werden können und so zusätzliche Energie für private Haushalte liefern.
Solarwindow startet Verkauf von Solarfolie
Das US-Unternehmen Solarwindow Technologies hat jetzt den Verkaufsstart einer Solarfolie angekündigt, die nicht nur ultradünn und flexibel ist, sondern auch mit einem hohen Wirkungsgrad punkten kann. Einem Bericht von pv-magazine.com zufolge soll die Zelleffizienz der nur 0,85 Millimeter dicken Solarfolie 24,4 Prozent erreichen und sich damit auf dem Niveau moderner Solarmodule bewegen.
Die selbstklebende Folie eignet sich vor allem für flache und gebogene Oberflächen sowie für Anwendungen, bei denen es auf jedes Gramm ankommt und wo herkömmliche Module nicht geeignet sind. Mit Electrolux zielt Solarwindow eigenen Angaben zufolge auf die Bereiche Transportwesen, Luft- und Raumfahrt, Landwirtschaft, Infrastruktur sowie Gebäudearchitektur ab.
Electroflex: Marktstart in den USA
Zunächst liefert Solarwindow die Folie nur an industrielle Hersteller in den USA aus. In den kommenden Quartalen sollen weitere Märkte in Nordamerika und Asien dazukommen. Ob irgendwann auch private Haushalte oder kleinere Firmen die Solarfolie kaufen können, ist nicht bekannt.
Bisher hatte sich Solarwindow auf die Entwicklung einer transparenten, flüssigen Beschichtung für Glas- und Kunststoffoberflächen konzentriert. Liquidelectricity soll auch in Innenräumen und bei schattigen Verhältnissen Strom erzeugen können.
Strategiewechsel euphorisiert die Börse
Mit Electroflex erweitert Solarwindow sein Portfolio jetzt um physische, flexible Solarprodukte. Das Ganze ist Teil eines Mitte August 2026 kommunizierten Strategiewechsels hin zu einer breiter aufgestellten Energieplattform. Neben Electroflex und Liquidelectricity sollen weitere neue Produkte kommen, wie Solarwindow-CEO Amit Singh ankündigte.
An der Börse hatte das für Euphorie gesorgt, wie es bei boerse-express.com heißt. Innerhalb der vergangenen zwei Wochen hatte sich der Kurs der Aktie des Unternehmens mehr als versiebenfacht. Ob die Hochstimmung anhält, hängt laut Beobachter:innen aber davon ab, ob die angekündigten detaillierten Produktinformationen sowie die Updates zur Produktzertifizierung halten, was sie versprechen.

articles.title: I tried the Suri Core 1.0 toothbrush for three weeks, and it's a solid budget pick
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
The Suri Core 1.0 is a fairly basic sonic toothbrush, offering a cheaper alternative to the Suri 2.0 (or Pro 2.0, as it’s now known). There are a few compromises, but in general it stays true to Suri’s philosophy of keeping what works – simplicity of design and recyclable elements – and leaving out what many people simply don’t want from an electric toothbrush, such as apps and a tons of settings. I'd like to see a few more settings for sensitive teeth and a more responsive pressure sensor — but overall, the execution is hard to fault and it looks good, too.
Pros
- +Affordable
- +Simple sonic operation
- +Recyclable heads
- +Sleek and pleasant design
Cons
- -No oscillation or extra settings
- -No travel case, just a brush cap
Why you can trust TechRadar
Suri Core 1.0: One minute review
I’ve tested numerous electric brushes with far too many settings and features, from 12+ brushing modes to apps that provide real-time guidance. Yet I inevitably end up using them in the same way: pick up the brush, press the button once, brush my teeth, then put it back in the cupboard until the next time. I’ve never used an app outside of a review period, and I rarely bother with any extra settings either. Battery life is also important to me, as I don’t have a compatible plug socket in my bathroom. And I’d also rather not throw out too many plastic brush-heads that will ultimately end up in landfill.
Suri brushes are designed to be no-fuss, no-frills sonic toothbrushes with minimal settings to avoid a simple tool from becoming unnecessarily complicated, alongside recyclable elements. The Suri Core 1.0 sticks closely to this brief, offering a more affordable alternative to its successful, pricier Pro range.
Naturally, Suri has cut some corners with the Core 1.0 to keep the price down, notably replacing the metal body with a "bio-plastic" one made from renewable sources and recycled material, while the motor is slightly weaker, offering 28,000 movements a minute instead of the Pro 2.0’s 30,000. It doesn’t come with a clean-and-charge case as the Pro does, either. Instead, you simply get a brush cap for travel. It lasts six days fewer than the Pro on a full charge, with a battery that lasts 28 days compared to the Pro's 34 days.
These efficiency savings are minor, and do nothing to impact the toothbrush’s overall quality. The simple design makes it eminently easy to use, while the built-in timer uses haptic feedback every 30 seconds to help you keep track of brushing time. It looks great, too, especially when stuck to the wall using the provided magnetic mirror-mount attachment. It doesn't feel quite as pleasing in the hand as the metal model, but the pastel-coloured body has a stylish look that will happily fit the aesthetics of a variety of bathrooms. Whichever colour you choose, the brush head is white.
Speaking of brush heads, in the US and UK, Suri operates prepaid mailing programs that enable you to send used heads back to the company, which it then recycles and makes into new products such as soap dishes. The toothbrush is also covered by a warranty, during which Suri will repair and return it at no cost. In addition, across the brush's construction, Suri has introduced measures to reduce the environmental impact of the plastics it uses, from recycled to recyclable materials to more responsible production and disposal .
I tested this toothbrush for 21 days straight, and in that time didn't have to charge it. The two-minute timer is automatic, with no option to adjust it manually: the brush pulses every 30 seconds to signal that you move to the next quadrant of your mouth then shuts off automatically when the two minutes are up.
There are a couple of niggles. The first is that the brush is almost too simple: alongside its Clean and Polish settings, I’d like to see a gentler mode "sensitive" setting for more delicate teeth and gums. The pressure sensor requires some force to activate it, which could result in over-brushing, and it’s quite loud in operation, registering 69db in my noise measuring app.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
But I’m nitpicking. Overall, the Suri Core 1.0 is a simple, high-quality sonic toothbrush for a reasonable price, with some sustainability credentials to boot. It would certainly be my pick over some of the more expensive, feature-stuffed brushes that spring to mind.
Suri Core 1.0: Specifications
| Component | Suri Core 1.0 | 
| Battery life | 28 days | 
| Sonic vibrations | 28,000/m | 
| Charging stand | USB-C | 
| Timer | 30 seconds, haptic | 
| Noise | 69db | 
| Settings | Two | 
Suri Core 1.0: Price and availability
- $75 in the US
- £65 in the UK
- Not yet in the AU
The Suri Core 1.0 is priced at $75 / £65, cheaper than other brushes in the Suri range, which come in at $99 / £85, and offers good value. It’s more expensive than budget electric toothbrushes such as the Ordo Sonic Lite, which is similarly basic in terms of features, but the Core 1.0 feels like a worthwhile step up.
It’s reliable, looks great on your bathroom counter-top, and with Suri's free brush-head recycling scheme, you can feel good about doing your bit for the environment, too.
Suri Core 1.0: Scorecard
| Category | Comment | Score | 
| Value | Pricier than some budget toothbrushes, but good value overall. | 4/5 | 
| Design | Great look, simple to use, recyclable and sustainable design elements. | 5/5 | 
| Performance | Strong motor, great battery, simple to use. | 4.5/5 | 
Suri Core 1.0: Should I buy?
Buy it if…
You’re after something simple
The Suri Core 1.0 does one job, at two intensities, and does it well.
You want a toothbrush that looks good
The Suri Core 1.0's pleasant design will look great on a bathroom shelf.
You want value
Suri made this toothbrush specifically to appeal to budget buyers.
Don’t buy it if…
You want an oscillating toothbrush
The sonic toothbrush is just a simple vibration model, whereas Oral-B models come with rotating heads.
You’ve got very sensitive teeth
You may prefer a brush with more settings and a lighter pressure sensor.
Also consider
Ordo Sonic Lite
One of the best budget toothbrushes on the market.
Read our full Ordo Sonic Lite review
Suri 2.0 electric toothbrush
Suri's excellent full-price electric toothbrush model.
Read our full Suri 2.0 review
How I tested
I used the Suri Core 1.0 sonic toothbrush for three weeks, brushing morning and night. I measured the decibel levels of the toothbrush using an app, and compared the specs to its contemporaries in the space.
First reviewed: August 2026
Matt is TechRadar's expert on all things fitness, wellness and wearable tech.
A former staffer at Men's Health, he holds a Master's Degree in journalism from Cardiff and has written for brands like Runner's World, Women's Health, Men's Fitness, LiveScience and Fit&Well on everything fitness tech, exercise, nutrition and mental wellbeing.
Matt's a keen runner, ex-kickboxer, not averse to the odd yoga flow, and insists everyone should stretch every morning. When he’s not training or writing about health and fitness, he can be found reading doorstop-thick fantasy books with lots of fictional maps in them.

articles.title: Windows vous indique que “la protection antivirus est désactivée” ? C'est probablement un bug
articles.text:
Windows vous indique que “la protection antivirus est désactivée” ? C'est probablement un bug
La Sécurité Windows/Microsoft Defender vous alerte soudainement que votre PC n'est pas protégé contre les virus ? Dans le doute, vérifiez, mais il s'agit probablement d'un nouveau bug de Windows.
Microsoft Windows 11 Famille
La dernière mise à jour majeure de Windows 11 n'est, comme souvent, pas avare en bugs. Cependant, aujourd'hui il est plus spécifiquement question de la dernière version de Microsoft Defender, l'outil de Sécurité Windows par défaut de Windows 11 et des précédentes moutures qui permet de se passer d'un logiciel antivirus tiers.
Après des retours utilisateurs remontant à début août, Microsoft a confirmé qu'un bug peut affecter certaines personnes et qu'elle travaille à un correctif. Ce bug n'est heureusement pas une faille de sécurité (cette fois), mais peut malgré tout semer la confusion.
Une fausse alerte de sécurité sur tous les Windows
Sur Windows 11, mais aussi les précédentes versions de l'OS, une notification peut ainsi s'afficher au démarrage du PC ou de manière aléatoire, indiquant que "La protection antivirus est désactivée". Cliquer dessus ouvre alors Microsoft Defender/la Sécurité Windows, où il est probable que ladite protection est pourtant bien activée. Microsoft confirme que ce souci est dû à la dernière mise à jour du service, sans préciser laquelle exactement.
En attendant que Microsoft déploie un correctif, qui arrivera probablement avec une future mise à jour de Microsoft Defender, il est impossible de masquer cette notification, qui peut revenir même en désactivant le système de notification ou en activant le mode "Ne pas déranger". Il faudra donc simplement se montrer patient.
Une rapide vérification s'impose malgré tout
Pour vérifier que l'antivirus de Microsoft Defender est malgré tout bien activé et qu'il s'agit d'une fausse alerte, c'est simple. Ouvrez la Sécurité Windows (depuis son icône dans la barre d'état système en bas à droite de votre écran par exemple) et direction le menu "Protection contre les virus et menaces". Cliquez sur "Gérer les paramètres" sous "Paramètres de protection contre les virus et menaces". Vérifiez que toutes les cases sont cochées.

articles.title: YouTubers "fix" melting RTX 5090 power connector by soldering cables directly to PCB
articles.text:
In a nutshell: The RTX 5090 and its predecessor, the RTX 4090, have been plagued by reports of catastrophic thermal failures that can cause the 16-pin power connector to melt, often destroying the card in the process. A team of Brazilian YouTubers has now seemingly found a "solution" to the problem by soldering the power cables directly to the GPU PCB.
TecLab recently demonstrated a workaround for the RTX 5090 thermal failures by modifying a 5090 to bypass the problematic 16-pin power connectors and route the power wiring directly to the GPU's PCB instead. For the experiment, they used a Galax GeForce RTX 5090 D HOF OC LAB XOC, which comes with two 16-pin power connectors designed for extreme overclocking.
The modification was carried out in two steps. First, the team used two adapters to accommodate two sets of wires from each 16-pin connector before soldering them to the connector traces on the PCB. Next, they removed the heatsink and the two 120mm fans cooling the GPU and added an industrial-strength water cooler to reduce the GPU's core temperature.
While the YouTubers did not reveal the GPU's temperatures after the modifications, the ~50A reading from the power meter connected to the 12V rail suggests that the card was drawing around 600W. For context, the Galax HOF OC LAB XOC can handle up to 2,000W, far more than the 575W TDP of standard RTX 5090 cards, thanks to a custom BIOS designed for professional overclockers.
TecLab acknowledged that its "solution" is not practical for most gamers and insisted that it was intended as a sarcastic take on Nvidia's repeated failures to fix the long-standing problem, rather than an actual recommendation to disassemble and permanently modify a $5,000 graphics card.
Ever since the RTX 5090 launched in January 2025, dozens of users have complained about melting 16-pin connectors. One of the earliest reported cases surfaced in February 2025, followed by two more reports in April and another in May. The issue was also documented by John Papadopoulos of DSO Gaming, who claimed that the 12V-2x6 cable connected to his RTX 5090 melted while he was playing Wuchang: Fallen Feathers.

articles.title: TP-Link announces its first consumer Wi-Fi 8 routers — Archer 8 Ultra preorder commences September 30, in select regions
articles.text:
TP-Link announces its first consumer Wi-Fi 8 routers — Archer 8 Ultra preorder commences September 30, in select regions
The Archer 8 Ultra launches first, while the Deco 8 Ultra arrives in Q1 2027
Earlier this year, TP-Link announced its intentions to launch the first members of its Wi-Fi 8 (802.11bn) networking family. At the time, the company revealed that it would first launch a standalone Archer 8 consumer router this fall, followed by a Deco 8 mesh router. And right on cue, TP-Link stated today that the Archer 8 Ultra BN19000 tri-band router will launch on September 30.
TP-Link is going light on the details at this time, but this is what we know so far. The Archer 8 Ultra BN19000 will come equipped with 18 internal antennas and deliver up to 19 Gbps aggregate wireless speeds. In addition, it will have 10 Gbps wired connectivity, though we don’t know whether that includes WAN and LAN ports or just the latter.
For users who require broader coverage in larger homes or offices, the Deco 8 Ultra BN22000 tri-band mesh router offers aggregate speeds of up to 22 Gbps and includes 10 Gbps wired connectivity. TP-Link typically sells its mesh systems in two- or three-pack configurations, and the Deco 8 Ultra BN22000 3-pack covers up to 9,800 square feet. Unfortunately, the Wi-Fi 8 mesh system won’t be available until Q1 2027, according to TP-Link.
TP-Link plans to expand its Wi-Fi 8 portfolio by Q2 2027 with a new Roam 8 travel router, along with range extenders and PCIe/USB client adapters. Although we don’t know which specific chipsets will power Archer 8 Ultra, Deco 8 Ultra, and other unannounced Wi-Fi 8 devices, the company says its products will use hardware from Broadcom, MediaTek, and Qualcomm.
Wi-Fi 8 is shaping up to be more of a quality-of-life improvement over Wi-Fi 7 than a substantial theoretical speed improvement. Put simply, Wi-Fi 8 hardware devices should be able to come closer to fulfilling the real-world performance metrics that Wi-Fi 7 devices originally promised.
To this end, TP-Link says that its so-called StabilityEngine leverages core Wi-Fi technologies including Enhanced Long Range (ELR) and Distributed Resource Units (DRU). These features together help improve wireless connectivity, primarily for low-power IoT devices that are typically positioned at the edge of your home’s wireless coverage. There are also additional technologies at play, such as Unequal Modulation (UEQM) and Modulation and Coding Schemes (MCS), to ensure uninterrupted wireless traffic in high-interference situations.
A new design language is also being ushered in with the Archer 8 and Deco 8 products, which was teased during TP-Link’s May 2026 announcement. “We stopped building a piece of networking equipment and started designing for the home,” explained TP-Link industrial design chief Gary Chang. “When a router’s design becomes something people want to display, it ends up exactly where it performs best.”
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
What remains unclear is how or when these new Wi-Fi 8 products will launch in the U.S. As of today, TP-Link has yet to obtain FCC approval to release all-new products in the country. Unlike competitors Amazon and Netgear, which received conditional approval from the FCC Covered List, the U.S. government is still playing hardball with TP-Link. For its part, TP-Link only says that preorders for the Archer 8 Ultra will open in “select regions” on September 30.

From Patna’s Settlements to Cancer Care and AI: The Story of Gautam Gauri
Discover how Gautam Gauri transformed personal loss into purpose, advancing education, cancer care, and AI-driven access in Bihar.
When Gautam Gauri returned to Patna in 2010 after leaving his corporate job, he did not come back with a grand business plan. He had just one question in mind:
How can children from low-income families be given better opportunities to learn and grow?
This question led to the creation of Diksha Foundation.
Today, nearly 16 years later, Gautam’s work has expanded beyond education into cancer awareness, healthcare, and artificial intelligence (AI). Along the way, he lost his mother to cancer, transformed that personal tragedy into a social initiative, and is now using technology to make reliable information and opportunities more accessible across Bihar.
Gautam’s story is not just about building social organisations. It is also the story of a changing Bihar, where people committed to long-term grassroots work are creating new possibilities for local communities.
In a recent conversation with YourStory, Gautam Gauri, Founder and Executive Director of Diksha Foundation and Co-Founder of Suchitra Cancer Care Foundation (SCCF), spoke about his decision to return to Bihar, the journey of Diksha Foundation, the cancer care initiative established in memory of his mother, and his experiences using AI in education and healthcare.
Leaving a corporate job to return to Patna
Gautam earned a Bachelor of Engineering in Computer Science from Birla Institute of Technology, Mesra between 1999 and 2003. He later completed an MBA from Institute of Management Technology (IMT), Ghaziabad between 2005 and 2007.
After graduation, he began his career as a Business Analyst at Cognizant, working in the company’s analytics division in Gurugram. While his career was progressing well, by 2010 he felt it was time to return to Bihar and contribute to his home state.
His family’s strong connection to public service also influenced this decision. His father, Tilak Raj Gauri, worked in Bihar’s Finance Department and served as Budget In-Charge for over a decade. His mother, Suchitra Gauri, was the principal of a DAV School in Patna.
Initially, his father considered leaving a stable job financially risky. But Gautam had already made up his mind.
He recalls:
"There was a sense of optimism in Bihar at that time. Many people were returning from outside the state, and I felt it was the right moment to contribute. I wanted to see whether it was possible to create meaningful impact while living and working in my own city and state."
Diksha Foundation began in local settlements
Diksha Foundation started on a very small scale. Gautam visited settlements around Laloo Nagar and Jagdeo Path in Patna and asked families whether they would send their children to a new learning centre.
The centre was about two kilometres away from where many children living near railway tracks stayed. Yet within just a few days, 30 to 40 children had enrolled.
For Gautam, this was the first sign that the need went beyond schools and textbooks. Children also needed spaces where they felt heard, understood, and encouraged.
At the beginning, there were no major institutional grants. The team created a live Google Sheet where friends and supporters could pledge small donations based on their capacity, with full transparency on how funds were used.
Sangeeta Didi joined the initiative from the start. She remains associated with the organisation today and has grown into a community teacher and leader.
A mother’s support helped transform 800 lives
Diksha Foundation’s work never remained limited to academic teaching. The organisation sought to connect education with children’s voices, confidence, and overall development.
About a year after its launch, Gautam’s mother, Suchitra, joined Diksha as a full-time volunteer. She worked directly with children and played a vital role in making the learning centres more welcoming and humane.
According to Gautam, his mother believed education was about far more than books and examinations. Children should have opportunities to express themselves, ask questions, and be heard.
In 2015, roughly five years after starting Diksha, Gautam received a Commonwealth Scholarship and went to the University of Cambridge, where he completed an MPhil in Education between 2015 and 2016. His studies focused on the purpose and values of education.
Ideas such as Howard Gardner’s Multiple Intelligences Theory and Nobel Laureate Amartya Sen’s Capability Approach helped provide theoretical grounding to many of the educational practices already being explored at Diksha.
However, Gautam chose not to simply replicate foreign education models in Bihar. Instead, he adapted ideas to local realities and needs.
Today, approximately 800 children and adolescents participate in Diksha’s educational programs. Around 500 children attend the organisation’s KHEL Learning Centres in Patna, Bihta, and Sarairanjan. Another 300 adolescent girls are part of the Empowering Futures program operating across six communities in Patna.
Learning centres became a second home
During Bihar’s scorching summers, when temperatures often exceed 40°C, Diksha’s learning centres serve as more than classrooms.
Children spend their afternoons and evenings there, studying, playing, and interacting until around 6 PM. Many parents work in construction, daily wage labour, or other occupations, making the centres safe and supportive environments for their children.
With support from Feeding India, meals are also provided to children at the centres.
Over time, the role of these centres has evolved. Former students return, mothers participate in activities, and children use the spaces not only for learning but also for sharing their experiences and concerns.
Gautam explains:
"We no longer see this merely as an after-school program. It has evolved into a community learning centre."
His mother’s illness inspired a new mission in cancer care
Around 2017–18, Gautam’s father began showing early symptoms of dementia. His mother, Suchitra, was caring for him when she herself started experiencing rapid weight loss and recurring fever.
Despite consulting multiple doctors, the illness was not immediately diagnosed. Eventually, it was discovered that she had cancer, by which time the disease had advanced significantly.
Gautam took her to Mumbai’s Tata Memorial Hospital for treatment, while his father remained in Patna under the care of a caregiver. Gautam spent nearly three months focused almost entirely on hospital visits and treatment.
After his mother passed away, it took him nearly a year to recover emotionally. Yet that experience eventually led to the creation of Suchitra Cancer Care Foundation (SCCF).
Dr Amit Kumar, who had been involved in his mother’s treatment, later became a co-founder of the foundation alongside Gautam.
Today, SCCF conducts cancer awareness programs and works to provide trustworthy information to patients and families. Gautam also hosts a podcast called Gautam OncoTalks, featuring conversations with oncologists from across India.
The foundation’s online cancer education library contains more than 50 videos, including expert discussions, awareness sessions, conference talks, and podcast episodes.
For Gautam, the challenge of cancer extends beyond treatment itself. Patients and families must navigate doctors, tests, medical terminology, and difficult decisions. Access to reliable information and guidance can make that journey less overwhelming.
Using AI to expand access to information
Technology has always been part of Gautam’s journey. His career at Cognizant began in analytics and technology, and the rise of Generative AI has given him a new opportunity to apply those skills to social impact.
SCCF is currently developing Suchi, an AI-powered cancer information guide designed to help patients and families understand trustworthy medical information and ask better questions during consultations. The goal is to make it available in regional languages such as Bhojpuri and Nepali.
Meanwhile, Diksha is developing Rusty, an AI tutor built around the Bihar Board curriculum. The project is being supported through JPMorgan Chase’s Force for Good program.
Diksha also runs WhatsApp-based life-skills programs through Glific.
For Gautam, AI is not about replacing teachers or doctors. Instead, he sees technology as a way to improve access to information and guidance, particularly in regions where resources are limited.
He says:
"In a state like Bihar, the challenge is not only a lack of resources. Often, people also struggle to access the right information and direction. If technology can help bridge that gap, then it is worth experimenting with."
“Bihar lives in my heart”
In 2010, Gautam was walking through Patna’s settlements, speaking with children and their families. Today, his work spans education, cancer awareness, and artificial intelligence.
During these years, Bihar itself has changed. New opportunities have emerged in education, technology, and the social sector. People like Gautam have chosen not merely to observe these changes but to actively participate in shaping them.
Yet for him, the greatest lesson of this journey is not about technology, institutions, or models. It is about showing up consistently and staying committed.
Gautam reflects:
"You will not always have solutions to every problem. Major transformations will not happen every time. But if you remain with people over the long term, you create a space of trust."
Perhaps that is the most significant aspect of his 16-year journey. Whether in education, cancer care, or AI, his work has remained centred on one idea: living among people, understanding their needs, and making information and opportunities more accessible wherever possible.
Bihar may have been the starting point of Gautam Gauri’s journey, but even after 16 years, it remains the centre of his story. It is here that his work found meaning, and it is here that his heart continues to belong.

articles.title: The Bentley Supersports: A stripped-out engineer's indulgence
articles.text: Bentley provided flights from Washington, DC, to Monterey, California, and accommodation so Ars could drive the Supersports, as well as ride in a preproduction Torcal EV, which we wrote about last week. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. MONTEREY, Calif.—Last week, we brought news of the Bentley Torcal, a new electric vehicle that the luxury automaker has been cooking up at its HQ in Crewe, England. The company wants to attract new customers with its first battery EV, part of a plan to make sustainability as much a part of the brand's character as its high-end fit and finish. W12 engines have given way to V8 plug-in hybrid power, and the new Continental GT is all the better for it . But around the same time as Ars got its first experience of that new PHEV two-door on a rather wet Spanish racetrack, some of Bentley's boffins were wondering what might happen if you also built one without the hybrid stuff. Or all-wheel drive—something that has been a characteristic of every new road-going Bentley since the turn of the century. That would certainly cut the curb weight. So, too, would leaving out the rear seats. That sort of idea leads down a well-trodden path for some OEMs, and Porsche in particular is famous for making stripped-out road cars inspired by its race cars and making money from them, too. articles.title: Il a gagné plus d'un million d'euros grâce à un service IPTV illégal, il finit en prison
articles.text:
Trois ans. C’est le temps qu’il aura fallu à Milan Ibrahim pour bâtir l’un des plus gros réseaux de streaming pirate du Royaume-Uni. Cet habitant de Chorley, 68 ans, vient d’écoper de six ans et demi de prison ferme pour avoir empoché près de 980 000 livres, soit environ 1,13 million d’euros, grâce à cette activité.
Un business bâti sur 80 serveurs
La Preston Crown Court l’a reconnu coupable de conspiration en vue de commettre une fraude. Selon l’enquête de la Police Intellectual Property Crime Unit (PIPCU), rattachée à la police de la City de Londres, son opération tournait sur pas moins de 80 serveurs, installés dans des locaux à Chorley. Tous ont été saisis et mis hors service lors de l’intervention des autorités.
Comme souvent, la méthode se voulait relativement simple sur le papier et redoutablement efficace en pratique : Ibrahim captait illégalement des diffusions télévisées appartenant à de grands ayants droit, notamment la BBC, ITV, Sky, la Premier League et la Motion Picture Association, avant de les reconvertir en flux IPTV et de revendre des abonnements à des clients partout dans le monde. Sa clientèle ciblait en particulier les expatriés britanniques installés à l’étranger, désireux de continuer à suivre leurs programmes favoris depuis chez eux.
Une procédure pour récupérer l’argent gagné illégalement
Au-delà de la peine de prison, Ibrahim devra désormais faire face à une procédure spécifique en vertu du Proceeds of Crime Act, visant à récupérer les sommes obtenues via la vente de ces services illégaux.
« Il est important que la PIPCU poursuive les criminels qui cherchent à profiter de la fourniture de services IPTV illégaux. Ces contrevenants font preuve d’un mépris total envers les ayants droit ainsi qu’envers les acteurs, artistes, techniciens et équipes de soutien impliqués dans la production du contenu qu’ils distribuent illégalement », a déclaré Emma Slater, responsable de l’enquête à la PIPCU. « L’IPTV illégale n’est pas un crime sans victime. Le préjudice financier causé par ces services affecte l’ensemble de l’industrie créative. »
Un signal fort envoyé par les ayants droit
Plusieurs des grands noms lésés par cette opération ont réagi à l’annonce de la condamnation. Stefan Sergot, directeur des affaires juridiques et de l’application du droit à la Premier League, a salué « un résultat significatif contre l’un des fournisseurs de services pirates les plus importants et les plus anciens du Royaume-Uni », ajoutant que la peine « envoie un message clair : ceux qui profitent du piratage seront tenus responsables ».
Même son de cloche à la Federation Against Copyright Theft (FACT), à l’origine du signalement qui a déclenché l’enquête : Nick Sumner y voit une décision dissuasive. Sky et la BBC ont, eux aussi, pris la parole par la voix de leurs responsables anti-piratage respectifs, rappelant que ce genre d’activité prive l’industrie créative britannique de revenus essentiels, avec des conséquences bien réelles pour les créateurs et les professionnels du secteur.
Le nom de Milan Ibrahim n’est pas totalement inconnu des registres officiels britanniques : les autorités britanniques recensent son passage comme dirigeant d’une société aujourd’hui dissoute spécialisée dans les logiciels IPTV, sans toutefois établir de lien direct entre cette structure et le service illégal visé par cette affaire.

articles.title: OpenClaw just gave everyone version 2.0 and it comes with major updates - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
OpenClaw just gave everyone version 2.0 and it comes with major updates
OpenClaw, the popular open-source personal agentic artificial intelligence framework, today announced the launch of version 2.0, the largest update in the agent’s history.
Unlike a traditional chatbot such as ChatGPT, which lives in a browser tab and only answers questions, OpenClaw acts like a digital secretary that can actually execute tasks on a user’s behalf and lives on their computer or in the cloud. It is a free, open-source AI agent that many users have turned into a coding agent or personal assistant to organize their inbox, manage their calendar and check in on their everyday activity.
Although the version release is 2026.8.1, the OpenClaw team is calling this 2.0 because it is a massive update, including mostly quality-of-life updates, better persistence, easier installation and increased security.
Up front, the OpenClaw team streamlined the installation experience so that new and veteran users can detect what’s already on their personal computer or cloud instance. For example, active ChatGPT or Claude subscriptions, application programming interface credentials and locally hosted models. The team said certain configuration options are set to defaults so users can start talking to their agent sooner, instead of getting bogged down guessing what’s available.
The dashboard has also been updated to become a real control center. Chat is now front and center and looks immediately like other AI interfaces users expect, with a text box that leads into a conversation. It allows users to start a new chat, rejoin ongoing work and watch an AI agent doing live work.
OpenClaw has also rebuilt the interface to be more interactive, with new widgets and dashboards. Users can bring widgets into chats, pin them to dashboards and assign actions that can be triggered by events.
In particular, the team said, it removed one previous limitation: Groups couldn’t work together with the same AI agent. Now, shared cloud sessions change that: Team members can join ongoing sessions and continue work where it left off, assign tasks to teammates with full context, and collaborate in real time on content and automations.
The OpenClaw team said it now uses this “multiplayer” collaborative feature to build the AI agent framework code itself.
Other quality-of-life updates include an updated search that lets users look through past conversations using exact text, words or phrases, and reopen the surrounding messages. This will let users easily find past work and resume where they left off.
Security updates include explicit trust boundaries, least-privilege controls and stronger protection against prompt abuse. OpenClaw is now aligned around who can trigger it, what it can access, where code executes and where credentials can be sent. It does this by controlling the gateway, providing permissions based on role and tool handling.
Early OpenClaw versions and installations suffered from major security flaws, so these updates help reduce the attack surface. Users are still expected to harden their installation against the open internet and maintain strong authentication if they choose to connect personal information or use tools that can execute on their cloud service or local machine.
This is the first major version update to OpenClaw since OpenAI Group PBC hired Peter Steinberger, the creator of the AI agent framework.

articles.title: La trabajadora de un hotel descubrió de la peor forma el precio de seis rollos de papel: 60.318,50 euros
articles.text:
Sustraer material del centro de trabajo puede ser motivo más que suficiente para que una empresa juegue la baza del despido improcedente para dejar en la calle a su empleado. No importa si el valor de lo sustraído es de un millón de euros o de poco más de tres euros.
Es lo que le sucedió a la gobernanta de un hotel de Calella, en Barcelona, que consideró que sacar por seis rollos de papel para secarse las manos por la puerta trasera del hotel no era motivo suficiente para su despido. El Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Cataluña no opina lo mismo. Cada rollo de papel le ha salido por más de 10.000 euros.
El lío de los rollos de papel y un perro mareado. Tal y como se recoge en la sentencia dictada por el TSJ de Cataluña, la protagonista del suceso era gobernanta en un hotel de Calella desde 1995. El 20 de junio de 2024, sobre las tres y cuarto de la tarde, las cámaras de videovigilancia captan como la empleada coge una bolsa grande de plástico. Dentro hay seis rollos de papel industrial, el que se usa para secarse las manos en el baño.
La grabación registra que la empleada esconde la bolsa cerca de la lencería, para a continuación salir con su hijo hacia la puerta trasera. Al ver que nadie mira, vuelve a entrar sola a por la bolsa. Al día siguiente, le entregan la carta de su despido disciplinario.
En ese momento, la empleada escribe a mano una explicación: "cogí el papel porque cuando vino a buscarme mi hijo el perro había vomitado el coche, lo cogí para limpiarlo y hoy lo he devuelto", se recoge en la sentencia. Ese mismo día también firma otro documento, redactado por el hotel, en el que reconoce los hechos y "muestra su arrepentimiento, manifestando que no volverá a suceder".
El juzgado le da la razón…y una indemnización. Ante la desproporción del castigo, la trabajadora demanda al hotel impugnando la demanda de despido disciplinario. El Juzgado de lo Social nº1 de Mataró da por buena la versión del vómito canino y considera que llevarse seis rollos de papel no es motivo suficiente para perder un empleo de treinta años. Por lo que le da la razón considerando excesiva la medida y declara el despido improcedente.
En este contexto, el juzgado establece que la empresa puede elegir entre readmitirla de nuevo asumiendo los salarios atrasados, o asumir el despido y pagarle 60.318,50 euros de indemnización por sus casi 30 años de servicio. Pero el hotel decide recurrir. Y lo hace.
Al TSJ de Cataluña no le cuadra. Los magistrados del Tribunal Superior de Justicia de Cataluña revisan las grabaciones de seguridad y lo que ven en ellas no les cuadra con la coartada. La sentencia recoge que "se observa como el hijo de la actora sale de una sala y avanza por el pasillo hacia la puerta trasera (...) la actora vuelve hacia dentro, y entra en la sala nuevamente, saliendo con un saco de 6 rollos de papel higiénico de uso industrial". Nadie más aparece en el vídeo. No hay coche a la vista, ni rastro de vómito, ni prisa por limpiarlo.
Tampoco ayuda el certificado del veterinario que la trabajadora presentó como prueba, fechado un día después, y justo cuando ya le habían entregado la carta de despido. El tribunal recuerda además que ella misma firmó, sin alegar presiones de ningún tipo, un documento reconociendo el hurto por escrito.
La confianza se quedó en papel mojado. El TSJ de Cataluña se apoya en el artículo 54.2 d) del Estatuto de los Trabajadores, que castiga "la transgresión de la buena fe contractual, así como el abuso de confianza en el desempeño del trabajo". Y recuerda una idea que se repite en los tribunales laborales: cuando hay hurto, no importa el valor de lo robado. "El contrato de trabajo se apoya esencialmente en la confianza mutua entre las partes", citan los jueces catalanes.
El convenio colectivo de hostelería de Cataluña también recoge en su artículo 6.4 el "robo, hurto o malversación" en la empresa como falta muy grave y motivo de despido disciplinario. Según el tribunal, en este caso es especialmente relevante esa falta porque la trabajadora era gobernanta, un puesto que exige, según recoge la propia sentencia, "un especial celo en el cumplimiento de sus obligaciones laborales".
Seis rollos de papel, cero indemnización. Con estos argumentos en la mano, el el TSJ anuló la primera sentencia que daba la razón a la empleada y declaraba el despido como procedente.
Al ser un despido disciplinario reconocido, no genera derecho a indemnización, pese a los casi treinta años que la trabajadora llevaba en el hotel. Por lo que, de facto, la empleada perdería los más de 60.000 euros que le reconoció la primera sentencia. La sentencia del TSJ, todavía admite recurso de casación ante el Tribunal Supremo, por lo que la historia de los seis rollos de papel, de momento, no ha terminado.

articles.title: Trump admin shelves Cyclospora research despite record-breaking outbreak
articles.text: The Trump administration is halting vital federal research on the foodborne parasite Cyclospora, despite the record-breaking, nationwide outbreak of the diarrheal pathogen, according to Politico . Of the three research programs that represent nearly all of the Cyclospora work at the US Department of Agriculture, two have been defunded, and the third is about to lose every scientist working on it. The Trump administration is shuttering the USDA's Beltsville Agricultural Research Center near Washington, DC, and moving its work to a location in Iowa. That includes relocating the remaining Cyclospora research. Although the research is still funded, insiders told Politico that not one of the scientists working on the project plans to relocate from Maryland to Iowa. Instead, they are either retiring, being reassigned to a different project, or leaving the USDA's research services. Read full article Comments

articles.title: Après leur fusion ratée, Nissan et Honda vont partager le logiciel de leurs voitures dès 2029
articles.text:
Cette fois, c’est la bonne. Honda et Nissan ont signé un accord pour standardiser une partie des calculateurs de leurs voitures, ainsi que le logiciel qui tourne dessus. Dans un communiqué publié ce 31 août 2026, les deux constructeurs japonais ont précisé que cette architecture commune doit équiper leurs modèles à partir de l’exercice 2029.
Leur cible, c’est la voiture définie par le logiciel, ou « SDV » (software-defined vehicles). Pour mémoire, il s’agit d’une auto qui a été conçue autour du logiciel, comme Tesla.
Une réponse tardive à la poussée chinoise
Le chantier avait démarré en 2024, quand Nissan et Honda annonçaient vouloir travailler ensemble sur les plateformes logicielles de nouvelle génération. Si entre-temps les deux groupes avaient finalement renoncé à fusionner, potentiellement à cause de Renault, il semblerait que tout soit revenu dans l’ordre.
En mutualisant les couches matérielles et logicielles, les deux groupes espèrent réduire la facture et gagner du temps. Car on ne peut pas dire que l’industrie locale est la meilleure sur le segment de la voiture électrique. Les constructeurs chinois avancent vite avec des modèles bourrés de logiciel et ils grignotent des parts en Europe.
Nissan et Honda ne sont pas les seuls à mutualiser pour tenir la cadence. En Europe, Volkswagen fait par exemple appel à Rivian pour développer la base logicielle qui équipera les futures voitures électriques du groupe allemand.
Nissan et Honda accusent un certain retard et cherchent donc des économies d’échelle pour tenter de le combler. D’ailleurs, ce ne sont pas les seules marques nationales à la traîne. Mitsubishi, qui ne fait que reprendre des modèles de chez Renault, se dit intéressé pour rejoindre le projet technique. Toutefois, rien de visible à court terme puisque l’échéance de cette alliance est fixée à 2029, lorsque leurs premières voitures en seront équipées. D’ici là, les rivaux chinois auront certainement déjà mis les bouchées doubles.

articles.title: ChatGPT, Reddit et Roblox rejoignent officiellement le club des géants surveillés par l'Europe
articles.text:
Bruxelles serre la vis, puisque ChatGPT, Reddit et Roblox rejoignent la liste des plateformes surveillées de près par l'Europe. Ces trois services ont désormais quatre mois pour se mettre aux normes du règlement sur les services numériques.
La Commission européenne a officialisé, ce lundi 31 août 2026, la désignation de ChatGPT comme très grand moteur de recherche en ligne, aux côtés de Reddit et Roblox, promus très grandes plateformes en ligne. Les trois services, qui affichent chacun plus de 45 millions d'utilisateurs mensuels dans l'Union, ont franchi le seuil fixé par la législation sur les services numériques, le fameux DSA (Digital Sercices Act). Ils rejoignent une liste qui compte désormais 28 géants du numérique surveillés par Bruxelles, avec pour eux de nouvelles obligations autour des contenus illicites, de la protection des mineurs et des processus électoraux.
ChatGPT, Reddit et Roblox désignés très grandes plateformes par la Commission européenne
En rejoignant la liste des services éligibles au DSA, ChatGPT décroche une étiquette à part, puisque la Commission le classe en « service hybride », capable de répondre aux requêtes en interrogeant le Web comme un moteur de recherche classique. Résultat, l'assistant conversationnel d'OpenAI entre dans la catégorie très grand moteur de recherche en ligne, aux côtés des mastodontes historiques Google Search et Bing, avec 159 millions d'utilisateurs mensuels revendiqués dans l'Union.
Pour Reddit et Roblox, c'est assez différent dans le fond, même si le verdict est le même. Considérez-les désormais comme de « très grandes plateformes en ligne ». Le forum communautaire, qui est organisé en communautés thématiques où chacun crée et partage du contenu, revendique 57 millions d'utilisateurs mensuels. Roblox, la plateforme immersive où l'on crée, publie et joue à des jeux conçus par d'autres utilisateurs, en compte 46,6 millions. Toutes deux permettent de diffuser du contenu de tiers à un large public, ce qui justifie leur classification selon le règlement européen.
Concrètement, ChatGPT, Reddit et Roblox ont jusqu'à la fin du mois de décembre 2026, soit quatre mois, pour se mettre en conformité avec les obligations renforcées du DSA. En clair, ils doivent désormais passer leurs propres algorithmes au crible pour repérer et corriger les risques qu'ils font courir à la société, à savoir la propagation de contenus illégaux, les dangers pour les mineurs, l'impact sur la santé physique et mentale des utilisateurs, les atteintes aux droits fondamentaux, les risques pour les processus électoraux, ou encore les menaces pour la sécurité publique. Notons d'ailleurs que les trois services n'étaient jusqu'ici soumis qu'aux règles générales du DSA. Il faut bien comprendre qu'ils basculent désormais dans le régime renforcé réservé aux poids lourds du numérique.
Bruxelles renforce sa surveillance entre coordinateurs nationaux et amendes salées
Ces désignations donnent surtout à la Commission européenne de nouveaux pouvoirs d'enquête sur le fonctionnement de ces services et, le cas échéant, sur tout système connexe qui y serait rattaché. Elle partagera la supervision avec les autorités nationales compétentes, à savoir Coimisiún na Meán, le régulateur irlandais pour ChatGPT et Reddit, et l'Autorité néerlandaise des consommateurs et des marchés (ACM) pour Roblox, où ces sociétés sont établies.
Les « petits nouveaux » sont en tout cas prévenus des risques qu'ils encourent, comme peuvent en témoigner les vétérans du club. Ces derniers savent déjà ce que coûte un faux pas. TikTok croule sous les procédures depuis 2024, Meta enchaîne les demandes d'informations et les ouvertures d'enquête, tandis qu'AliExpress et Temu ont respectivement écopé de 550 et 200 millions d'euros d'amende ces derniers mois.
Ces nouvelles désignations vont, selon la Commission, exposer les trois services à « un niveau plus élevé de contrôle et de responsabilité » répondant à leur poids dans la société européenne, que l'a dit ce matin Henna Virkkunen, vice-présidente exécutive de la Commission européenne. La liste des 28 plateformes sous surveillance rapprochée pourrait encore s'allonger dans les prochains mois.

articles.title: Riskante Software-Ausfälle: Robotaxis verletzen zunehmend das eigene Testpersonal
articles.text:
Unfallrisiko Robotaxi: Abrupte Manöver führen zu Verletzungen bei Testfahrten
Menschliche Sicherheitsfahrer:innen ziehen sich bei Testfahrten in den autonomen Fahrzeugen von Waymo und Zoox immer wieder Verletzungen zu. Das geht aus Daten der US-Arbeitsschutzbehörde OSHA, wie TechCrunch berichtet.
Demnach erlitten insgesamt mehr als zwei Dutzend Testfahrer:innen in den Jahren 2024 und 2025 Verletzungen, die durch plötzliche und unberechenbare Bremsmanöver der Software ausgelöst wurden. Zu den gemeldeten physischen Schäden gehören unter anderem Schleudertraumata, Verstauchungen und Brüche des Handgelenks, aber auch anhaltende Schmerzen im Bereich der Wirbelsäule.
Systemausfälle bei Robotaxis führen zu abrupten Bremsmanövern und Spurwechseln
Bei dem zu Amazon aus Seattle im US-Bundesstaat Washington gehörenden Entwickler Zoox ereignen sich die Vorfälle vor allem in modifizierten SUV des japanischen Herstellers Toyota. Wie TechCrunch unter Berufung auf anonyme Vertragsmitarbeiter:innen schreibt, kommt es bei diesen Fahrzeugen zu sogenannten „Nogos“, bei denen sich das autonome System unerwartet abschaltet und eine plötzliche Vollbremsung auslöst.
Diese harten Bremsmanöver passieren den Berichten zufolge oft bei Geschwindigkeiten von über 70 Kilometern pro Stunde, wenn das System vermeintliche Hindernisse auf der Fahrbahn fälschlicherweise als Gefahr einstuft. Bei einem dokumentierten Vorfall im Januar 2025 verletzte sich eine Testperson durch einen solchen abrupten Stopp an der Schulter, während eine andere Fachkraft in Las Vegas nach einer unerwarteten Fahrzeugbewegung für mehr als zwei Monate mit Rückenschmerzen ausfiel.
Verletzungen auch bei Waymo-Testfahrten
Auch bei der Alphabet-Tochtergesellschaft Waymo steigen die Unfallzahlen in Verbindung mit unvorhersehbaren Fahrzeugreaktionen. Das Unternehmen vergrößert seine Flotte für den kommerziellen Betrieb dennoch. Die für Waymo tätigen Testfahrer:innen sind meist beim französischen Mobilitätsdienstleister Transdev angestellt, der für die Jahre 2024 und 2025 insgesamt 16 solcher Verletzungen an die zuständigen Behörden meldete.
Die Verletzungen traten hauptsächlich in den Großstädten San Francisco, Los Angeles und Phoenix auf, wo Waymo den Ausbau seiner autonomen Flotte zuletzt vorangetrieben hatte. In einem Fall bremste ein Fahrzeug in Los Angeles derart hart ab, dass die betroffene Testperson 175 Tage lang nicht arbeiten konnte, während ein Kollege durch eine plötzliche Lenkbewegung des Autos einen Bruch des Handgelenks erlitt.
OSHA-Richtlinien verdecken Dunkelziffer bei kleinen Startups
Die tatsächliche Zahl der verletzten Fahrer:innen in der gesamten Branche dürfte noch spürbar höher liegen, da die OSHA-Richtlinien lediglich Unternehmen mit mehr als 100 Angestellten zur öffentlichen Meldung der Verletzungsdaten verpflichten. Startups und kleinere Entwickler autonomer Fahrsysteme, die ihre Software auf öffentlichen Straßen testen, tauchen in dieser behördlichen Statistik aufgrund der gesetzlichen Ausnahmeregelung gar nicht erst auf.
Weil die unerwarteten Stopps bereits mehrfach Auffahrunfälle verursacht haben, steht das Bremsverhalten der Zoox-Fahrzeuge schon länger im Fokus der US-Verkehrssicherheitsbehörde NHTSA. Zwar spielte das Unternehmen ein Software-Update auf, um den Fehler zu beheben. Laut TechCrunch berichten Vertragsfahrer:innen jedoch, dass die Systeme trotz des Updates noch bis in den Juli 2026 hinein abrupte Vollbremsungen hinlegten.
Wie Gizmodo ergänzt, belegen diese Zwischenfälle anschaulich, dass die Softwareentwicklung den Expansionsplänen der Technologieunternehmen hinterherhinkt. Trotz der ungelösten Probleme vergrößern die Betreiber ihre Testgebiete rasant.
Die Systeme lassen sich nach wie vor von harmlosen Objekten auf der Fahrbahn irritieren und reagieren mit abrupten Stopps. Solche Phantombremsungen sind ein handfestes Sicherheitsrisiko: Sie verletzen nicht nur das Personal an Bord, sondern gefährden auch die Insassen nachfolgender Autos. Bevor die Flotten weiter wachsen, müssen die Entwickler ihre Sensorauswertungen zwingend in den Griff bekommen.

articles.title: Workday reimagines workflows with enterprise AI agents - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Workday rethinks the enterprise workflow for AI agents
Enterprise AI agents promise to simplify everyday work, but delivering that experience requires far more than embedding AI into existing enterprise applications.
Enterprise AI has expanded well beyond chatbots and copilots into workflows that affect hiring, finance and other business operations. As organizations move AI deeper into those processes, they also need ways to preserve the governance and accountability that enterprise systems already provide, according to Gabe Monroy (pictured), chief technology officer at Workday Inc.
“It’s really around how do you take the magic of these probabilistic systems and mirror it with the deterministic guarantees that you get out of an [enterprise resource planning] system like a Workday?” he said. “You can get the guarantees of people and money and the rules that are in such a system, but you can get the probabilistic reasoning that is provided by AI systems and those two things working together.”
Monroy spoke with theCUBE’s John Furrier during the Google Cloud: AI Agents in Action Series on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how Workday and Google Cloud are integrating AI into enterprise workflows while preserving the guardrails organizations require for mission-critical business processes. The segment included live demonstrations that showed how the partnership is designed to simplify everyday work while keeping AI agents aligned with enterprise policies and systems of record. (* Disclosure below.)
Rethinking the enterprise workflow
Many organizations already rely on Google Workspace as the center of employees’ daily work. Rather than asking customers to switch applications, Workday’s collaboration with Google Cloud focuses on extending enterprise AI agents into the tools users already know, according to Monroy.
“What we find is that a lot of customers are really bought into the Google Workspace and broader Gemini ecosystem,” he said. “We don’t want to ask customers to have to switch their front doors or log into Workday when they’re happy to use Gemini systems. Instead, we want to bring our agentic innovation through Google Cloud and allow customers to choose those front doors.”
During the first live demonstration, Monroy showed how an employee could begin a quarterly performance review directly from Gmail using Gemini Enterprise, automatically incorporate recent Workday feedback, initiate the review workflow and schedule time with a manager without leaving the existing workspace. The approach reflects a broader shift toward embedding AI into employees’ existing workflows instead of requiring them to navigate multiple enterprise applications.
“If you think about the perception of ERP systems like Workday, they’re considered clunky, slow,” Monroy said. “You’re clicking through a lot of screens; you’re navigating, and I think that perception’s fair. What you’re seeing here is what the next generation of ERP is intended to look like: It’s natural; it meets you where you are in email. It’s a structured workflow that’s allowing you to follow the guardrails … but the net result is something a lot more … joyful than the equivalent today.”
Building guardrails for enterprise AI agents
A second demonstration contrasted what Monroy described as “lawless” agent behavior that runs on the platform it’s governed by. While the first agent completed a worker onboarding request without required approvals or policy checks, the second followed compensation limits, background check requirements and approval workflows before proceeding. That difference illustrates why enterprise AI depends on deterministic guardrails backed by authoritative systems of record rather than AI reasoning alone, according to Monroy.
“In that first example, you almost didn’t know that it was lawless, because it wasn’t the agent’s fault; it was just goal-seeking in a vacuum,” he explained. “In this case, it’s running on the Workday platform that supplies those guardrails that are really difficult to supply when you’re not running on top of the system of record.”
Building those capabilities remains an evolving engineering discipline, Monroy added. Organizations developing AI agents independently must create their own approaches to context management, permissions, tool selection and governance, while Workday’s platform incorporates those controls into its runtime for enterprise workloads.
“We’re able to provide guardrails that are wildly differentiated,” Monroy said. “If you’re building on your own, you’re going to have to come up with your own versions of these things. There’s no solved answer to this. This is emerging technical best practice.”
As organizations expand enterprise AI agents into more sophisticated business processes, their deployment strategies should match the complexity of the task, Monroy noted. Simpler interactions may rely on protocols such as Model Context Protocol, with more advanced workflows often requiring orchestrated reasoning or richer user interfaces tailored to enterprise applications.
“Today, the best place to get that experience is inside of our Sana UI, where we’re able to control every pixel and provide a truly rich experience for customers,” Monroy said. “I think for folks who are trying to build AI solutions, you’ve got to think about where do you need to control just the MCP surface? Where do you need to control the reasoning chain as the second step versus where do you need to control the end-to-end UI and every pixel on the screen? That’s, I think, the guidance as best I’ve laid out.”

articles.title: Vehículos autónomos Zoox están lesionando a los conductores que prueban los autos antes de salir al mercado
articles.text:
La proliferación de vehículos autónomos en las calles de ciudades como Los Ángeles o San Francisco está transformando la movilidad urbana, pero el avance tecnológico convive con una realidad menos visible: los conductores de prueba aún son esenciales para operar estos automóviles y su seguridad laboral está siendo cuestionada.
Un reporte reciente indica que los empleados que supervisan y prueban modelos de Waymo y Zoox han sufrido lesiones, lo que plantea interrogantes sobre el impacto de la automatización en el bienestar humano.
PUBLICIDAD
Lesiones laborales en la industria de vehículos autónomos: datos y causas
Un informe publicado por TechCrunch, que cita datos de la Administración de Seguridad y Salud Ocupacional (OSHA), revela que Waymo y Zoox, compañía perteneciente a Amazon, notificaron más de 20 incidentes en los que empleados resultaron lesionados durante pruebas en sus vehículos autónomos.
La mayoría de las lesiones estuvieron relacionadas con maniobras inesperadas, como frenazos o cambios bruscos de dirección, situaciones comunes cuando se prueba software que aún no está completamente pulido para la conducción sin intervención humana.
PUBLICIDAD
Entre los daños sufridos por los conductores de prueba se incluyen esguinces, dolores de espalda y latigazos cervicales. Estos incidentes han ido en aumento conforme las empresas expanden sus operaciones a nuevas ciudades y suman más kilómetros de pruebas.
Los conductores de prueba son operadores humanos contratados por las empresas de tecnología que viajan a bordo de los vehículos de desarrollo para supervisar su funcionamiento en el mundo real.
PUBLICIDAD
Especialmente, se observa una mayor incidencia en mercados prioritarios para el sector, como Phoenix, Los Ángeles y San Francisco, donde la circulación de estos vehículos de prueba es cada vez más frecuente.
La diversidad de vehículos utilizados para las pruebas también es un factor relevante. No siempre se emplean modelos específicamente diseñados para la conducción autónoma, como el Waymo Jaguar I-Pace, el Zoox Robotaxi o el nuevo Ojai.
PUBLICIDAD
En muchos casos, los ensayos se realizan en automóviles modificados, como el Toyota Highlander adaptado con sensores y sistemas de software experimental, lo que puede incrementar la probabilidad de movimientos imprevistos y, en consecuencia, de accidentes laborales.
Impacto de la expansión acelerada de vehículos autónomos en las ciudades
La rápida extensión de los ensayos con vehículos autónomos pone en evidencia que, tanto las ciudades como las empresas, enfrentan desafíos logísticos y de seguridad. Los incidentes reportados muestran que la infraestructura urbana y los protocolos internos de las tecnológicas no siempre están preparados para el ritmo de crecimiento de la industria.
PUBLICIDAD
Esto se traduce en una dificultad para garantizar la seguridad de los conductores de prueba y, eventualmente, de los pasajeros de estos futuros servicios.
Los organismos federales de seguridad han comenzado a investigar los incidentes relacionados con vehículos autónomos que ya circulan sin conductor.
Este escenario podría obligar a las empresas a reducir el ritmo de despliegue de nuevas unidades y a revisar sus estrategias de expansión, priorizando el desarrollo de software y la capacitación en seguridad para los empleados que aún intervienen en el proceso.
PUBLICIDAD
Perspectivas para la industria automotriz y el rol de la regulación
La relevancia de la conducción autónoma no se limita a grandes empresas como Waymo, Zoox, Uber o Tesla. Fabricantes más pequeños de vehículos eléctricos como Lucid y Rivian, así como grandes conglomerados como Hyundai, consideran que el sector autónomo será clave para su crecimiento en los próximos años.
En este contexto, se prevé que instituciones como la OSHA incrementen la vigilancia sobre las condiciones laborales de los conductores de prueba, exigiendo mayores estándares de seguridad y protocolos de prevención.
PUBLICIDAD
La evolución de la industria dependerá en gran medida de la capacidad de las empresas para equilibrar la innovación tecnológica con la protección de los trabajadores que actualmente hacen posible el desarrollo de los vehículos autónomos.

articles.title: « Ils se sont dit qu’on était une arnaque » : redressement judiciaire pour l'antivol vélo qui pue le cadavre après son passage sur Qui veut être mon associé
articles.text:
CactUs Lock a été fondée par Aïko Leroux, une ingénieure chimiste lyonnaise que nous avions rencontrée pour la première fois au salon Vélo in Paris 2025. L’idée d’Aïko Leroux était à l’époque inédite : un antivol vélo qui dégage une odeur de cadavre dès lors qu’on le coupe.
Malheureusement, l’avenir de CactUs Lock semble profondément menacé, elle qui est aujourd’hui en redressement judiciaire – qui ne signifie pas une faillite et encore moins une liquidation judiciaire.
Votre production solaire dépasse votre consommation ? Le SolarFlow 2400 AC+ stocke automatiquement votre surplus dans vos batteries. 100 % compatible avec la grande majorité des installations solaires en toiture, il permet de faire évoluer votre système simplement et à moindre coût.
Le tribunal de commerce de Romans a en effet rendu son jugement d’ouverture le 29 juillet 2026, publié au BODACC le 7 août, avec une date de cessation des paiements fixée au 14 juillet. L’entreprise poursuit son activité le temps de trouver une porte de sortie.
Des ventes pourtant au beau fixe
Nous avions de nouveau échangé avec Aïko Leroux au Vélo in Paris 2026, en avril dernier, pour faire un point d’étape sur l’entreprise. À l’époque, l’entreprise comptait plus de 1000 ventes en un an et se satisfaisait de ce résultat après avoir apporté moult modifications et optimisations à son cadenas.
Un passage à la télé qui aurait fait fuir les clients
En réalité, son passage sur l’émission Qui veut être mon associé ? semble être la cause directe de ce redressement judiciaire. « Les suites de Qui veut être mon associé ont été tragiques pour nous. Le soir de l’émission, nous n’avons pas eu de trafic sur notre site. Nous avions pris un risque en constituant un stock plus important. Je ne le regrette pas. Si nous avions reçu des commandes sans constituer de stock, cela aurait été un scandale de refuser des commandes. Le risque n’a pas payé, c’est le jeu », racontait-elle dans les colonnes de Lyon Décideurs, début août.
Et d’enchaîner : « Les personnes qui avaient passé commande se sont dit qu’on était une arnaque. On a failli perdre la moitié de nos contrats. L’émission n’a eu que des retombées négatives ».
Pour autant, Aïko Leroux assure que « la boîte va bien, nous avons seulement besoin de plus de temps pour payer nos fournisseurs ».
CactUs Lock n’est pas un cas isolé. Ces derniers mois, le vélo français a enchaîné les procédures : Reebike a été placée en liquidation, Lapierre est actuellement en redressement à la suite de la faillite de sa maison-mère Accell Group, alors qu’O2feel est à la recherche d’un repreneur.

articles.title: How new broadcast technology is changing the way fans watch cricket
articles.text:
itw Universe
View Brand Publisher
How new broadcast technology is changing the way fans watch cricket
The India-Afghanistan cricket series will bring together immersive camera angles, AI-led graphics, and a fan-powered sight screen to create new ways for audiences and brands to engage with the game.
Cricket broadcasting has come a long way since the BBC showed matches from a single end of the stadium, using three to four cameras. Today, multiple camera angles, smart graphics, and new technology have changed how viewers experience the game, while giving brands ways to integrate themselves into the broadcast without disrupting it.
When India take on Afghanistan in Delhi from September 13, the bilateral series will introduce several broadcast innovations together for the first time.
Film directors often have signature techniques that become part of their storytelling. Martin Scorsese is known for tracking shots, Alfred Hitchcock used the Dolly Zoom to create a sense of urgency, while Wes Anderson is known for his symmetrical framing. Sport has developed its own visual language, with distinctive camera angles, effects, and graphics helping make live action more cinematic. The NFL, for instance, used NFL Films to develop a distinctive approach to American Football.
Cricket has adopted similar innovations over the past three decades as the game’s popularity, particularly in India, has grown. The India-Afghanistan series will bring several of these technologies together.
One of them is the Magic 360 Cam, which “freezes” a moment and then unfolds it across multiple camera angles, creating the impression that the field is rotating 360 degrees. The visual is similar to some of the action sequences in The Matrix.
The Skel Track will offer a biomechanics view of players in action, showing how their bodies move while playing a shot. It is designed to help viewers understand elements such as balance, head angle, and weight transfer.
There will also be an Umpire Cam, using AI-stabilized technology to provide a first-person view of the action from the umpire’s perspective. Player trackers will show the real-time positioning of fielders, allowing fans to see how a field is set and imagine themselves as armchair captains.
These technologies also offer brands opportunities for contextual branding and messaging within the broadcast, without adding to the visual clutter viewers already encounter during a match.
When fans power the game
The series will also feature what is being described as a first in cricket: a fan-powered sightscreen.
At branded cycle stations, spectators will pedal to generate kinetic energy that helps power the sight screen. The idea is to turn the energy generated by fans into a visible part of the live cricket experience.
Traditionally powered by diesel generators, the sight screen will instead use clean kinetic energy generated by spectators. The activation brings together sport, fitness, technology, and sustainability, while creating opportunities for health, fitness, lifestyle, and energy brands to engage with fans.
The concept also gives brands an opportunity to extend their activations beyond the stadium through content and storytelling around the property.
Explaining the thinking behind elevating the broadcast experience for bilateral cricket, Bhairav Shanth, Co-founder of ITW Universe, who are the rightsholders for the series, said: “Our focus has always been on creating platforms where brands can move beyond visibility and become part of the fan experience. The India versus Afghanistan series allows us to do exactly that by combining innovative broadcast assets with interactive fan activations.”
He added, “We want brands to connect with audiences at moments that are exciting, relevant, and memorable, ultimately driving deeper engagement and stronger recall.”

articles.title: Redditor Picks Up a GeForce RTX 5070 For Just $129 After Walmart Mixes Up Price Tags
articles.text:
Monday, August 31st 2026
	
		
	
	
	
Redditor Picks Up a GeForce RTX 5070 For Just $129 After Walmart Mixes Up Price Tags
A Walmart customer in California paid just $129 for a PNY RTX 5070 after a store employee misplaced a price label. Reddit user "TransformersGuru" found the GPU on a shelf with a $129 tag positioned directly below it. The price actually belonged to a Corsair Nautilus 360 ARGB AiO liquid cooler, not to the graphics card sitting on the shelf. Apparently, the RTX 5070 was locked inside a glass display case, with the wrong price tag sitting just below it. After the customer raised the issue with a store manager, Walmart accepted the mistake and sold the card at just $129.
The buyer also purchased a $59 extended service plan for the card. With tax included, the total came to $198.97. Thanks to recent RTX 50-series price hikes, the cheapest RTX 5070 listing on Amazon at the time was around $820, putting the total price well below a quarter of typical retail cost. Under California's consumer protection rules, retailers are required to honor a displayed shelf price even when it results from an error; however, that can vary on a case-by-case basis. Pricing protections around mislabeled shelf tags vary by state, so the outcome here may not be typical outside California.

articles.title: Encore moins de démarchage téléphonique : ces deux applications ne plaisantent plus face aux appels indésirables
articles.text:
Encore moins de démarchage téléphonique : ces deux applications ne plaisantent plus face aux appels indésirables
Malgré l’interdiction légale du démarchage téléphonique, les appels indésirables persistent et signent sur nos mobiles. Bonne nouvelle : deux apps phares déploient de nouvelles armes pour les filtrer toujours plus efficacement.
Malgré la loi sur le démarchage téléphonique d’août 2026, cela ne suffit pas à éradiquer les coups de fil abusifs et intempestifs qui polluent le quotidien sur smartphone. Saracroche et Silence.app, deux applications anti-démarchage, ont riposté en affûtant leurs fonctionnalités. Voici les nouveautés majeures à activer dès maintenant pour retrouver (enfin) un peu de tranquillité.
Anti-démarchage téléphonique : les nouvelles fonctionnalités à activer
Saracroche 5.0 : des listes communautaires renforcées
Toujours 100 % gratuite, l'app Saracroche passe en version 5.0, repensant à cette occasion la gestion de ses répertoires de blocage. En plus de pouvoir activer ou désactiver chaque liste à la carte, d'explorer le détail des numéros enregistrés ou d'en retirer manuellement, l’utilisateur peut désormais en ajouter de nouvelles particulièrement utiles.
L’application intègre en effet des registres alimentés par les signalements de la communauté, composés de numéros identifiés “au moins 30 fois avec un taux de spam d’au moins 90 %”. De quoi affiner le filtrage automatique grâce aux multiples retours partagés par les utilisateurs.
Pour information, iGeneration rapporte que vos listes existantes risquent d’être réinitialisées lors du passage à cette nouvelle version ; il faudra alors utiliser la fonction Réinstaller les listes pour les restaurer.
Silence.app : le filtrage des appels en direct avec Live Caller ID
De son côté, Silence.app (3,99 €, uniquement sur l’App Store d’Apple) ajoute une nouvelle corde à son arc avec la fonction Live Caller ID (l'identification des correspondants en direct).
Concrètement, cette option vient interroger instantanément une base de données distante, sécurisée et anonymisée, lorsqu’un numéro inconnu tente de vous joindre. Si le numéro est répertorié comme indésirable, le rejet s’effectue automatiquement avant même que votre iPhone ne se mette à sonner.
Pour l’activer sur iOS, il suffit de suivre ce chemin dans les réglages de l'appareil : Apps > Téléphone > Blocage d’appels et identification > Recherche d’identifiants de correspondants en direct.

articles.title: Polymarket reportedly raises $300 million from Donald Trump Jr.'s investment fund | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The popular prediction market Polymarket has raised $300 million from 1789 Capital as part of a new funding round totaling around $1 billion, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing unnamed sources.
1789 Capital, an investment fund in which Donald Trump Jr. is a partner, previously invested $200 million in the prediction site. The firm has funded other controversial tech-related projects, including the Enhanced Games, the so-called “steroid Olympics” founded by veterans of various tech companies.
TechCrunch has reached out to Polymarket for comment.
Prediction markets have come under increased regulatory scrutiny, as many state governments seek to institute new rules around how (or even if) the sites can be used by residents. There are at least 20 states engaged in litigation against prediction sites over sports wagers offered on those sites.
The federal government, meanwhile, has frequently sought to defend the prediction industry from state regulation. The Trump administration has argued that the sole regulator of the industry should be the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), not state governments. The CFTC has sued at least nine states over their attempts to regulate the industry.
A coalition of 44 state attorneys general recently signed a letter arguing that the CFTC does not have the authority to regulate sports-related wagers on prediction sites.
The New York Times has reported that Donald Trump Jr. recently appeared at an event involving conservative state attorneys general, where he described the prediction industry as already having “robust oversight” and characterized prediction sites as a tool “overseen by federal officials, not state attorneys general.”

articles.title: Tablet 512 GB: os 7 melhores modelos para quem prioriza armazenamento • Tecnoblog

Tablet 512 GB: os 7 melhores modelos para quem prioriza armazenamento
Precisa de espaço? Selecionamos os melhores tablets com 512 GB de memória interna para armazenar milhares de livros, vídeos e mais arquivos
Um tablet com 512 GB traz a vantagem de guardar muitos aplicativos, documentos, fotos e vídeos sem a necessidade de armazenamento externo. Essa capacidade de memória está presente tanto em dispositivos mais poderosos, como o Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra e o iPad Air M4, quanto em alternativas mais acessíveis, de marcas como Xiaomi e Lenovo.
Neste guia, o Tecnoblog reuniu sete tablets com 512 GB para comprar em 2026, comparando armazenamento, desempenho, tela, expansão por microSD e recursos para trabalho e estudo. Veja prós e contras de cada modelo.
O Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra de 512 GB usa armazenamento UFS 4.0, com taxas de transferência superiores às de gerações anteriores.
O modelo também permite expandir o espaço via cartão microSD de até 2 TB, ajudando a manter arquivos pesados, vídeos e documentos fora da memória interna — uma vantagem sobre os iPads, que não oferecem suporte a microSD.
A combinação de 12 GB de RAM com o processador MediaTek Dimensity 9400+ coloca o tablet entre os modelos mais preparados para multitarefas, apps de edição, jogos e uso como PC no modo DeX. A bateria de 11.600 mAh permite até 23 horas em reprodução de vídeo.
Ele traz ainda tela Dynamic AMOLED 2X de 14,6″ (2960 x 1848 pixels) e taxa de atualização de até 120 Hz. O kit vem com S Pen e capa-teclado, que favorece quem pretende substituir parcialmente um notebook por um tablet.

Para quem pretende usar o tablet como computador, o Magic Keyboard adiciona trackpad e conexão inteligente, dispensando o Bluetooth. Porém, o acessório é vendido separadamente.
O iPad com chip A16 também oferece uma versão com 512 GB de armazenamento, sendo uma opção menos cara para quem prefere o ecossistema da Apple.
Assim como no iPad Air, não há leitor de microSD, embora seja possível conectar unidades externas pela porta USB-C para transferência de arquivos.
O processador A16 é suficiente para navegação, documentos, estudos, reuniões e multitarefa convencional.
O iPad tem tela Liquid Retina de 11 polegadas, resolução de 2360 x 1640 pixels e 60 Hz de taxa de atualização.
