articles.title: Clinical-Grade Home Light Therapy Devices: Wavelength Accuracy, Dual-Chip Design and Build Quality Explained - Tech Guide
articles.text:
There has been a shift in the use of red and near-infrared light therapy from professional clinics into homes. This shift has led to the design and manufacturing of more sophisticated RLT devices that incorporate multiple wavelengths, have more advanced LED designs, employ efficient optical systems, and offer more detailed performance specifications.
But what does “clinical-grade” actually mean when applied to at-home RLT devices? Since this term is not a universal technical standard, consumers need to look beyond the label and understand specifications like wavelength accuracy, irradiance, treatment dose, coverage, and electrical safety at a deeper level to find out how thoughtfully a device has been designed and engineered.
This article explains these intricacies about RLT devices to help you understand what clinical-grade means for home light therapy devices and how to evaluate these devices in terms of wavelength accuracy, dual-chip design, and build quality.
What Defines a Clinical-Grade Home Light Therapy Device?
The phrase “clinical-grade” does sound reassuring. However, from a consumer’s point of view, it can be difficult to determine what it actually represents because there is no specific requirement or feature that makes any RLT device clinical-grade.
Hence, instead of simply relying on the term clinical-grade, it is important to consider the engineering principles of the device you plan to choose to ensure you achieve the benefits you expect from your RLT sessions.
For example, a well-designed light therapy device should provide consistent and predictable exposure to red and near-infrared light. This feature comes from clearly defined wavelengths, high-quality LEDs and lenses, irradiance at a specified distance, an efficient power supply and cooling system, and robust physical construction. Checking this technical information can help you make informed choices.
In addition, electrical safety and other certifications are other important parameters to consider when choosing an RLT device.
In short, the term “clinical-grade” should be understood as one of the marks of the quality of engineering and intended performance rather than as a guarantee of clinical outcomes.
Why Wavelength Accuracy Matters in Modern Light Therapy Technology
Wavelength is one of the most important features of photobiomodulation technology. The accuracy of wavelengths can play a key role in determining the results you can achieve from your RLT sessions.
Most RLT devices use wavelengths of around 630 to 680 nm in the visible red range and approximately 810 to 850 nm in the near-infrared range. These wavelengths differ in their abilities to penetrate tissue. This is why some manufacturers combine several wavelengths in a single device to help you get benefits associated with a wider spectrum of red and infrared light.
However, not all devices available on the market produce wavelengths they claim in every circumstance. Factors like manufacturing tolerances, operating temperatures, electrical conditions, and the quality of components can influence the actual output of wavelengths. Also, small differences in wavelengths can affect how your device interacts with your biological tissue.
Therefore, it is important to choose an RLT device that supports higher-quality engineering aimed at controlling and testing LED output and is transparent about meaningful technical information. This gives you a better basis for comparison instead of relying on broad claims such as “full spectrum” or “maximum power.”
Dual-Chip LED Design: Improving Output Consistency and Device Performance
A dual-chip configuration basically contains two semiconductor chips capable of producing different wavelengths instead of one light-emitting chip per LED package. This technology allows multiple wavelengths to be incorporated into a relatively compact RLT device. This means a single LED package may be engineered to deliver both red and near-infrared wavelengths. This is expected to broaden the application of red light therapy and enhance the benefits of your sessions.
Reputed manufacturers like BestQool are using dual-chip LED technology in their red light therapy devices to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of their devices.
Beyond Wavelengths: Understanding Irradiance, Dose, and Coverage
Parameters and specifications other than wavelengths, such as irradiance and coverage, influence the efficient functioning of RLT devices.
Irradiance describes how much optical power is delivered to a specific area. It is typically expressed in mW/cm² (milliwatts per square centimeter).
Being aware of what irradiance means for your RLT session is important for choosing the right device. For example, a device may advertise a high irradiance figure. However, that number can offer meaningful results only when measurement conditions like distance and treatment dose are clearly stated.
Distance from the panel can affect the amount of light that actually reaches the area of treatment on your skin or tissue, while the treatment dose depends on the duration of exposure. So, the energy actually delivered over a session is influenced by irradiance, distance, and duration.
Also, a small, highly concentrated device may deliver substantial light to a limited coverage area. At the same time, a larger panel is likely to distribute light across a larger part of your body.
Understanding what influences the coverage area can help you choose the right at-home RLT device such that it delivers an appropriate amount of light across the intended treatment area while remaining convenient and comfortable to use.
Build Quality Features That Separate Premium Devices From Basic Models
Here are some build quality features that separate premium RLT devices from basic models:
- Thermal management: LEDs and electronic components generate a lot of heat during use. Hence, thermal management with effective ventilation, heat sinks, fans, and other cooling systems is necessary to maintain reliable performance.
- Stable power supply: A reliable power supply can ensure consistent LED operation and might enhance the durability of the device.
- Optical design: Lenses and reflectors determine the beam angle, influence light distribution, and affect how evenly light reaches the treatment area.
- User-friendly controls: Intuitive controls can make it easier for you to operate your RLT device correctly and incorporate sessions into your regular routine easily.
- Electrical safety: It is important to choose a device with features that ensure electrical safety and protection.
- Flicker performance: Devices that minimize or eliminate LED flickers are likely to improve visual comfort, particularly during repeated or longer sessions.
How Professional Light Therapy Technology Is Moving Into Consumer Devices
The growing interest among consumers in improving their health through safe, non-invasive methods has led manufacturers to design and manufacture RLT devices that are easy to use, while preserving their quality and sophisticated engineering technologies.
This transition is also changing what consumers expect from their wellness products.
However, technical sophistication should not be confused with proven clinical effectiveness. A device having advanced LEDs and impressive engineering may not always produce a particular health outcome. Hence, consumers should be aware of how to distinguish between technical engineering terms and health claims so that they can choose the best device that meets their needs and expectations.
Final Thoughts
Clinical-grade home light therapy is less about one specific feature and more about the quality of multiple specifications, including accurate wavelength delivery, thoughtful dual-chip LED configurations, appropriate irradiance, controlled dosing, effective coverage, thermal management, and durable construction.
Being aware of what these specifications actually mean and how they influence your RLT sessions and results is the key to choosing the best device suitable for your specific health goals.

articles.title: Bharat Innovates: Building the ecosystem for India’s deeptech future
articles.text:
Bharat Innovates: Building the ecosystem for India’s deeptech future
India’s deeptech ecosystem is moving from promise to global relevance, with 4,000+ startups and growing support from academia, industry, policy, and capital. Bharat Innovates 2026 highlights what the ecosystem needs next: stronger research commercialisation, industry adoption, and patient capital.
India’s deeptech journey is rapidly evolving from early promise to global relevance. Today, the country has over 4,000 active deeptech startups, driven by an enabling policy environment, stronger industry participation, world-class research institutions, a maturing capital architecture, and a new generation of entrepreneurs building IP-led technologies that strengthen resilience in critical sectors from India, for the world.
Bharat Innovates 2026 - the recent national platform accelerating deeptech entrepreneurship, anchored by the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, in partnership with 15+ higher education Institutions, key policy stakeholders including the Department of Science and Technology (DST), the Department of Biotechnology, IN-SPACe, DPIIT and NITI Aayog, MEA, and 175+ investors, industry leaders, and ecosystem stakeholders - offered a clear signal of this growing momentum.
The Core Advisory Committee, chaired by Honourable PSAI, evaluated more than 3,000 applications, ultimately selecting 120 pioneering ventures spanning energy, supply chains, mobility, advanced manufacturing, biotechnology, advanced materials, semiconductors, artificial intelligence, space, healthcare, and climate technologies.
The scientific capability and entrepreneurial ambition demonstrated by the applicants reflected a deeptech ecosystem that has matured well beyond isolated success stories, with founders building globally competitive, differentiated technologies engineered to compete globally on performance, reliability, and cost from the outset.
Bharat Innovates 2026 surfaced three critical themes that will define the continued evolution of India’s deeptech ecosystem.
Turning scientific research into scalable ventures
The first was the vital role of academia in deeptech venture creation. Bharat Innovates reaffirmed the depth of scientific capability and research-led entrepreneurship emerging from India’s academic ecosystem. This transition is propelled by a robust network of 21,400+ scientific research bodies, R&D organisations, and technical institutions - collectively anchoring a talent pool of over one crore STEM students.
Institutions like IIT Madras are increasingly demonstrating how academia can evolve beyond knowledge creation to become a catalyst for translational research and technology commercialisation. Throughout the programme, leading universities like IIT Bombay and IIT Gandhinagar played a critical role in steering the evaluation process and convening pre-summit engagements that brought together stakeholders within the deeptech ecosystem to identify opportunities, challenges and collaborative solutions.
The ventures showcased Agnikul, Ather Energy, BacAlt, Brainsight AI, IdeaForge, and Sarvam AI, each born out of academia, exemplify how scientific breakthroughs can be translated into globally competitive deeptech enterprises across advanced manufacturing, mobility, advanced materials, medtech, defence, and AI. The opportunity now is to further strengthen our research infrastructure to translate scientific discovery into venture-scale enterprises through technology transfer, translational research, founder-friendly IP frameworks, validation infrastructure, and closer collaboration between researchers, entrepreneurs, and industry.
Why industry partnerships matter for deeptech
Second, the program reinforced the critical role of industry participation in accelerating deeptech commercialisation. Across evaluations, pre-summits, and sectoral roundtables, there was strong alignment that structured co-development, paid pilots, lighthouse customers, and long-term procurement pathways provide the technical validation, operational learning, and commercial credibility gained only through real-world deployment.
Many of the ventures showcased through Bharat Innovates illustrated how early industry adoption can accelerate the journey to commercial scale.
AmpereHour Energy, now India’s largest battery energy storage systems (BESS) operator, is deploying grid-scale energy storage in partnership with leading companies like ReNew Power, IndiGrid, and Serentica Renewables.
Tsuyo is commercialising indigenous, rare-earth-free electric powertrain technologies with leading OEMs like Volvo, Mahindra, and the Sonalika Group.
Intello Labs is leveraging Physical AI to transform quality assessment across fresh produce value chains in partnership with Reliance Fresh, Adani, and others market leaders.
Ethereal Machines’ advanced manufacturing platform is supplying high-precision components to marquee aerospace clients like HAL, BEL, and Collins Aerospace.
Lohum is leading India’s lithium-ion battery recycling sector, working with global players like Mercedes-Benz Energy, MG Motor India, and Glencore.
The scale of commercial adoption is already measurable: national data reveals that 300+ large corporations are now actively investing in, acquiring, or partnering with technology startups, driving a 30% year-on-year surge in corporate-startup open innovation pathways.
Both Amperehour and Tsuyo were also selected to represent India at VivaTech 2026 - their recognition at Europe’s largest technology, innovation, and entrepreneurship platform is strong validation of India’s growing ability to build world-class deep tech solutions.
The imperative now is to deepen industry adoption of homegrown innovation, creating the commercial pathways that enable deeptech startups to scale while strengthening strategic capability across India’s critical value chains.
Deeptech needs patient, specialised capital
Finally, Bharat Innovates reflected the need for a purpose-built capital architecture aligned with the longer development cycles of scientific innovation. India’s capital stack is beginning to mature to support this shift. Landmark initiatives such as the Rs 1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme, the Anusandhan National Research Foundation, and the Rs 10,000 crore Deep Tech Fund of Funds are catalysing the long-term strategic capital architecture required to strengthen India’s deep tech innovation economy.
As more companies progress from discovery to commercialisation and manufacturing scale-up, this architecture must continue to deepen - bringing together patient public funding, venture capital, specialised debt, working capital, catalytic finance, as well as domestic and international institutional capital to support every stage of the deep tech journey.
Engaging with the exceptional winning cohort at Bharat Innovates reinforced our conviction that the next generation of Indian deeptech founders is building for international scale from day one - engineering technologies that can outperform foreign counterparts on performance, efficiency, reliability, and cost. Their ambition must be met by equally supportive institutional scaffolding built on interdisciplinary collaboration across policy, academia, industry, and capital. With world class scientific talent and a unified ecosystem, India is well positioned to lead the world in deep tech, placing growth, resilience and global technology leadership at the heart of the nation’s growth story.
(Anjali Bansal is the Founding Partner of Avaana Capital, an early-stage venture capital firm)

articles.title: L'Europe classe ChatGPT parmi ses services les plus surveillés - Numerama
articles.text:
Les Européens vont-ils, à terme, utiliser une version différente de ChatGPT ? Déjà habitué à décaler la sortie de certaines nouveautés dans l’UE, OpenAI vient d’entrer dans un club très sélect : celui des grandes entreprises dans le viseur de la Commission européenne.
Le 31 août 2026, la Commission européenne a annoncé avoir désigné ChatGPT comme « très grand moteur de recherche en ligne » (VLOSE, pour Very Large Online Search Engine) au titre du Digital Services Act (DSA), le règlement sur les services numériques entré en vigueur en 2023, à ne pas confondre avec le Digital Markets Act (DMA), qui porte sur des enjeux de concurrence. Reddit et Roblox rejoignent au passage la catégorie voisine des « très grandes plateformes en ligne » (VLOP). Les trois services ont quatre mois pour se mettre en conformité.
L’Europe considère ChatGPT comme un moteur de recherche et va le forcer à évoluer
Pour la première fois, un grand service d’IA générative entre dans le viseur du DSA en étant requalifié en tant que moteur de recherche. Le DSA fixe un seuil simple : tout service qui dépasse 45 millions d’utilisateurs actifs mensuels dans l’Union européenne, scoit environ un Européen sur dix, bascule automatiquement dans la catégorie la plus surveillée. Reste à déterminer dans quelle case le service tombe, et les chatbots IA étaient jusque-là épargnés.
Selon la Commission, ChatGPT est un « service hybride ». Puisque le chatbot peut aller chercher des informations sur le web pour répondre à une question, il remplit selon Bruxelles la définition d’un moteur de recherche au sens du DSA. Reddit et Roblox, eux, permettent à leurs utilisateurs de diffuser du contenu tiers auprès du public : ce sont donc des plateformes. Un raisonnement qui ne contentera pas tout le monde, mais la Commission a choisi cette lecture plus large.
Comme le relève Maître Alexandre Archambault sur X, l’inscription de ChatGPT en tant que grande plateforme régulée par le DSA a une autre conséquence : la Commission européenne est désormais la seule à avoir la compétence pour le réguler. La France et ses voisins viennent de perdre le droit d’exiger de bloquer ChatGPT. Avec cette désignation, la Commission obtient aussi des pouvoirs d’enquête et peut demander à OpenAI des informations confidentielles sur son service.
Quelles conséquences pour ChatGPT en Europe ?
ChatGPT va-t-il être obligé de se transformer en Europe ? Attention à ne pas confondre le DMA et le DSA : les obligations ne sont pas les mêmes. Le DMA est un texte de concurrence. Il vise les « contrôleurs d’accès » et les force à ouvrir leurs écosystèmes à des tiers : boutiques d’applications alternatives, interopérabilité des accessoires, accès aux puces NFC… C’est ce texte qui pousse Apple à retarder ou modifier certaines fonctions en Europe. C’est aussi lui qui alimente l’idée, largement répandue, d’une Europe qui dégrade l’expérience de ses utilisateurs au nom de la concurrence.
Le DSA, de son côté, ne parle pas de concurrence. Il parle de responsabilité : contenus illégaux, protection des mineurs, transparence des algorithmes, accès des chercheurs aux données. Il force les plateformes à mettre en place des mesures de modération renforcées en Europe.
Les obligations qui accompagnent le statut VLOSE sont plus lourdes que le régime général du DSA, auquel ChatGPT était déjà soumis. Sous cette nouvelle régulation, OpenAI devra :
- Évaluer chaque année les risques systémiques de son service et de ses systèmes algorithmiques : diffusion de contenus illégaux, effets sur les mineurs, atteintes au bien-être physique et mental des utilisateurs, droits fondamentaux, processus électoraux et sécurité publique.
- Mettre en place des mesures d’atténuation pour chacun de ces risques, et pas seulement les documenter.
- Se soumettre à des audits indépendants annuels, réalisés par des tiers.
- Partager des données avec les régulateurs et avec des chercheurs agréés.
- Renforcer ses obligations de transparence, notamment sur le fonctionnement de ses systèmes de recommandation.
En cas de manquement, l’amende peut atteindre 6 % du chiffre d’affaires mondial annuel. Pour une entreprise dont les revenus explosent comme ceux d’OpenAI, la note pourrait vite devenir lourde.
OpenAI a désormais quatre mois pour se mettre en conformité, soit jusqu’à la fin décembre 2026. La supervision sera assurée par la Commission européenne en coopération avec la Coimisiún na Meán, le régulateur irlandais des services numériques, puisque c’est en Irlande qu’OpenAI est établi. L’entreprise n’a pas encore réagi publiquement à la décision, mais s’opposera très certainement à son nouveau statut.

articles.title: Étudiants gamers, cette Logitech G502 HERO à moins de 30€ coche toutes les cases
articles.text:
La rentrée s'accompagne souvent d'un renouvellement de matériel informatique, et le budget alloué aux périphériques n'est pas toujours extensible. Amazon propose actuellement la souris filaire Logitech G G502 HERO à 29,99 euros au lieu de 59,99 euros, une offre que nous avons passée au crible pour vous aider à faire le bon choix.
Best-seller historique chez Logitech, la G502 HERO mise sur un capteur HERO 25K et une mémoire embarquée pour séduire aussi bien les joueurs compétitifs que les utilisateurs polyvalents. Cette version filaire s'adresse en priorité à celles et ceux qui veulent une précision constante sans se soucier d'autonomie, un argument qui prend tout son sens à l'approche de la rentrée. L'offre actuellement disponible chez Amazon permet de se procurer cette souris gamer reconnue pour moins de 30 euros, soit une remise de moitié sur son tarif habituel.
Un arbitrage intéressant pour qui doit répartir son budget entre plusieurs achats de rentrée, sans sacrifier la qualité d'un périphérique du quotidien. Entre un ordinateur portable, des manuels ou un abonnement logiciel, chaque euro économisé sur les accessoires compte, et une souris capable de tenir plusieurs années reste un investissement raisonnable.
Voici la Logitech G G502 HERO à 29,99 € au lieu de 59,99 € chez Amazon !
Pourquoi choisir le Logitech G G502 HERO ?
- Un prix nettement revu à la baisse : la souris passe de 59,99 € à 29,99 € chez Amazon, soit une remise de 50 %.
- Un capteur taillé pour la précision : le capteur HERO 25K grimpe jusqu'à 25 600 PPP, pour un suivi fidèle en jeu comme en usage bureautique exigeant.
- Une personnalisation poussée : 11 boutons programmables et un poids ajustable permettent d'adapter la souris à sa main et à ses usages.
Une souris pensée pour durer entre jeu et bureautique
Avec ses 11 boutons programmables et sa molette à double mode, la G502 HERO s'adapte aussi bien aux sessions de jeu qu'à un usage quotidien plus posé, un point que la rédaction Clubic a pu vérifier lors du test de la gamme, où le modèle avait obtenu une note de 8/10. Le poids ajustable, via cinq masses de 3,6 grammes, permet de retrouver la prise en main qui convient le mieux, un détail apprécié par les joueurs habitués à personnaliser leur matériel. Le format filaire, souvent perçu comme une contrainte, s'avère ici un gage de fiabilité : pas de batterie à surveiller ni de latence à redouter. Pour un étudiant ou un télétravailleur qui alterne jeu et productivité sur un même poste, cette polyvalence pèse dans la balance.
Face aux souris sans fil récentes, où se situe la G502 HERO ?
Comparée aux modèles sans fil apparus ces dernières années, la G502 HERO ne propose ni connectivité multi appareils ni format ultra léger, des caractéristiques désormais courantes sur le haut de gamme, y compris chez Logitech avec sa déclinaison LIGHTSPEED. Elle conserve en revanche l'avantage d'un tarif nettement plus accessible et d'une fiabilité éprouvée, ce qui en fait un choix pertinent pour qui privilégie le rapport prix performance à la nouveauté plutôt que les dernières innovations sans fil.
✅ Les points forts
- Capteur HERO 25K précis, y compris pour un usage bureautique exigeant
- 11 boutons programmables pour une personnalisation poussée
- Poids ajustable grâce aux cinq masses fournies
- Connexion filaire fiable, sans contrainte de charge
- Prix particulièrement accessible pendant la durée de l'offre
❌ Les limites
- Pas de connectivité sans fil ni multi appareils
- Design pensé pour les droitiers uniquement
- Mécanisme cranté de la molette parfois jugé bruyant à l'usage
- Gabarit moins compact que certains modèles ultra légers récents
La Logitech G G502 HERO à 29,99 € chez Amazon : vérifiez la disponibilité avant la fin de l'offre
Cette Logitech G G502 HERO à 29,99 euros s'adresse avant tout à celles et ceux qui cherchent une souris gamer fiable et polyvalente sans faire exploser leur budget de rentrée, en particulier les joueurs sur PC fixe peu gênés par le format filaire. Les habitués des configurations mobiles ou multi écrans, en quête de connectivité sans fil et de légèreté extrême, trouveront sans doute leur bonheur ailleurs dans le catalogue Logitech.
Pour un usage mixte entre jeu et bureautique, avec un capteur précis et une personnalisation complète, l'offre mérite clairement le coup d'œil avant la fin de la remise chez Amazon. À vous de voir si elle correspond à votre setup et à vos priorités de rentrée.

articles.title: Cinéma sans reflets le jour, gaming à 165 Hz le soir : cette TV OLED Samsung 55" nouvelle génération en promo à -500 € séduit — Frandroid
articles.text:
Les TV Samsung S95H, aux côtés des S99H, S90H et S85H, ont été dévoilées lors de l’évènement First Look du CES 2026 à Las Vegas. Elles sont toutes disponibles depuis le début de l’été 2026 avec comme promesse principale une avancée sur le traitement anti-reflet. Ce qui permet de se poser devant tranquillement en pleine journée ensoleillée et d’en profiter sans être gêné. Sans oublier la fréquence de rafraîchissement élevée qui en fait un téléviseur tout indiqué pour le gaming, avec la qualité de l’OLED en plus. Le site Cobra se permet en plus une réduction conséquente de 500 euros, soit près de 24 % sous le prix conseillé.
Les atouts du Samsung TQ55S95H
- Le nouveau filtre anti-reflet Glare Free efficace dans les pièces lumineuses
- La luminosité HDR élevée avec la qualité de l’OLED
- Le taux de rafraîchissement à 165 Hz avec faible input lag
Le prix fort du Samsung TQ55S95H est de 2 090 euros, mais si vous allez sur le site de Cobra en ce moment, il est en promotion à 1 590 euros.
Un TV OLED récent qui corrige un point important
Ce téléviseur Samsung S95H adopte le nouveau design FloatLayer de la marque, à savoir un cadre métallique qui entoure l’écran sur tout le pourtour, donnant l’impression que l’image flotte devant le cadre. Un choix qui tranche avec le design ultra-fin et presque sans cadre du S95F. On retrouve avec plaisir le boîtier One Connect qui permet de n’avoir qu’un seul fil qui part du téléviseur. Comme ça, vous pouvez l’installer sur un mur, par exemple, et profiter de ses options Art pour afficher un tableau connu lorsqu’il est en veille.
La grosse mise à jour vient de l’écran, une dalle QD-OLED Penta Tandem, ici de 55 pouces, qui permet un gain de luminosité d’environ 30 % par rapport au S95F, le modèle précédent. Avec surtout le fameux traitement anti-reflet « Glare Free », une couche mate supplémentaire pour les pièces lumineuses. C’est un vrai plus si votre TV est posé face à une fenêtre ou tape le soleil. Mais ça permet de regarder des films sans être gêné en pleine journée quand il fait beau.
Samsung brosse les gamers dans le sens du poil
Le Samsung S95H supporte le HDR10, HLG, HDR10+ et même le HDR10+ Advanced, mais pas de Dolby Vision. Pour les puristes, c’est un point négatif face à des concurrents comme les LG C6 ou LG G6, ou encore le Sony Bravia 8 II. Si vous souhaitez jouer sur votre téléviseur, vous avez de quoi faire, avec les 4 ports HDMI 2.1 à 48 Gbps, tous compatibles 4K jusqu’à 165 Hz, avec VRR, ALLM, G-Sync et FreeSync Premium Pro. Vous profitez du Gaming Hub avec cloud intégré et il y a une Game Bar qui permet d’afficher les FPS et les réglages en jeu.
Le S95H tourne sous Tizen 2026, avec interface One UI. Pour ça, il utilise un processeur NQ4 AI Gen 3 et des fonctions IA notamment pour l’upscaling, cette fonction qui permet d’améliorer la qualité d’images qui sont nativement inférieures à de la 4K. Vous pouvez même intégrer un assistant IA comme le Copilot de Microsoft ou Perplexity, pour des réponses plus avancées. Enfin, pour l’audio, vous avez un système 4.2.2 avec Dolby Atmos, Q-Symphony pour ajouter une barre de son de la marque et même le support du format Eclipsa Audio sur YouTube.
Vous pouvez aussi retrouver notre guide sur les meilleurs TV OLED du moment si vous souhaitez comparer les performances de ce modèle Samsung avec d’autres marques.

articles.title: 👨🏿🚀TechCabal Daily – Paystack cuts the Allawee | TechCabal
articles.text:
Happy new month. ☀️️

Let’s dive in.

M&A
South Africa’s Nedbank gets CBK’s approval to acquire 66% of Kenyan lender NCBA
Remember the proposed acquisition of Kenyan digital-first bank NCBA by South African tier-1 lender Nedbank that has hogged headlines since the start of the year?
We’ve got a big development in that saga. On Monday, the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) said it had approved Nedbank’s acquisition of up to 66% of NCBA on August 28, clearing a major regulatory hurdle for the South African lender. The approval follows months of regulatory reviews and a shareholder offer that saw NCBA investors accept Nedbank’s proposal in exchange for cash and Nedbank shares.
State of play: The deal isn’t fully closed yet, but once completed, Nedbank will take control of NCBA, giving the South African lender a major foothold in East Africa. Nedbank will become NCBA’s majority owner, while the remaining 34% will stay in public hands. The Kenyan digital-first bank will also retain its brand, local management, and Nairobi headquarters.
Explain like I’m new here: In January, Nedbank announced that it wanted to acquire about two-thirds of NCBA through a tender offer, asking existing NCBA shareholders to offer up their shares for sale. Under the proposed deal, shareholders would receive 20% cash and 80% newly issued Nedbank shares. The offer opened in May and closed on July 10, with NCBA shareholders offering 1.32 billion shares, equivalent to 79.9% of NCBA.
However, shareholders offered more shares than Nedbank’s 66% target, so the bank had to scale back the allocation to 1.09 billion shares, leaving some shareholders unable to sell their shares to Nedbank.
Why does Nedbank want NCBA? NCBA gives Nedbank an established presence across East Africa. It has banking subsidiaries in Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania and Rwanda, plus a joint venture in Côte d’Ivoire. NCBA reported KES 12.4 billion ($95.7 million) in profit after tax in H1 2026, while its total assets reached KES 739 billion ($5.7 billion).
Nedbank also sees the acquisition as a way to get closer to other East African and nearby markets it is eyeing, including the Democratic Republic of Congo and Ethiopia.
Is this the end of the road? Not yet. CBK’s approval clears a major hurdle, but the deal still has a few other regulatory, banking, and market conduct conditions to meet before it can be completed. Nedbank previously said it expects the deal to finalise by the fourth quarter of 2026.

Fintech
Nigerian fintech Allawee folds into Paystack after 2025 acquisition
Customers of Nigerian card-issuing fintech Allawee have until November 30 to move their money, replace their cards, and tell anyone who pays them that their account details are changing, the startup wrote in an email. Allawee has since been folded into Paystack’s operations.
What happened? Paystack, the Stripe-backed payments company, acquired Allawee in a 2025 deal that was not publicly announced. Allawee will close its personal and business account services on December 1, 2026; its cards will stop working, and payments sent to its virtual account numbers issued on its platform will fail. Customers will need to withdraw their balances, update their bank details with senders, and replace saved card details on subscriptions before the deadline.
Businesses are being directed to Paystack MFB, its parent company’s microfinance bank, while individuals are being directed to Zap, Paystack’s consumer transfer app. Balances, account numbers, transaction history, and verification records will not move across automatically, so customers opening new accounts will start again.
Explain like I’m new here: Allawee launched in 2022 as a credit-card lender; it later pivoted to credit-risk software before settling on card infrastructure, enabling other fintechs to issue and manage cards.
By May 2025, it was providing services to Nigerian fintechs such as PiggyVest, Nomba, and Carbon, letting them launch cards in weeks instead of months. That infrastructure is likely more valuable to Paystack than Allawee’s consumer accounts. Once Paystack had its own microfinance bank, Allawee’s Providus Bank-backed accounts were competing with products Paystack could offer itself. Acquiring Allawee lets Paystack take the useful infrastructure while moving customers onto the banking products it now controls.
Zoom out: Allawee is the second fintech brand Paystack has folded into its operations this year, after absorbing Nigerian business-banking startup Brass in June. Nigeria’s fintech market seems to be moving from “build everything” to “buy the missing pieces.” For customers, that can mean better-connected products, but also the inconvenience of being moved between companies, setups, and platforms whenever these changes happen.

Fintech
Yele Bademosi transitions to Chairman at Nigerian fintech Onboard Global
Yele Bademosi is transitioning from chief executive officer to the chairman’s seat at Onboard Global, the Nigerian stablecoin-based fintech startup that launched in 2022.
Onboard lets users spend stablecoins like everyday money, using cards and stablecoin-to-fiat payment accounts. The fintech spun out of Nestcoin, a Web3 banking platform Bademosi co-founded in 2021.
Between the lines: On Monday, Bademosi announced that he was stepping down as Onboard’s chief executive officer and taking up a new role as chairman. Paul Oladimeji, who has worked on Onboard’s products and infrastructure, will take over the day-to-day running of the company. The leadership transition and Oladimeji’s background point to a handover from founder-led direction to product-led execution.
State of play: Bademosi co-founded Onboard when stablecoins and cryptocurrency wallets were still the centre of the company’s pitch. The business is now trying to build something broader: financial infrastructure that connects local currencies, dollars, and stablecoins for individuals and businesses.
Zoom out: Onboard is entering a more demanding phase of its growth. Moving from a consumer wallet into payments, business accounts, and financial infrastructure means competing for customers while navigating the licencing and compliance requirements that come with moving real money across borders. Bademosi’s move gives the company a chance to put a new operator at the helm as it makes that transition.

Moonshot 2026 is coming! Join us at the National Theatre, Lagos on October 28 & 29 for two days of tech and innovation. Grab your early bird tickets now and get 15% off.
Digital Infrastructure
Namibia launches DigiNam to let citizens prove their identity and sign documents online
Having to enter your name, submit an ID, and fill out the same forms every time you access a government service is a real pain. It gets worse when you make the trip to an office only to realise you left one crucial document at home.
It’s one of the reasons blockchain bros have been clamouring for decentralised identity (DID), which allows you to prove who you are once and use that identity across different services without carrying files or memorising your ID number.
Well, it’s not quite DID, but Namibia wants to make some of that hassle disappear.
What happened? On Monday, Namibia launched DigiNam, a national digital trust system that will let people prove their identity and sign online. The system is built around the country’s National Public Key Infrastructure (NPKI), the technology and rules that help verify digital identities and electronic signatures. Namibia’s Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety, and Security; the Ministry of Information and Communication Technology (ICT); and the Communications Regulatory Authority of Namibia (CRAN), the country’s telecoms regulator, are behind the rollout.
Explain like I’m new here: Think of DigiNam as a verified identity for the Internet. Once electronic IDs are issued through the system, they can carry digital credentials that let a government agency verify that you are really you when you use an online service. The system can confirm that an electronic signature belongs to the person who signed a document and that the document has not been changed afterwards.
Why did Namibia bother? Today, accessing many services can mean proving who you are over and over again. Namibia wants authorised government agencies to securely cross-check information, so citizens do not have to keep submitting the same documents or visiting offices in person.
However, moving more services online also creates a trust problem. In H1 2025, 65% of Namibians reported being targeted online, by email, phone call, or text messaging fraud, according to TransUnion Africa, a risk management agency. Between April and June 2026, the country also recorded over 500,000 cyber vulnerabilities.
What happens next? CRAN will oversee the trust system as the “Root Certification Authority,” setting standards and approving organisations that can issue trusted digital credentials. The Ministry of Home Affairs will be the first to roll out those credentials. Namibia plans to eventually connect more government services and extend the system to sectors such as financial services and telecoms.

articles.title: ICE seeks to purchase up to $2 million in Boston Dynamics Spot robots
articles.text:
A hot potato: Spot, the robotic quadruped from Boston Dynamics, has been used in numerous professions over the years, but its most controversial application could be on the way. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is set to spend $2 million on the robot dogs, which could support officers by remotely assessing environments before they enter.
A new Department of Homeland Security procurement notice describes the possible purchase of Boston Dynamics SPOT robots and accessories valued at between $1 million and $2 million.
The document lists the robots' potential uses as inspection, situational awareness, and hazard assessment in environments that may pose risks to personnel.
It adds that these capabilities helps improve officer safety, supports informed operational decision-making, and enhances DHS's ability to respond to incidents involving dangerous, confined, unstable, or difficult-to-access areas.
Also read: Hyundai wants to sell humanoid and robot dogs through its car dealerships
There's no mention of the robots being used to apprehend people or make arrests, which was later confirmed by a senior DHS official speaking to NBC News, though that's unlikely to make their use by ICE any less controversial.
This won't be the first time Spot has been used by a government agency. In 2019, the Massachusetts State Police bomb squad leased one of the robots for use as a "mobile remote observation device." It was sent to inspect suspicious objects and dangerous locations, taking part in at least two incidents.
The NYPD later deployed a heavily modified Spot known as Digidog. The robot was used for reconnaissance during a 2020 incident in which a gunman barricaded himself inside a basement, and again the following year to investigate a house during a reported home invasion before officers entered.
Digidog reportedly completed around six missions without harming civilians, but footage of the robot in action prompted a backlash over surveillance and the increasingly Black Mirror-like appearance of modern policing. The NYPD terminated its $94,000 lease in 2021, only to bring Digidog back two years later. The department acquired two of the robots for $750,000, saying they would only be deployed in life-threatening situations such as bomb threats.
Spot also has a history with the US military. An early version was tested by the Marines as a potential load-carrying and ground-reconnaissance platform. While it was much quieter than Boston Dynamics' gas-powered AlphaDog, Spot had to be monitored continuously and could carry only around 40 pounds of equipment. Those limitations meant the military ultimately shelved the project.
Boston Dynamics prohibits customers from using Spot to harm or intimidate people, warning that it will take "appropriate measures to mitigate that misuse." Even if it believes this doesn't apply to ICE, the company will have to decide whether up to $2 million in sales will be worth the bad publicity.

articles.title: A “quantum bath” puts quantum entanglement on autopilot
articles.text:
A “quantum bath” puts quantum entanglement on autopilot
A 20-year-old quantum prediction has finally been demonstrated, using a bath of correlated light to automatically entangle distant qubits.
- Date:
- August 31, 2026
- Source:
- Institute of Science and Technology Austria
- Summary:
- Physicists have demonstrated a new way to entangle distant quantum bits without the constant measurements and active control normally required. The team created a “quantum bath,” a shared environment filled with correlated microwave photons that automatically pushes separated qubits into an entangled state and helps keep them there. The experiment confirms a theoretical prediction made more than 20 years ago and could offer a simpler way to connect modules in future quantum computers.
- Share:
Future quantum computers may depend on the ability to connect widely separated modules through distributed entanglement. Until now, creating this kind of connection has generally required active control and repeated measurements. Physicists at the Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA) have now demonstrated a fully autonomous alternative based on a "quantum bath" made from correlated particles of light.
Published in Physical Review X, the experiment provides the first demonstration of a prediction proposed more than 20 years ago. The approach could eventually offer a new foundation for practical quantum technologies.
Connecting Distant Quantum Bits
Entanglement is one of the defining phenomena of quantum physics. It allows particles or systems to share correlations that cannot be explained by classical physics. Creating distributed entanglement between physically separated qubits (quantum bits) could be important for building larger quantum computers and future quantum networks.
Previous attempts to entangle distant qubits have generally followed one of two strategies. One method sends a single, actively controlled photon from one qubit to another. Another has each qubit emit a photon, with the two photons then matched in an effort to generate entanglement.
The second approach was recognized by the 2022 Nobel Prize in Physics. However, it still depends on repeated measurements and post-selection, and even then, the process does not always successfully produce entanglement.
PhD student Alejandro Andrés-Juanes and professor Johannes Fink at the Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA) worked with international collaborators to develop a different solution. Their system uses a quantum bath that automatically brings distant qubits into synchronization. In a prototype device, the researchers used a shared source of correlated light particles to entangle two separated qubits, experimentally realizing an idea that had remained theoretical for more than two decades.
Fully Autonomous Quantum Entanglement
Quantum entanglement can take several forms. Continuous-variable entangled states can be produced efficiently and are therefore relatively accessible. They can be compared with a pendulum, whose position and momentum change continuously.
Many useful quantum technologies, however, depend on "discrete-variable" systems. These involve 'all-or-nothing' forms of entanglement that stationary qubits can use. The challenge for the ISTA team was finding a way to connect these readily available continuous forms of entanglement with the discrete forms needed for practical applications.
"In this work, we aimed to overcome this mismatch between the readily available and the practically useful forms of entanglement," says Andrés-Juanes. "By stabilizing the entangled states remotely, our approach is fully autonomous and requires no active control or measurement."
A Quantum Bath Powered by Correlated Light
Maintaining both entanglement and quantum coherence is one of the major difficulties facing quantum computing.
The researchers addressed that problem by making the qubits' surrounding environment itself responsible for producing and stabilizing entanglement.
"In our method, the quantum bath -- meaning the qubits' environment -- is the source of entanglement. It creates a new ground state through a continuous stream of correlated photons," says Fink. "This way, the entangled qubit state is stabilized, even beyond the qubits' own 'lifetime', and remains always available as a resource for further quantum processing. This makes the approach conceptually significant."
Because the entangled state remains available, researchers can access it whenever it is needed. That differs from temporary entanglement, which has to be used during the brief period when it exists.
Microwave Photons Keep Qubits Connected
To couple the qubits with the entangled photon source, the researchers relied on microwave photons. These low-energy light particles are especially useful for manipulating quantum information and are already central to leading superconducting-qubit technology.
Optical photons serve a different role and are commonly used in optics and atomic physics. They may also become important for carrying quantum information between distant quantum computers through fiber optics, an area that the Fink group at ISTA is also investigating.
Measuring the Hidden Quantum State
The researchers needed to confirm that the two qubits were actually synchronized inside the quantum bath. To do that, they used quantum tomography, a technique that reconstructs a quantum system by examining many different 'slices' of its behavior.
"Qubits can be in a superposition of states, but all these states collapse when we measure them, leaving us with a 0 or 1 state," says Andrés-Juanes.
Quantum tomography allowed the researchers to perform measurements lasting only 20-80 nanoseconds and use those observations to investigate the qubits' underlying states. A nanosecond is one billionth of a second.
A 20-Year Prediction Becomes an Experiment
By successfully entangling two isolated qubits through a quantum bath, the ISTA researchers created a proof-of-concept laboratory prototype for the long-standing theoretical proposal.
"We present a relatively simple method that could be scaled up to synchronize multiple distant qubits," says Andrés-Juanes.
The new approach is promising, but it is not yet as efficient as methods that actively control qubit states. "Our method currently transfers about 10% of the bath's available entanglement."
The researchers suggest that one reason the idea took more than two decades to demonstrate is that the original theory was developed under idealized conditions that are difficult to reproduce experimentally.
"Our experiments helped us reveal several factors that may have prevented scientists from designing a functional quantum bath using a single source of correlated photons for distributed entanglement," says Fink.
The prototype developed at ISTA could provide new opportunities for quantum-optics experiments. It may also contribute to efforts to expand quantum processors and ultimately move them closer to fault-tolerant operation.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Institute of Science and Technology Austria. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- A. Andrés-Juanes, J. Agustí, R. Sett, E. S. Redchenko, L. N. Kapoor, S. Hawaldar, P. Rabl, J. M. Fink. Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement through a Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir. Physical Review X, 2026; 16 (3) DOI: 10.1103/r4jt-j39w
