The 8GB card hasn't received nearly as much attention recently as the 16GB model, because the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB is now sitting above $700, almost the MSRP of an RTX 5070 Ti. That's insane.
This model is up 22% compared with last month, which is already a very significant increase, but it's also 27% more expensive than in February. That's particularly shocking given that the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB wasn't even an MSRP-priced card in some regions back then.
Pricing for this model has continued to rise throughout 2026. In the US, it's now 70% above MSRP. Globally, it's the second most overpriced card behind the RTX 5090, sitting an average of 53% above its $430 MSRP after accounting for local currency conversions.

The 8GB version, meanwhile, is just 14% above MSRP across the 10 regions we're examining. That illustrates the enormous discrepancy between the unpopular 8GB card and the much more desirable 16GB version.
Right now, you have to spend roughly 50% more to get 16GB of VRAM instead of 8GB at this tier, and in some regions the premium reaches 62%. That's the reality of current memory pricing.
RTX 5070 Pricing Is Bad, but the Ti Is Worse
GeForce RTX 5070 + RTX 5070 Ti
Next we have the RTX 5070. This model has risen by 20% on average over the past month and now costs 19% more than it did in February. The RTX 5070 is currently sitting 31% above its global MSRP. That's not as bad as the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB, but it's still pretty bad, and these increases have significantly narrowed the gap between the two cards.

At MSRP, the RTX 5070 should cost 28% more than the RTX 5060 Ti 16GB, a difference of $120. Right now, that gap has shrunk to just 10% worldwide because both models have become more expensive, but the 5060 Ti has risen by more. In the US, the raw price gap has fallen from $120 to just $70, likely a byproduct of the RTX 5070 having a lower 12GB VRAM capacity.
The RTX 5070 Ti is an interesting one. This model is up 17% month over month and is 14% more expensive than it was in February, but many of its price increases were heavily front-loaded.

In other words, the card became dramatically more expensive at the beginning of the year and has been treading water to some degree since then. So while pricing is "only" up 17% since July, a smaller increase than we're seeing for many other models, the RTX 5070 Ti is still 44% above MSRP on average. That makes it the third most overpriced GPU on the market.
High-End GeForce Pricing Goes From Bad to Absurd
GeForce RTX 5080 + RTX 5090
The RTX 5080 tells a similar story to the RTX 5070 Ti. Prices are up 15% on average compared with July, with the US getting stung especially hard. The 24% increase there is roughly double what we're seeing in European markets such as Germany and Poland.

Surprisingly, the RTX 5080 is only 8% more expensive than it was in February. This is another model where prices fell slightly during the first half of the year after rising sharply earlier on. Even so, the RTX 5080 is currently sitting 38% above MSRP on average. In the US, it's 55% above MSRP, which is a significant outlier.
Then there's the RTX 5090, which just keeps getting more ridiculous. Prices increased another 20% over the past month and are now 41% higher than in February, by far the largest six-month increase of any card we're tracking. At nearly $5,000 in the US, the RTX 5090 is 145% above MSRP there and 136% above MSRP across the 10 regions we're examining.

At this point, it's difficult to consider the RTX 5090 a gaming card. This is workstation-level pricing, and the card continues to command such ridiculous prices largely because of its AI performance and 32GB of memory.
Radeon Prices Are Rising Too, Just Not as Quickly
Radeon RX 9060 XT: 8GB + 16GB
For a slight change of pace, let's move over to Radeon, starting with the RX 9060 XT series. The 8GB model is actually the Radeon card that has been hit hardest between August and July. While this GPU saw no price increase in the US, it rose by 16% on average across the 10 regions, with particularly large increases in India, Poland, the Netherlands, and the UK.
It's now 20% more expensive than it was in February and sits 26% above its global MSRP on average.

That sounds relatively good because it's only a single-digit increase, and the card is also just 11% more expensive than it was in February.

However, the overall price is now 28% above MSRP, making it the most overpriced Radeon model relative to where it should sit in a normal market. That's a similar level of overall inflation to the RX 9060 XT 8GB, but it has occurred at different times. The 8GB model has risen more sharply recently, while the 16GB card has gradually crept upward throughout the memory crisis.
That's probably because the 16GB card is far more desirable, so stock sitting on store shelves is constantly being replaced with more expensive inventory.
The RX 9070 Series Is Holding Up Surprisingly Well
Radeon RX 9070 + RX 9070 XT
The RX 9070 has been one of the most resilient cards on the market, with relatively small price increases in several regions. On average, pricing is up 8%, largely because of significant increases in India, Brazil, and Poland. Here in Australia, for example, it's only around 5% more expensive.
The RX 9070 is also just 5% more expensive than it was in February, the smallest six-month increase of any model we're tracking, and it currently sits only 13% above MSRP.

This is supposed to be a $550 GPU and it has 16GB of VRAM, making it just as susceptible to memory pricing pressures as other 16GB cards. Given those conditions, we'd say the RX 9070 currently has one of the best prices on the market at a little over $600.
The RX 9070 XT is holding up reasonably well, too. Pricing has risen by 12% across the 10 regions, with Australia and Brazil getting hit the hardest, but we're still looking at a card that's only 8% more expensive than it was in February. The Australian price, for example, is more of a correction back toward previous levels. The RX 9070 XT was unusually cheap there in July compared with other regions.

Unfortunately, the RX 9070 XT is now 21% above MSRP and 16% more expensive than the RX 9070. We recently found the 9070 XT to be about 12% faster than the 9070 across a 52-game sample, so that currently makes the RX 9070 slightly better value.
That calculation does vary by region. In the Philippines, for example, the XT model makes more sense because the price gap is smaller.
Intel Battlemage Supply Keeps Getting Worse
Intel Arc B570 + B580
Lastly, we have Intel's Arc GPUs. The B570 is becoming increasingly difficult to find and doesn't appear to be in particularly good supply. Even in regions where we could find pricing, there were often only one or two listings available.
Pricing is up around 12% compared with July and 22% compared with February, although the B570 remains one of the cheapest GPUs you can buy. It's even cheaper than AMD's new RX 9050, which is diabolically bad.

Intel Arc B580

| Feb 2026 | $300 | $420 | 300 € | £270 | $360 | ₹31,000 | ₱20,000 | R$1,700 | 1,200 zł | €290 | 
| Jul 2026 | $310 | $390 | 270 € | £320 | $450 |  |  | R$2,000 | 1,300 zł | €290 |

The Arc B580 is in better supply, though availability still isn't great compared with GeForce or Radeon. This model has risen by 7% on average since July and 14% since February, and it now sits 25% above MSRP.
In the US, for example, it's priced similarly to the RTX 5050 while remaining comfortably below the RTX 5060. So even after these increases, the B580 remains competitive at the lower end of the market.
GPU Prices Jumped 15% in a Single Month
As expected, the current state of GPU pricing isn't pretty. After prices remained stagnant or slightly improved over the months leading into July, we've now seen a sudden and sharp increase across the market. If you didn't pick up the graphics card you wanted in June, for example, you're now getting absolutely rolled, and there's no indication that prices will return to those levels anytime soon.
Looking across every graphics card model in all 10 regions, we recorded a 15% average price increase compared with this time last month. That's the simplest number for quantifying just how quickly things have deteriorated. But it doesn't tell the full story, because these increases haven't been distributed evenly across every model or manufacturer.
| GPU | MSRP | Current US Price | % Increase MSRP vs Retail | Approx. Global Increase vs MSRP | 
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RTX 5050 | $249 | $300 | 20% | n/a | 
| RTX 5060 | $299 | $450 | 51% | n/a | 
| RTX 5060 Ti 8GB | $379 | $500 | 32% | 14% | 
| RTX 5060 Ti 16GB | $429 | $730 | 70% | 53% | 
| RTX 5070 | $549 | $800 | 46% | 31% | 
| RTX 5070 Ti | $749 | $1,050 | 40% | 44% | 
| RTX 5080 | $999 | $1,550 | 55% | 38% | 
| RTX 5090 | $1,999 | $4,900 | 145% | 136% | 
| RX 9060 XT 8GB | $299 | $360 | 20% | 26% | 
| RX 9060 XT 16GB | $349 | $460 | 32% | 28% | 
| RX 9070 | $549 | $630 | 15% | 13% | 
| RX 9070 XT | $599 | $750 | 25% | 21% | 
| Arc B570 | $219 | $260 | 19% | n/a | 
| Arc B580 | $249 | $310 | 25% | 25% | 
Some GPU models are now 40 to 50% more expensive than they should be, which is just bloody fantastic.
GeForce GPUs have risen by 19% month over month, while Radeon GPUs are up by 11%, excluding the recently released RX 9070 GRE. That's broadly in line with what we heard would happen at the end of July, when much larger increases were expected for Nvidia cards than AMD models.
Unlike in previous GPU pricing updates, the impact across the GeForce lineup has actually been quite similar from one model to another. Previously, we saw much larger increases for 16GB GPUs compared with 8GB models. Between July and August, however, most GeForce cards simply rose by around 20%. In fact, some of the largest percentage increases have affected 8GB cards, which had previously been more resistant to rising prices.
There are a couple of ways to frame all this, depending on how positive you want to be. The positive interpretation is that GPU prices are "only" 17% higher on average than they were in February, and in some cases the latest round of increases has simply returned cards to pricing levels seen earlier in the year.
The negative interpretation is that the overall GPU market is now priced 28% above launch MSRP on average, excluding the ridiculously overpriced RTX 5090, which isn't really a gaming GPU anymore. Some models are now 40 to 50% more expensive than they should be, which is just bloody fantastic.
Memory Pricing Is Now Written All Over GeForce Prices
How Much Are Nvidia GPUs Above MSRP?
If we focus on actual dollar increases in the US market, much of the GeForce lineup has risen by an amount that broadly tracks the VRAM capacity of each card.
The RTX 5070 Ti and RTX 5060 Ti 16GB are now around $300 more expensive than at launch. The RTX 5070, with 12GB of VRAM, is up $250, while the RTX 5060 and RTX 5060 Ti 8GB are roughly $120 to $150 more expensive. It's not a perfect explanation, of course. The RTX 5080 has the same 16GB of VRAM as the RTX 5070 Ti yet is now $550 above MSRP. Still, it certainly appears that Nvidia pricing is being heavily affected by increased memory costs.
A while ago, we published an article modelling what rising GDDR7 prices could do to graphics card pricing. We estimated that if memory became three times more expensive, 16GB Nvidia GPUs would become at least $250 more expensive, while 12GB models would rise by roughly $200.
We're very much living in that reality now.
Radeon Has Escaped the Worst of It, for Now
AMD GPUs haven't been affected nearly as badly, although its 16GB Radeon models are still around $100 to $150 more expensive than MSRP. There are a couple of reasons AMD's offerings have been more resistant to memory-related price increases. AMD uses GDDR6 instead of GDDR7, and its margins are different from Nvidia's. Ultimately, though, Radeon cards are still facing many of the same pricing pressures.
We suspect Radeon GPUs will become more expensive throughout the remainder of 2026, especially if you look at what's happening on the console side. The PlayStation 5, for example, is a lower-margin product than a discrete Radeon GPU and has increased in price by $150 since the middle of 2025. Of course, the PS5 also contains NAND flash, which has become significantly more expensive, but a decent portion of that increase is likely tied to its 16GB of GDDR6 becoming more costly as well.
Right now, though, the difference between GeForce and Radeon price increases has created some very interesting matchups. The RTX 5060 should be directly competing with the RX 9060 XT 8GB, but it's currently priced at roughly the same level as the RX 9060 XT 16GB. The RTX 5060 Ti 16GB and RTX 5070 are both sitting around the same price as the RX 9070 XT, which is pretty crazy considering the performance difference between those cards.
And across the 10 regions we're examining, the RTX 5070 Ti is now 50% more expensive than the RX 9070 XT. That makes it extremely difficult to recommend a GeForce GPU right now. Radeon cards are simply much better value. That value gap may not last, given the rumors of incoming Radeon price increases, but at the moment it just doesn't make much sense to buy most of Nvidia's lineup.
You could argue that it doesn't make sense to buy any GPU right now, and that's fair.
But if you're going to buy one anyway, Radeon is clearly the way to go.

articles.title: Boston Scientific Still Recovering From Cyberattack
articles.text:
Nearly one week after being hit by a highly disruptive cyberattack, US medical technology giant Boston Scientific is still recovering and working on resuming operations.
Boston Scientific detected an intrusion into some of its IT systems on August 25 and disclosed the incident the next day.
The cyberattack led to a network outage that disrupted global operations, including product manufacturing, customer order processing, and shipping.
Boston Scientific develops and manufactures devices and therapies used in cardiology, neurology, and oncology.
The company said the hacker attack did not affect existing implantable cardiac rhythm management (CRM) devices, but it did disrupt new remote activations for some cardiac monitors.
CrowdStrike and other cybersecurity experts have been called in to assist with the investigation.
In updates shared over the weekend, Boston Scientific said it found no signs of malicious activity on its networks since August 25, and the breach appears to be limited to some on-premises systems.
The company hopes to resume shipping some products at least partially this week, but it could not provide a full restoration timeline.
It’s still unclear who is behind the attack. No known cybercrime group appears to have taken credit for the breach.

articles.title: London's HITAI acquires YC-backed fitness gaming studio Quell to boost its sports motion-tracking platform | EU-Startups
articles.text:
HITAI, a London-based movement intelligence platform for sports, has acquired the technology and IP of Quell, a UK-based fitness gaming developer and publisher behind the ‘Impact’ fitness gaming platform and Shardfall, its flagship high-intensity combat game.
The acquisition will enhance HITAI’s camera-based motion recognition platform via Quell’s camera-less, patent-pending tech, built to run in real time on compact, low‑power devices. The deal includes motion‑recognition models, the firmware and hardware stack for Quell’s Impact console, and its Shardfall combat game.
“This acquisition brings years of cutting-edge engineering in the field of human movement recognition into the HITAI fold, with the backing of a team that knows how to ship. Quell’s technology allows us to build upon our video-first core to deliver exceptional products in a wide range of new spaces,” said Ismail Baran, founder and CEO of HITAI.
HITAI claims to be building the movement-intelligence infrastructure for sports video. Its platform uses computer vision and machine learning to convert existing training, event and broadcast footage into structured movement and performance data, without wearables, sensors, or specialised camera systems.
The company states that it is commercialising its platform first in combat sports before expanding into selected additional sports. Its technology can support coaching, athlete analysis, live-event statistics, broadcasting, automated content and sports-data services.
Founded in 2020 by Lorenzo Spreafico, Cameron Brookhouse, Martin Tweedie and Douglas Stidolph, Quell is a fitness gaming developer and publisher. The company states that its lightweight motion and fitness-tracking technology is combined with athlete-grade resistance bands to deliver real-world feedback, resistance and tracking to player action, claiming to burn over 600kcal an hour on average.
In 2023, the company announced the completion of an €8.63 million ($10 million) Series A funding round led by Tencent. Quell is backed by blue-chip investors including Y Combinator, Khosla Ventures, Tencent and Heartcore Capital.
HITAI converts real-time combat sports video into movement and performance data. Quell’s sensor-based motion models and gaming technology will enhance accuracy and speed in environments with challenging camera placement. This will help HITAI deliver engaging content for athletes, coaches and fans.
“A core part of Quell’s mission was redefining what was possible in sports motion recognition. Seeing this technology carried forward at scale by HITAI is an exceptional outcome, and we’re excited to be a part of their future,” said Cameron Brookhouse, CEO of Quell.

articles.title: Gemini Notebook agora pode puxar informações de livros que você comprou • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Gemini Notebook agora pode puxar informações de livros que você comprou
Antigo NotebookLM agora pode extrair trechos diretamente de obras compradas via Google Play Livros.
O Gemini Notebook, antigo NotebookLM, pode levantar dados diretamente dos livros disponíveis em sua biblioteca do Google Play Livros. A ferramenta, chamada Expert Intelligence, é compatível com mais de 100 mil livros oferecidos no app, e o usuário pode não só extrair trechos como também acessá-los por inteiro diretamente pela IA.
A inteligência artificial “acadêmica” do Google pode, então, realizar fichamentos, organizar gráficos e até gerar podcasts a partir de conteúdos originais, diminuindo os riscos de informações incorretas e alucinações. Isso não acaba com as chances de erro, mas é uma maneira bem interessante de evitá-los.
Segundo o The Verge, alguns usos foram demonstrados pelo diretor editorial Steve Johnson, do Google Labs. Entre os exemplos estão a criação de um livro de receitas e até sugestões de como ter uma conversa difícil com um funcionário a partir de um livro de gerenciamento de empresas.
Ao permitir a consulta diretamente via Google Play Livros, o Gemini Notebook facilita a vida do usuário, que não precisa inserir links e trechos completos na IA para receber uma resposta mais direcionada. Essa é uma das principais recomendações de especialistas para diminuir riscos de erros e alucinações, o que aumenta consideravelmente a confiança na inteligência artificial na hora de montar apresentações, planos de estudos, entre outros materiais.
O Google afirma ter trabalhado junto a autores para desenvolver controles específicos. Entre os exemplos dados, entretanto, a empresa citou apenas a limitação da consulta a livros adquiridos pelo próprio usuário, excluindo a possibilidade de acessar obras compartilhadas por algum amigo.
Recentemente, diversos vendedores de livros impressos alegaram um aumento nas compras em larga escala de títulos publicados antes de 2022 por desenvolvedoras de IA. O movimento aponta para uma confiabilidade maior em conteúdos escritos antes da presença massiva da inteligência artificial entre as produções, evitando o chamado AI Slop.
A novidade anunciada pelo Google reforça essa lógica, “limpando” a base de dados a ser analisada pela IA na hora de gerar uma resposta. Pensando no modelo voltado para usos acadêmicos, é essencial que o conteúdo gerado seja o mais assertivo possível. Mas, vale reforçar: isso não elimina totalmente a possibilidade erros e alucinações, sendo necessário sempre checar as informações e utilizar os materiais junto aos livros em questão.

articles.title: El color de los cables USB no es casualidad: esto es lo que significa que sea blanco, negro, azul, rojo o amarillo
articles.text: En esta fotografía ilustrativa, tomada en Bruselas, Bélgica, el 29 de diciembre de 2024, se aprecian cables Lightning y USB-C. Seguro que te ha ocurrido alguna vez: necesitas pasar unas fotos del móvil al ordenador, encuentras un cable USB-C por casa , lo conectas y no funciona. El teléfono carga, pero el ordenador no lo reconoce. La razón es que no todos los cables USB son iguales y, pese a su forma aparentemente idéntica, tienen funciones muy diferentes. El propio USB Implementers Forum (USB-IF) , organismo responsable del estándar, señala que no todos los cables tienen las mismas capacidades y que es responsabilidad del usuario elegir uno adecuado para el uso que necesita: carga rápida, copiar archivos… Y hay un detalle importante: conectar un dispositivo USB 3.0 a un puerto USB 2.0 no hará que funcione a su máxima velocidad. En una conexión intervienen tanto el dispositivo como el puerto y el cable. Si uno de ellos es más lento, esa limitación puede afectar al resultado final. ¿Cómo podemos identificar los puertos y cables? ¿Es posible saber qué hace un cable simplemente mirando su color? Seguir leyendo

articles.title: Man uses robot vacuum to covertly record his wife's affair, wins divorce settlement but gets sentenced to prison for making an illegal recording — Husband lands behind bars after counter-suit over privacy rights
articles.text:
Man uses robot vacuum to covertly record his wife's affair, wins divorce settlement but gets sentenced to prison for making an illegal recording — Husband lands behind bars after counter-suit over privacy rights
A net loss.
In a strange turn of events under Taiwanese law, both parties in a judicial contest lost against each other. A man sued his wife for having an extramarital affair and used footage from a robot vacuum to prove his case. He ultimately won the lawsuit and was awarded a healthy ~$19,000 USD in compensation for emotional distress, but since he secretly recorded his wife, she sued him back for invading her privacy. The courts ruled in her favor, forcing the man to pay a fine equal to 30% of what he'd just earned, along with a sentence of five months in prison.
The couple got married in 2021 and used to live with their parents, but they would occasionally spend time in their holiday home. During a vacation in 2023, the man discovered a used toothbrush in their bathroom, sparking suspicion that was confirmed by checking CCTV footage from a parking garage. In the footage, he saw another person who had driven his wife home before, hypothesizing him as his wife's partner in crime.
Three months later, he used a robot vacuum app to try to remotely contact his wife but, upon doing so, stumbled upon something shocking: The footage from the robot vacuum's camera showed his wife changing her clothes, getting in bed with the same person he had previously identified, and walking around the house naked while the other man comfortably sank into their sofa. He recorded the entire thing to use as evidence in a lawsuit that he brought shortly after.
Cheating is not a criminal offense under Taiwanese law, but infringing on someone's marital rights can still yield monetary compensation because it's a breach of contract. As such, the man sought a 2 million TWD (Taiwanese dollar), or roughly $63,000, reimbursement from his wife and her new lover. He used the footage from the robot vacuum's camera feed to prove that their relationship expanded far beyond casual friendship and the judges ruled in his favor. He won 500,000 TWD in compensation, which translates to $19,000. However, the fight was far from over.
Since recording someone without their consent is illegal across most parts of the world, including Taiwan, there were grounds for a counter-lawsuit for evidence collection. As such, the wife sued him for recording private, intimate footage of her and argued that the sensors and lights on the robot vacuum cleaner weren't enough to indicate she was being filmed. The man contended that the courts already admitted the footage as evidence, so it wasn't illegal material.
However, it was still obtained via illegal means, so the courts rejected his defense on the basis of invading the wife's privacy. In the hierarchy of constitution, individual rights outweigh marital duties. He was fined 150,000 TWD ($4,700) and sentenced to prison for five months. It won't be unreasonable to say that prison time is a much worse outcome than any amount of compensation paid by the other party. Not to mention having a criminal record on your name can tarnish your civil reputation.
Without the smoking gun that was the robot vacuum footage, the marriage lawsuit could've dragged on for much longer, draining the man of his time, energy, and money in place of a swift verdict. Still, the fact that the husband has to go to jail and pay the equivalent of 30% of his payout back to the state as a fine basically negates the financial gain from the marriage lawsuit. This was a net loss, especially when you consider he already only received a fraction of the 2 million TWD compensation initially sought.

articles.title: Filtración de última hora en Apple: así van a ser los Apple Watch Series 12 y Ultra 4
articles.text:
Hace unos días te contamos que Apple tiene todo listo para presentar nuevos productos el día 9 de septiembre. ¿Cuáles? Es bien sabido que habrá nuevos iPhone (incluido el plegable), auriculares y también relojes. Hoy nos centramos en estos últimos, los Apple Watch Series 12 y Watch Ultra 4. Ha sido Mark Gurman el encargado de recopilar varios datos sobre estos dispositivos y ponerlos encima de la mesa pocos días antes de que sean oficiales.
Y, aunque todavía hay muchos detalles guardados en secreto, gracias a las palabras del filtrador es posible hacerse una idea de lo que está por venir, si merece la pena renovar tu viejo reloj por un nuevo Apple Watch Series 12 o conocer qué modelos van a presentarse la semana que viene.
De hecho, una de las cosas que Gurman ha afirmado con rotundidad es que este año no habrá Apple Watch SE de 4ª generación. Hasta el momento, todo apunta a que se presentarán los Apple Watch Series 12 y también un nuevo modelo para la versión Ultra. Por lo tanto, si estabas esperando para renovar tu reloj con la opción más barata de la serie, tendrás que echarle un vistazo al SE del año pasado o esperar.
¿Cómo serán los Apple Watch Series 12 y Watch Ultra 4?
Lo que ha publicado Gurman es un recopilatorio de detalles que, o bien se intuían, o se habían filtrado anteriormente. En su artículo para Bloomberg lo deja claro y afirma que los relojes de este año no tendrán una renovación de diseño radical. De hecho, deberían ser bastante similares a los de generaciones pasadas.
Por lo tanto, se descartan detalles como un nuevo método para anclar las correas o la llegada del Touch ID para desbloquearlo con la huella. Tanto el Apple Watch Series 12 como el Ultra 4 podrían contar con ligeros cambios en peso y dimensiones, pero su estética general debería mantenerse sin demasiados cambios.
No en todas las versiones, eso sí: Gurman sigue apostando por un modelo con cuerpo de cerámica en color blanco o gris oscuro, un detalle que podría darle un soplo de aire fresco a la generación, aunque solo para quienes tengan un gran bolsillo (las anteriores opciones cerámicas fueron las más caras de la serie).
¿Dónde estarán las novedades? Según Gurman, en el rendimiento. Él comenta que los Apple Watch Series 12 y el Ultra 4 tendrán un nuevo procesador más eficiente y potente. No es algo que se deba pasar por alto, pues la anterior generación de relojes no renovó este componente: utilizó el mismo chip que los Series 10 de hace dos años.
Si esto es cierto, los nuevos relojes de Apple contarán con un rendimiento mayor y una eficiencia más notable, lo que podría traducirse en una mejor autonomía sin necesidad de aumentar la batería y con ella el peso y el tamaño.
¿Y ya? No, aunque las siguientes novedades no están directamente relacionadas con una mejora en los Apple Watch, sino en las apps que lo gestionan. Se espera que Apple renueve las aplicaciones de gestión y la de salud para tener nuevas métricas, un diseño diferente y más opciones.
Es más, Gurman afirma que Apple está trabajando en una función que le permitiría a sus relojes recopilar información del sensor de frecuencia cardiaca de forma continua durante las 24 horas del día. La opción está en fase de pruebas y, por ahora, no sabemos si estaría en todos los relojes o solo en los Apple Watch Series 12 y Ultra 4.
No se ha mencionado nada sobre la posible pulsera con sensores integrados, por lo que no parece que esa filtración esté apoyada por los que más información tienen sobre el reloj.

articles.title: Tim Cook's parting message: Apple is in the hands of a product builder | TechCrunch
articles.text:
On his last day as Apple CEO, Tim Cook offered a rousing endorsement of his successor: John Ternus, the company’s senior vice president of hardware engineering. In a memo to employees, Cook reminded staff that he’s “not leaving Apple,” just stepping away from the role of CEO, while declaring that “few people understand what it takes to build products that change the world the way John does.”
Ternus’ elevation to the top job suggests that Apple’s next era will see a renewed focus on hardware and product execution. Under Ternus, Apple shipped a number of notable products, most recently, the new ultra-thin iPhone Air, the lower-cost MacBook Neo, and AirPods with hearing health features. He also led the hardware engineering team across Apple’s full device lineup.
Hardware will play an important role in the AI era, not only in terms of chips, but also the devices people use to run enterprise AI. Apple this year, for instance, offered earlier releases of its new Mac models, the Mac mini and Mac Studio, compared with years past, driven by AI demand.
Cook’s memo, reported by Bloomberg and others, naturally says little about Apple’s future when it comes to AI, services, regulation, China, or the other challenges that lie ahead. Instead, Cook focuses on his gratitude for the opportunity to lead Apple and exalts the company’s culture as ultimately what matters most.
“We share a belief that what we build matters and that we have both the opportunity and the responsibility to leave the world better than we found it,” Cook wrote. He also referenced the famous Steve Jobs quote about leaving a “dent in the universe,” saying that Apple makes that possible because of “who we are and what we believe,” as well as “what we value and how we see the world.”
Cook will remain at Apple as executive chairman and will continue to manage political relationships, including those with President Trump and the Chinese government.
On X, Cook also wrote: “Sending lots of love to the Apple community on my last day as CEO. My title changes tomorrow, but the love I have for the Apple community never will. Thank you for being a constant source of inspiration. My gratitude is endless, and I’m excited for the next chapter!”
The full memo is below (via Bloomberg):
Team,
Today is my last day as CEO of Apple. This is a moment I always knew would come one day, and yet it is still hard to believe it has arrived and I am writing these words. I love this company and the team behind it, and I couldn’t let this day pass without sending a note to you to tell you how grateful I am for the outpouring of affection you’ve sent my way, for the way you’ve shown up each and every day, and most of all, for the privilege of a lifetime serving as your leader.
The truth is, whatever there is to say about my success, I know it is all because of you. You have brought out the best in me. In all my life, I have never seen or been with such an extraordinary team of people before, and every day I get to see more examples of that.
There is something truly special about Apple. I am most proud of what an annual report could never capture. This place is proof that culture triumphs over everything. We share a belief that what we build matters and that we have both the opportunity and the responsibility to leave the world better than we found it. That purpose is part of what makes this place extraordinary. Apple helps nurture it, but I believe it lived within each of you long before you arrived here. It is what brought you to this company and what continues to drive the work you do every day.
Together, we have created something far greater than any one of us could have imagined or accomplished alone. And that’s the secret to our success. We bring out the best in each other. We lift each other up. We have made it possible to leave our “dent in the universe,” as Steve once described it, because of who we are and what we believe, because of what we value and how we see the world. How fortunate we are. How fortunate I am.
As you know, I am not leaving Apple. But I am stepping away from a role that I have loved deeply. I will miss this work in ways I can only begin to imagine, even as I remain completely at peace with my decision. I will miss leading you and being with you for every step, even as I take enormous comfort in handing the helm to someone as brilliant and wonderful and capable as John. Few people understand what it takes to build products that change the world the way John does and I could not be more excited for his leadership.
I hope you know how much I appreciate you and what an honor it has been to be your CEO. Most of all, I hope you will continue to be proud to be part of this remarkable place we call Apple and always give it your very best. When we bring our whole selves to this work, with care for one another and for the people we serve, there is no limit to the profound difference we can make.
I look forward to seeing you in my new role at Apple Park and around the world.
With all I have and all I am, I am always.
Yours,
Tim

articles.title: Viraler Trick von Tiktok: Kann Alufolie deinen WLAN-Empfang verbessern?
articles.text:
Tiktok-Trick: Kann Alufolie deinen WLAN-Empfang verbessern?
Einige von euch dürften das Problem kennen: In vielen Wohnungen lässt der WLAN-Empfang in bestimmten Ecken und Winkeln zu wünschen übrig. Die richtige Positionierung des Routers, ein neueres Router-Modell oder ein Repeater können helfen, den Empfang zu verbessern.
Schuhkarton mit Alufolie auskleiden
Geht es nach Nutzer:innen in sozialen Medien wie Tiktok, genügen aber schon ein paar wenige Utensilien, die die meisten zu Hause haben dürften. Darunter: Alufolie. Wie das gehen soll? Ihr kleidet einen Schuhkarton mit Alufolie aus und macht den Karton dadurch zu einer Reflektorfläche. Dank der Alufolie wird nämlich ein Teil der Funkwellen reflektiert – und so kann das WLAN durch eine geschickte Positionierung auch in den hinteren Winkeln eurer Wohnung verbessert werden.
Wichtig ist allerdings zu wissen, und darauf verweist auch Chip, die den Test gemacht haben: Durch die Alufolie wird keine zusätzliche Sendeleistung erzeugt. Im Idealfall wird die vorhandene einfach besser verteilt.
Die Reflektorfläche muss gebogen sein
Und so bastelt ihr den Alufolien-Reflektor: Biegt die zwei kurzen Seitenflächen des Schuhkartons auf, sodass eine gebogene Reflektorfläche entsteht. Die Alufolie befestigt ihr dann mit Tesafilm oder Klebeband. Im Selbstversuch von Chip wurde mit diesem Reflektor der Marke Eigenbau die WLAN-Signalstärke im Garten von 16 Prozent auf 22 Prozent angehoben. Die einfach herzustellende und preiswerte Variante hat in diesem Fall also zu einer Verbesserung geführt.
Das bedeutet allerdings nicht, dass es auch in anderen Fällen funktioniert – jede Wohnung ist anders. Auch technisch gibt es potentielle Haken: Komplexe Techniken ermöglichen es WLAN-Systemen, die Funkübertragung an die jeweiligen Bedingungen vor Ort dynamisch anzupassen. Reflexionen an Möbeln oder Wänden haben auch Einfluss auf die WLAN-Verbindung.
Repeater oder ein Mesh-System bringen mehr
All diese Faktoren lassen sich mit dem Alufolien-Schuhkarton nicht kontrollieren. Zudem kommt, dass die Ergebnisse beim Selbstversuch trotz des selbst hergestellten Reflektors schwankend blieben und nicht für einen stabil besseren Empfang sorgten.
Einen Versuch ist der Alufolien-Schuhkarton aber durchaus wert, da er schnell gebastelt ist und wenig kostet. Ein Repeater oder ein Mesh-System dürften dagegen mehr bringen, beide Varianten kosten allerdings auch einiges.

articles.title: Phil Schiller is leaving his biggest jobs at Apple
articles.text:
Longtime Apple executive Phil Schiller is stepping down from his role as the head of the App Store and Apple events, according to a report from Bloomberg. Following the change, Schiller will keep his Apple Fellow title and continue “working on unspecified initiatives,” Bloomberg reports.
Phil Schiller is leaving his biggest jobs at Apple
The executive will remain an Apple Fellow, but it’s unclear what he’ll work on after handing off the App Store and events.
Schiller initially joined Apple in 1987 and became the company’s head of marketing in 1997. He helped launch the App Store alongside Steve Jobs in 2008, but only started heading up the store in 2015. Over the years, Schiller has played a role in the development of many of Apple’s products, including the iPhone, iPad, iPod, and Macs, and has presented several of them at the company’s launch events. In recent years, Schiller has started stepping away from some of these responsibilities, as he relinquished his role as senior vice president of marketing to Greg Joswiak in 2020.
The news comes just one day before hardware leader John Ternus is set to take over for Apple CEO Tim Cook, who is stepping down on September 1st. As reported by Bloomberg, Apple is moving the App Store division under services head Eddy Cue, while Carson Oliver will continue to lead the store with the help of Ann Thai, who is in charge of app distribution tools and third-party marketplaces.
Apple didn’t immediately respond to The Verge’s request for comment.
Along with heading up the App Store, which facilitated more than $1.4 trillion in transactions last year, Schiller has had to contend with legal battles and government regulations that have forced Apple to change its stringent policies surrounding app distribution and payments.
Schiller’s departure is part of a broader executive exodus at Apple, which could prove to be one of Ternus’ biggest hurdles as he takes over as CEO. Former chief financial officer Luca Maestri stepped down from his role in January 2025, followed by the departure of Apple COO Jeff Williams, design chief Alan Dye, and AI head John Giannandrea. Lisa Jackson, Apple’s environmental and policy lead, also retired last year, while Apple will replace general counsel Kate Adams with former Meta chief legal officer Jennifer Newstead.

articles.title: Advanced Cooling Technologies Tackle Automotive Heat - EE Times
articles.text:
Historically, vehicle cooling architectures were engineered almost exclusively around internal combustion engines (ICE), cabin climate controls, and basic electrical systems. This traditional paradigm is evolving rapidly as modern vehicle architectures become increasingly electrified and software-defined. The simultaneous rise of electric drivetrains, advanced driver-assistance features (ADAS), self-driving platforms, and high-performance central processing units has increased thermal demands throughout modern vehicles beyond what many legacy cooling architectures were designed to accommodate.
Batteries, traction inverters, charging systems, LiDAR sensors, cameras, and AI processors all generate heat that must be managed within increasingly compact spaces. These additions are creating heat fluxes that are beginning to challenge traditional cooling approaches (Figure 1). The industry requires innovative new cooling technologies to overcome high heat fluxes.
Automotive electronics
The amount of electronics in internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles has grown steadily for decades, with the addition of power brakes, power steering, and proximity sensors. Automakers have since added heat sensors, flow monitors, and positional sensors to monitor internal systems, along with cameras, LiDARs, and radars to support safety features such as ADAS and to enable semi-autonomous and autonomous driving. Increasingly powerful processors are necessary to orchestrate all of this, but they also generate more heat.
Hybrids and electric vehicles naturally expanded the complement of electronics, with electric motors, powertrains, and batteries, along with electronic power control units that must manage powertrain traction inverters, growing complements of sensors, and charging infrastructure.
The gradual transition from 400V architectures to 800V architectures necessitates the adoption of components and power ICs based on wide-bandgap materials (WBG) such as gallium nitride and silicon carbide, both of which will switch faster, operate efficiently at higher voltages, and reduce electrical losses. However, the remaining heat must still be managed within increasingly compact packages.
All of these components are being built into tighter spaces and are often placed next to other heat-generating systems (e.g., traction inverters, batteries), compounding the problem.
Hybrid bonding and vapor chambers
Several chip- and module-level technologies can help improve thermal management. One is to continue to improve the interconnect in multichip configurations through techniques such as hybrid bonding, which reduces thermal interface resistance and enables dense chip integration. Hybrid bonding is already being adopted in the manufacture of some advanced processor modules and some of the more complex multilayer memory ICs.
Another solution is the adoption of direct liquid-to-chip cooling, which brings liquid cooling closer to the primary heat source by reducing the number of thermal resistance layers between the device and the coolant.
Vapor chambers, already in use in some of the most advanced smartphones, can be modified to handle the significantly higher heat fluxes found in motor vehicles. Although a vapor chamber occupies a relatively small footprint, it spreads heat well beyond the dimensions of the heat source. Inside the sealed chamber, heat vaporizes the working fluid, allowing thermal energy to spread rapidly through the vapor before the fluid condenses and returns to the heat source via a capillary wick.
The goal is to improve the performance of vapor chambers for the levels of heat flux encountered in automotive electronics. One approach is to expand the effective heat-transfer surface area by constructing small, uniform, and triply periodic minimal surface (TPMS) structures. TPMS structures increase the effective heat transfer surface when compared to planar cooling solutions such as channels. Historically, TPMS structures have been difficult to manufacture at the microscale, but that challenge is beginning to be addressed (Figure 2).
Cascaded vapor chambers with TPMS interface geometries promise to distribute loads approaching 1,000 W/cm2, a level of heat flux actively explored in research settings for WBG traction inverter devices, for example. Without advanced heat spreaders such as vapor chambers, conventional air cooling is generally limited to heat fluxes below a hundred watts per square centimeter.
A solution for axial flux motors
While many cooling innovations focus on semiconductor packages, similar principles can also be applied at the system level. One example is the cooling of next-generation axial flux motors. A new class of axial flux motors has recently been introduced that is significantly smaller and more power-dense than existing electric motors. Depending on the application, they may incorporate multiple rotors surrounding a common stator to increase torque output. Their compact design makes conventional cooling approaches more difficult to implement.
A novel proposal combines pumped and wick flows to uniformly distribute coolant from an outer cooling ring, through the gaps between the coils, and into an inner cooling ring of the motor. Compared with conventional pumped-coolant approaches, this concept offers a simpler and potentially more effective method of distributing coolant.
Looking further ahead, researchers are also exploring adaptive cooling technologies. One speculative concept stems from the recent observation that certain polymers exhibit a mechanical response to light. The idea is to build micro-orifices into coolers for logic chips (CPUs, GPUs, etc.) and cover them with light-responsive polymer layers approximately 10- to 100 microns thick. LEDs or some other light sources could selectively illuminate the polymer, causing it to either expand to allow more coolant through or contract to restrict the flow of coolant. In this manner, the polymer can be optically manipulated to direct the flow of coolant to hot spots on processors without requiring electrically actuated valves or control circuitry near the coolant.
As automotive electronics continue to increase in power density, emerging cooling technologies offer new opportunities to improve heat transfer, coolant distribution, and thermal control across a broad range of vehicle applications. Together, these advances will play an important role in enabling the next generation of electrified, software-defined, and autonomous vehicles.
